We had dinner at Manhatta, located on the 60th floor of a skyscraper in the Wall Street district, and the experience was impressive overall.

From the moment you arrive, the welcome is highly professional. The hostess team, maître d’, and sommelier all contribute to a very polished and well-organized atmosphere. The service is attentive, refined, and genuinely professional throughout the evening.

The view is truly spectacular. One side overlooks the Brooklyn Bridge and Brooklyn, while the main façade faces Uptown Manhattan, showcasing the iconic, glittering skyline in all its glory. At the entrance, there is a stylish and functional bar area with a stunning backdrop view. Walking to the right, the restaurant opens into an L-shaped dining room with approximately 30 tables. The staff-to-guest ratio is excellent, and service flows smoothly.

They offer a 3- or 4-course prix fixe menu. Each course (starter, main, dessert) includes about five options, which keeps the selection focused and prevents the menu from feeling overwhelming. The concept feels standardized, elegant, and based on quality ingredients rather than excessive variety.

My wife and I both chose the four-course menu.

I started with the raw shrimp, which was excellent — easily the highlight of my meal. I then had scallops, followed by a vegan main course that, unfortunately, felt underdeveloped and barely cooked — surprisingly so, to the point that it felt almost unfinished. I ended with a chocolate mousse. I paired my meal with a mezcal-based spicy cocktail, which was well balanced and enjoyable.

My wife chose burrata as a starter, a lentil-based dish, tagliatelle, sea bass as her main course, and sorbet for dessert. She paired her meal with a Blanc de Blancs champagne, which complemented her dishes beautifully.

Overall, the food was good but somewhat mediocre in execution, with a few highlights (especially the raw shrimp). I would rate the food 4 out of 5. However, the atmosphere, views, and the professionalism and friendliness of the staff easily deserve 5 out of 5.

A unique and charming touch: the restaurant provides binoculars placed around the space for guests to enjoy the skyline up close — a thoughtful and memorable detail. Additionally, the small “bites” served between courses were delightful and well executed.

In summary: go for the view, the ambiance, and the impeccable service. The food is good, but the overall experience is what truly stands out.

The view is so awesome! The sun comes out after we sitting at the table! Services is so warm. The food is so so delicious! My very first time beef burger, great taste!

It is couple special occasions we celebrate today, best decisions made to come here. Cheers!

Visiting Little Italy in New York City with my family was like stepping into a small slice of Europe right in the heart of Manhattan. The moment we walked down Mulberry Street, the atmosphere felt lively, colorful, and full of character. Italian flags hanging across the street, outdoor seating areas, and the aroma of garlic and fresh tomato sauce instantly made us hungry.

What I loved most was simply strolling together and exploring the many snack outlets and restaurants lined up one after another. Small bakeries displayed cannoli, biscotti, and pastries that looked too good to resist. We stopped to try fresh cannoli filled on the spot — crispy shells with sweet, creamy ricotta inside. It was absolutely delicious.

The restaurants offered everything from classic pasta dishes and wood-fired pizzas to seafood and rich lasagna. Many places had outdoor seating, which made the experience even more enjoyable. Sitting there with my family, enjoying authentic Italian food while watching the crowd pass by, felt special and relaxed. The drinks were just as enjoyable — refreshing mocktails, Italian sodas, espresso, and cappuccino that completed the meal perfectly.

There were also small souvenir shops and specialty stores selling Italian sauces, olive oils, and sweets, adding to the cultural charm of the neighborhood. The entire area had a warm, welcoming vibe that made us slow down and truly enjoy the moment.

Little Italy is not just about food — it’s about culture, tradition, and togetherness. Visiting with my family made it even more memorable.

Great ambiance, would be a cute date spot with the nice views!

My friend and I did the the 4 course meal. I ordered the burrata, octopus, duck, and the an Asian toast dessert. Everything tasted great overall, but wasn't a huge fan of the thick breading on the octopus. Dinner took almost 3 hours, which felt a bit long, but service was attentive the whole time.

Tsukimi is one of the most memorable dining experiences in NYC. The atmosphere is intimate and elegant, and every course is beautifully presented and thoughtfully paced. The seasonal ingredients truly shine, especially the pristine sashimi and refined warm dishes.

Exceptional food, warm hospitality, and flawless execution. Absolutely worth it.

A top notch kaiseki in NYC. Every detail here is perfection. The chef showcases extraordinary technique and artistry, curating seasonal courses that feel both authentic and inventive. Service is impeccable—professional yet genuinely welcoming—and the extensive sake menu elevates the experience even further.

I look forward to returning each season to savor the evolving menu.

Lovely kaiseki spot with a good range of high quality dishes. Service is attentive and intimate, while the space feels like you’re walking into someone’s very nice home. Loved all the dishes especially the truffle rice and Wagyu rolls. Well paced as well.

Fourth or fifth time here. My favorite dish and the highlight tonight was the persimmon soufflé with cashew ice cream. In the past I’ve had banana soufflé which was also out of this world. My first time here I had the dry-aged slow-cooked low-charcoal-fired duck. Tonight they had the same, but it was not dry-aged long enough, and not slow-cooked long enough over the charcoal fire. The meat was a bit wet and did not have a “snap” to it as the first time, nor was the skin crispy enough like the first time. Also, another slight mishap tonight was a bone in one of my fish dish. Not a big deal to me, but to others it may be. I wish them good luck and hope they will earn an additional Michelin Star next year.

Tsukimi was great. The service was impeccable and the food was delicious. We had the summer menu and you could really taste that the ingredients represented the season. A lot of places say they picked the ingredients based off the season, but its usually simply the ingredients were in season. Tsukimi’s selection actually tasted like summer.

Had a wonderful dining experience here! The food was absolutely delicious, and you can really tell the quality from the first bite especially the meats, which were perfectly cooked, tender, and full of flavor without being over or underdone. We ordered the Achari Murgh Kebab, Royyala Veppudu, Tandoori Murgh, Mughlai Chicken Biryani, Malabar Parota, purani Delli Ki Papri Chaat, and Lamb Madras, and every single dish was outstanding. The kebabs were juicy, the seafood was flavorful, the biryani was rich and aromatic, and the lamb madras was cooked to perfection with deep, balanced spices. Each dish was oozing with freshness and taste. The staff were also very down-to-earth, welcoming, and attentive, which made the experience even better. This place is a must-try, and I highly recommend these dishes if you visit definitely coming back again!

Food:
Went with my girlfriend, it’s my favorite cuisine, it was delicious. Cashew curry is an old favorite, and tikka masala is classic so we tried and loved both. Not spicy at all if you prefer the mild side you’d enjoy the options here. And there were spicy options that I will be trying next time.

Service:
There were strands in our food that I was worried were something like plastic but it was just ginger and the manager and server were very attentive to the request to check. Also we did have a reservation that we were on time for but had a 5+ minute wait. Not a huge issue for me but it should be mentioned.

Atmosphere:
We dined around 7:30pm, it was quite busy, all tables taken and a few groups waiting outside from time to time.

Also I eat a toooooon but the food was quite filling. I left feeling satiated and honestly looking forward to my next dinner here

We came here for dinner and the food did not disappoint, every meal item we ordered was cooked to perfection. We had the lamb chops one of the best lamb chops I have ever eaten, the lamb biriyani fell right off of the bone.

Chola Coastal Indian Cuisine - Where every bite tells a story and every corner whispers elegance,where every dish is a work of art, and every moment is unforgettable.🫰🏻Everything from the grill to the plate smells and tastes delicious.
We tried the Dak Bungalow Murgh Curry,
Paneer Khurchan,
Paneer Malai Tikka,
Martha Stewart’s Favorite Murgh Malai,
Chicken Biryani, and
Martha Stewart’s Favorite Onion Naan.
For dessert, we had the Kolkata Tomato Chutney—a refreshing sweet chutney with Panch Phoron and gulab jamun with rasmalai twist, beautifully decorated with chocolate sauce. The Murgh Malai was incredibly tender—definitely a must-try dish! The food was full of flavor and beautifully prepared. More than a meal, it's an experience.😌
The cozy ambiance and friendly staff made it a memorable dining experience. Highly recommend for anyone looking to enjoy flavorful Indian cuisine in a welcoming setting.😋 This is a restaurant where people from all backgrounds—not just Indians—can enjoy the food.
Thank you for the amazing service and for making our dining experience truly wonderful. Everything—from the food to the attention we received—was perfect. We felt genuinely cared for and will definitely be coming back! ❤️

Absolutely loved our meal at Chola! We had the chili shrimp, Mangalore fish fry, and the coastal chicken gassi — every dish was bursting with flavor and hit the perfect spice level. Bold, authentic coastal Indian cuisine done right. Highly recommend!

I am such a huge fan of this place! My boyfriend found this restaurant online, and once we saw that most of the menu was gluten free and dairy free, I got so excited! I was even more excited that the head chef and creator was Black. We made a reservation for the same night. We really enjoyed our meal. Walking in, the restaurant was elegant, and I loved the open kitchen. The 2 seater tables were a bit tight, similar to most restaurants, but the seats were comfortable. Our server was nice and the other staff were great. It was also great to see so many Black chefs, and I loved the RnB and soul music. We ordered off the restaurant week menu as well as the regular menu. Looking at the both menus, it’s evident that a talented chef created these dishes. My boyfriend is Haitian, so we appreciated seeing some Haitian staples being converted to fine dining. Our favorites were the lobster pasta, which had plenty of lobster, but we wanted more noodles and more of the entire dish. The gumbo was interesting, but really good. The Sòs Pwa Nwa with the
Pickled red onions was next level. The light coconut cake with the sorbet was fantastic. The only disappointment was the cornbread. I was so excited to try to gluten-free bread. It seems like some nights they have mini muffins and some nights they have the bigger loaf. We were only given 1 mini muffin for two people, so I asked for more and was charged $12. I was annoyed since the mini loaf is clearly much bigger than the mini muffin. Even if it was only 1 mini muffin per person who ordered off the regular menu, we spent so much money, it feels like it’s ridiculous to charge for an extra mini muffin on a $350 bill. That made me a bit upset. Otherwise, I’m a huge fan and highly recommend. Thank you for offering delicious Haitian food that’s gf/df. We will be back.

Ate here for a birthday lunch.
I was not disappointed.  I loved the hand cut tile mosaic floor and the open kitchen.  The staff were attentive and  enthusiastic.  Excellent cocktails. Every dish was a wonderful melange of flavor combining French,  Asian and African influences.  Even the French fries were notable. .My wife described them as like a good baguette...crusty on the outside and fluffy on the inside.  My favorite was the the Duck Confit Curry.

The most marvelous dining experience in Manhattan—I find myself returning over and over again. Every dish showcases a blend of exciting flavors, drawing from Caribbean and southeast Asian cuisine. The food is as visually stunning and luxurious as the beautifully designed interior. The prix fixe format may seem pricey initially—but is very reasonable when considering the portions are more substantial and the cooking technique more refined than many modern restaurants that have opened in the last years.

This is the cool new restaurant inside the beautiful Printemps building downtown. The restaurant is eclectic with bright colored tiles and stand out chandeliers, a great spot for striking conversations over a small dinner.
We visited for restaurant week - and apparently got some new testers on the menu. Food is inspired by French colonial cuisines - lots of Thai, south east asian, New Orleans, etc.
The dishes were tasty. Some flavours were a bit boring compared to other places in NY but overall pretty good.
Service still working out some kinks.

An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. This  restaurant offers a thoughtfully crafted prix fixe menu that showcases both creativity and precision. The duck was outstanding—perfectly cooked, rich, and deeply flavorful, with a balance that felt refined rather than heavy. The cod was equally impressive: delicate, fresh, and expertly prepared, allowing the quality of the fish to truly shine. Each course was beautifully presented and timed perfectly, and the overall menu felt cohesive and intentional. Attentive service and an elegant atmosphere elevated the evening, making it ideal for a special occasion or a memorable night out. Highly recommended for those who appreciate fine dining done right.

Every time I have the pleasure of dining at Santi I leave full and beyond satisfied. The front of house staff is always friendly and welcoming. On top of Chef Michael White and the kitchen staff being so talented they are the kindest individuals.

I've gotten to enjoy Santi's lunch menu and dinner menu. I've also experienced service from the dining room and bar. No matter where I am sat or the time of day I always have a fabulous experience.

Aside from the restaurant's wonderful atmosphere the food is truly out of this world good. I am always pleasantly surprised with every dish. Their dishes have opened my eyes to foods I would never usually try or order and I always end up LOVING them! Some of my favorite dishes I've had from past visits have been the Faraona, Garganelli, Mare, Insalata, and the Gamberi Rossi. You must have dessert at Santi too. The Sole e Luna I had at my most recent visit was life changing to say the least. I dream of that dessert daily!

Santi is a must try if you are looking for a new spot to dine at in the city!

Everything about this restaurant was absolutely wonderful — the food was incredible, and the service from the staff was truly top-tier. Every dish was beautifully presented and unbelievably delicious. It really felt like a high-end dining experience in every sense.

Unfortunately, the only thing that significantly impacted my overall impression was the experience with the hostess. I arrived earlier than my friend and checked in my coat. I was told to wait for my friend before they could check for a table, which I understood. However, I was not offered a seat at the bar, even though there were many empty bar stools available. Instead, I was asked to wait in a corner, which felt very uncomfortable and unwelcoming.

When my friend arrived, I was then immediately told that I could sit at the bar and wait for our table. This left me genuinely confused as to why I wasn’t allowed to sit there earlier and feel comfortable while waiting.

In addition, the hostess’s overall attitude felt quite unfriendly. For a restaurant of this level, I believe the front-of-house experience should match the excellence of the food and service. A more professional and welcoming approach would truly elevate the entire experience.

Advanced cuisine in an incredibly chic setting in midtown east. Stunning raw appetizers and great pastas, we also enjoyed the steak which was cooked perfectly. Cocktails are expensive but very very good. Great vibes for an intimate group dinner. Gorgeous bar! Staff was so welcoming and helpful in keeping our dinner on pace before the show we were seeing. Very thoughtful all around!

An exceptional dining experience in the heart of Midtown East. The cuisine is refined and beautifully executed — the raw appetizers were stunning and both the fish and crab cakes were cooked to perfection. Definitely on the pricier side, but worth it.

The atmosphere is incredibly chic with a gorgeous bar and perfect ambiance for an intimate group dinner. The staff warm and attentive. A seamless, sophisticated experience all around.

Unforgettable! My experience at SANTI was absolutely magical. From the moment I walked through the door, I knew I was in a special place. The kitchen team excelled with every dish, each bite was an explosion of flavors and textures that left me breathless. But what really made my experience unique was the service. The waiters were attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable about the menu, which allowed me to enjoy each dish without worries. The managers were always ensuring that everything was perfect, and their passion for what they do shows in every detail.

the desserts... they're a masterpiece! Each one is a creation worthy of an artist, both in presentation and taste.

I want to especially thank the kitchen team for their hard work and dedication. To the managers, thank you for your hospitality. And to the waiters, thank you for your impeccable service and constant smile. This experience was truly unforgettable, and I can't wait to come back.

I dined at Cafe Commerce on Valentine’s Day for the prix-fixe menu and had such a wonderful experience. The food was truly excellent — the sweet potato tortellini was rich and perfectly balanced, and the short rib was incredibly tender; the perfect comfort meal.
What really made the evening special, though, was the service — especially Raymond. He was an absolute pleasure to chat with, explained the menu in detail, answered all of our questions with care, and gave top-tier recommendations. His warmth and professionalism elevated the entire night.
I’ll definitely be back and strongly recommend!

Food was very good. Scallops, burger and Branzino were highlights. Birthday cake was nostalgically good. Prices were high, especially for alcohol (friend had an $18 mocktail - there's no alcohol!! How are we paying $18 for juice and carbonated water?!? Even the birthday cake, which is just yellow cake with chocolate icing was $24!). If prices were more reasonable I'd say 5 stars, but factoring in value, 4 stars.

I recently dined at Cafe Commerce and had an exceptional experience that I just had to share! We started our meal with the Hamachi, which was nothing short of excellent—perfectly fresh and beautifully presented.

For the main course, we indulged in the Rigatoni Carbonara and the Chicken Schnitzel. The carbonara was creamy and rich, with just the right amount of seasoning, while the schnitzel was crispy on the outside and tender inside, making it a delightful comfort food choice.

To top off our meal, we ordered the birthday cake for dessert. It was a sweet celebration that was simply delicious—moist, flavorful, and the perfect ending to our dining experience.

What truly stood out was the staff; they were beyond nice, attentive, and made us feel welcome throughout our visit. Everything about Cafe Commerce was over the top in the best way possible.

This spot has quickly become one of my new favorite restaurants in New York City, and I can't wait to return! Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a fantastic dining experience!

Stopped by yesterday for lunch before a visit to the new Frick and felt like a local and a regular right away.

The place was filled with people who seemed like they’ve been coming for years. Each person more interesting than the last. We sat next to an a friendly couple who lived in the neighborhood and struck up a conversation.

The service was superb and the team made sure our water glasses were never empty and we were sat right away and offered all the seasonal specials including the mulled wine, Gruyère grilled cheese with tomato soup and chicken salad. Started with the deviled eggs and table bread and butter. All were delicious.

Will definitely stop back by when in the area again. Thanks team!

We just had Thanksgiving dinner at this restaurant — and it was phenomenal. From the moment we walked in, it felt like sitting down to a family feast, surrounded by warmth and kindness. The meal itself was unbelievably good — rich, comforting dishes that felt like home. The highlight though? The dessert and the mulled wine — they absolutely stole the show.

Our waiter (Raymond) made the night extra special. He was attentive, friendly, and genuine — we felt so seen and cared for, like we were dining with family. It’s rare to find a family-style spot in the city that gives you that homey feeling, and we couldn’t believe we stumbled on this one.

Honestly — a full 10/10. We can’t wait to go back. We’ll definitely be regulars.

I found Crevette when looking up new lunch spots near SoHo and I am very glad that I stumbled upon this place. They serve upscale French cuisine but the space did not feel overly formal during the day. I can see how it might be more upscale at night though.

We started with a Merguez & Morcilla Skewer and two pieces of Bluefin Tuna. Both were delicious (perhaps the best part of the meal). The Morcilla was so good that we ended up getting a second one.

Next, we split the Grilled Cabbage, Chickpea, and Jamón Ibérico salad and the Grilled Chicken w Fries. Both were really good. It was nothing too inventive but both dishes were done really really well! The fries were cooked perfectly and the chicken was delicious.

We left feeling full, but not too full. Honestly, I hope to go back. There were so many things on the menu that looked good. Definitely try this place. Either for date night or a weekend lunch with friends!

We stopped by Crevette in the West Village to see if we could move our reservation, and the staff was so accommodating—they were able to switch us to an earlier time right away. We were seated in a cozy corner booth, which ended up being the perfect spot for a relaxed dinner.

Service throughout the night was excellent. Our server was attentive, warm, and always on top of things without feeling intrusive.

The food overall was good. The Little Gem Salad was fresh and flavorful—simple but really well done. The Lobster Tagliatelle was rich and tasty, with great texture on the pasta. The Dover Sole had nice flavor, but it was a bit too buttery for us; it would’ve been much better with a lighter hand on the sauce.

We ended with dessert, and both treats were enjoyable—the soft serve sundae was fun and nostalgic, while the chocolate tart was rich and deep in flavor.

Crevette sits right in a great spot in the West Village, making it an easy and charming place for dinner. Service is truly the highlight, and the food has some solid hits, especially if you enjoy richer dishes. Overall, a pleasant neighborhood dining experience.

Truly incredible dining experience! Absolutely gorgeous and inviting interior. Our server was super knowledgeable and recommended incredible dishes and wine. The poached cod was the star of dinner but the dessert rum cake was close your eyes and say thank you good. This is what going out to dinner should feel like!

Very comfortable restaurant with great food.  The red shrimp carpaccio and grill cabbage is the best of all.  The scallops is nicely done but I like white sauce more than red one.   Dover sole can be better if we can cook it less for one to two minutes.

The food is really really good, main reason of why we came here. We sat on the patio in the sun (only available table at that time), and as soon as other table in the shade got available our server kindly allowed us (and helped us) to move. After that, the service was a bit slow, but the overall experience was great. We will come back again for sure!

My husband and I had an amazing experience at Massara on the Park! From the moment we arrived, the staff was kind, welcoming, and very attentive throughout our meal. The décor is simple and understated, which makes the space feel relaxed and comfortable.

We started with the Griglia Ciabatta (Classico with olive oil, garlic & salt) and it was so good we completely forgot to take a picture before eating almost all of it! Perfectly crisp on the outside, soft on the inside, and incredibly flavorful.

The Candele with ragù genovese and parmigiano was absolutely delicious, with deep, rich flavor in every bite. The portion was on the smaller side but with the rich flavor, any larger would have been too heavy.

The standout of the night was the Smoked Pork Chop with pancetta and quince mostarda, hands down the best pork chop we’ve ever had! It was unbelievably tender, juicy, and packed with flavor. The waitress gave us a heads up that it takes 20 mins, which worked for us because we were able to start with the Candele, which gave us some time to truly enjoy it.

We also enjoyed two sides: Sunchoke, roasted with fig gremolata and the Zucca Calabrese with squash with hazelnut & peperoncino, both beautifully prepared and full of flavor.

Finally for dessert we had the Torta di Ricotta e Pistachio. Which had great flavor and texture and a little crunch on top.

Everything we ordered was outstanding. Incredible food, attentive service, and a welcoming atmosphere. We can’t wait to go back!

A really spectacular brunch at Massara! While we had been to the restaurant multiple times for dinner and loved every moment, this was our first time tasting their daytime menu, and it did not disappoint. The signature pastas are, of course, not to be missed (the candele and quadratti are both out of this world) but the brunch specific offerings were also delicious—the eggs in purgatory had one of the best tomato sauces I’ve ever eaten!
The new space is beautiful and spacious, and the service, as always, was impeccably warm and attentive. Will definitely be adding this to the “return” list ASAP!

Honestly thought booking a reservation would be harder, but I guess that month ahead planning worked out!

We went in as a duo at around 7:00pm. At the temporary location, we asked for a coat check and got seated at a dark, isolated location. As there were still open tables, we were curious on why we were led so far away from the center of the restaurant. We asked to sit somewhere where the ambiance was felt and they said okay! After moving, we quickly ordered our food: paccheri, candele, and swordfish.

The pasta tasted so fresh and felt homemade, like in Italy! The paccheri was so flavorful and the candele was definitely unique! The swordfish was cut open but very little meat to be blunt. However, it was a charming experience and we definitely enjoyed the food!

We booked a last minute reservation on Friday night and were blown away. We’ve been to Rezdora and had been meaning to visit Massara for some time. Turned out to be a lovely date night for us. All team members we interacted with were very warm and knowledgeable. We were checked on multiple times throughout the meal and our water glasses were always full. We shared several dishes - the chicory salad, fluke crudo, quadrati (lobster ravioli), cheesemaker’s ravioli, corteccia, veal cheek, torta di pistachio / ricotta and a cross between a lemon meringue tart / olive oil cake and gelato. Can’t remember the name of the tart but I included a pic of it. The texture was perfect and it seemed there was actual drizzled olive oil in the center. It was truly a special dessert. The attention to detail here was refreshing. Can’t wait to come back!

Honestly I am just disappointed and I am not one to ever write a bad review. When looking for a special place to take my partner for our anniversary- Massara on park showed up and upon some a minor glance at infatuations review on it I thought it could be a good spot to celebrate. Boy was I wrong. First of all- do not trust those photos- the portion sizes are teeny and you WILL leave hungry. Contrary to many other poor reviews , we were actually sat on time, only to be asked twice what our water preference was and not receiving any for the first 15 minutes. 45 minutes after being sat , our cocktail order is dropped. Service was so intentionally upselling the most expensive items- when asked about gin recommendations the only item the server recommended was the priciest on the list (classic) which my partner only ordered because the dizzy rabbit (gin AND vodka) cocktail only really tasted like celery - one would expect more from such a spirit forward beverage. The food was fine- the pastas were good except for the lobster ravioli- which clearly featured below par lobster (chewy from frozen and not the melt in your mouth deliciousness you expect from a restaurant at this level). We ordered a bottle of wine which was “lost” because the other sommelier went who knows where and was served after finishing our second (2/3) pastas. Honestly we received better hospitality from our uber on the ride home. Maybe our expectations were high or maybe this restaurant just kinda disappoints.  All I know is we won’t be going back and it definitely will be an anniversary meal to remember (and not in a good way).

Food was delicious and the experience was lovely. Taking off a star because a couple sat down at the table next to us 30 minutes into our meal and by the end of the meal they got their last course before us. Service just slowed down a lot for us until the table next to us eventually surpassed us and it didn’t feel like the level of service you should get from a place with a Michelin star. We also ordered a cocktail mid-way through the meal and we were about to receive our last course and the cocktail still hadn’t come so we canceled it since they had clearly forgotten and my partner didn’t want to continue drinking so close to the end of the meal and instead of cancelling and making it up in another way they ended up bringing out multiple drinks for us to taste which is definitely nice but we didn’t really want to continue drinking (hence us canceling the drink). Not a big deal but definitely to be noted! Otherwise the meal was yummy.

Such an incredible and unique tasting menu.

I had fish (and a fish head that tasted like a chicken wing) that I would've never ordered on my own.

The highlights of the menu were
1. Steak with the sourdough tortilla
2. Taco
3. Potato with onion
4. Dessert of macarons, bonbons, and custard
5. Chicken wing fish head thing

I did the spirit pairing and got to taste a lot of unique Mezcal, Tequila, and Sotol. Probably something like 8-10 oz of liquor by the end.

My wife did the wine pairing which was very hearty. Probably 3-4 oz pours for each portion of food.

I am definitely going to go back. We saw lobster leaving the kitchen that I want to get my grubby hands on.

We ended up spending a little over 2 hours on dinner

Excellent! Food was delicious! We will definitely be returning for a la carte. We did the tasting menu and it was a great introduction to what we can look forward to on a future visit. Sourdough tortilla was divine. The perfect tortilla. 1st bite was my favorite. Thanks for a great night and outstanding food. 100% recommend.

Loved the menu and food at Corima. We made reservations 2 days before so coukd not get the tasting menu, but tried few things from their regular menu. Lobster was one of the best I have ever had and the tortilla with butter was very addictive. Will be back again!

Incredible Mexican Asian fusion.

Usually against skipping the tasting menu at a place like this, but going a la carte was absolutely the right call. I only tried 5-6 dishes (they recommend 2-3 dishes pp), but the highs were some of the most unique flavor profiles I’ve experienced in a Mexican restaurant.

Sourdough Tortilla + Recado Negro butter - Didn’t think much of it at first. Just a warm tortilla to nibble on. Then it hit me. I wasn’t dipping sourdough into butter, I was dipping tortilla into butter. The recado negro butter was borderline life-changing. Deep, smoky umami, almost like spreading beef tallow across your palate. Normally, butter and tortillas wouldn’t even cross my mind together, but the sourdough-like tang in the tortilla practically demanded it. I kept tearing off pieces long after I was full, even after demolishing the lobster.

Beef Cecina Tlayuda - A classic Oaxacan street food (and my first time having it). They referred to it as a “Mexican pizza,” which felt accurate. I could’ve probably eaten a dozen “slices” on the spot. Intensely aromatic, restrained but deliberate umami from an edamame-based guacamole (instead of avocado), and a pile of seasoned raw beef that was unapologetically beefy and satisfying.

Langosta Zarandeada - I’ve never seen an entire butterflied lobster served like this in a fine-dining setting. Grilled whole, yet the texture was as delicate as if it had been gently poached. The sauce was their take on a lime-infused XO, but the real magic came from mixing it with the juices pooled in the head. Also there was also something undeniably primal about cracking open a lobster with your hands at the counter of a Michelin-starred restaurant. Messy, tactile, but incredibly fun.

This is pizza done right 👍 I wanted to try the Johnny Peppers since it seems like it would be the most packed flavor pie. And I was right. Bell peppers, hot cherry peppers, onions, garlic, sausage all incorporated with gooey cheese and tomatoey sauce. Dispite all those toppings this pizza manages to taste light. I didn't feel heavy after eating. The location is on the smaller size and the day that owner it was a little too warm inside the restaurant. Staff wasn't that great. But definitely go for the pizza 🍕

Nothing scream more New York than a hidden pizza shop in a subway entrance.

Have being passing this little hidden spot every time we are taking the 1 train home on 50th street after a show nearby and we finally sat foot in.

One pie is good for sharing. The pie came out fast, love the doughy crust although a little sloppy just be careful not to burn your tongue because you just want to gaucho it down once you start.

The space reminds me of a 80’ vibe, a little small but they have many tables and can be joined together to sit a large group. For those big group who wants to get a late night snack after a show all together, head there asap it gets filled up quickly as many others are thinking of the same.

What a cool experience! This is more of a casual pizza spot in downtown 1 subway at 50th Street. It's a retro kind of feel, the place was popping! It was definitely a mix of tourists and locals. It felt like a unique but authentic experience in NYC, which is rare, usually 'unique' experiences can end up being kitschy/overpriced.

The pizza was SO delicious- Neapolitan style. We were actually struggling with all of the choices, because everything sounded so good. We went to their bar next door afterwards, Nothing Really Matters, and it was super lively at around 10 pm, and was actually going to get even livelier, according to the host. Oh! And there was an awesome dj.
The staff was super kind and very prompt. The food was amazing, and the vibes were vibing. I loved having the smaller dining area, makes NYC feel a little less crowded
Had an incredible experience at See No Evil Pizza. The pizza, appetizers, and desserts were absolutely delicious. Service was excellent. Definitely will be back.

Amazing experience here. One of the most affordable tasting menu's in NYC at $150 - especially for a Michelin star restaurant. Quality is amazing, the food fresh and cooked to perfection, seasoning on point. My standout dishes were the Caviar Kim, Uni Kim, Jook and Branzino. Staff is friendly and crisp in terms of watching and anticipating what diners need. Special shoutout to Tenzin! She is such a sweet server. I plan to come back in the late spring/early summer to see what changes on the menu but definitely to experience the Caviar Kim again!!

JUA offers a modern and thoughtful Korean tasting menu in an intimate, contemporary setting. There were so many highlights throughout the meal: the caviar Kim opened with decadent, punchy flavors, followed by the Uni Kim with deep umami and crisp seaweed. The mulhoe ceviche was refreshing with a good kick, and the abalone jook was hearty and comforting, if a bit risotto-like. The smoked branzino was a standout - rich, crispy-skinned, and served in a smoky, zesty broth - and the lamb with banchan delivered a fun mix of flavors and inventive sides.

Dessert also ended things on a high with a bright mandarin–yuzu ice cream and a chewy, deeply satisfying goguma juak. Overall, the meal was beautifully composed and thoroughly enjoyable.

What a special meal - one of the best, more affordable fine dining spots in the city. Each course has its unique taste, leaving you both satisfied while anticipating the next dish. My personal favorites were the caviar kim, jook, and donut. Coming in, I was worried that my expectations would not be met, but Jua exceeded all of them.

The service, the food, the experience - everything is top tier. It’s $140 for a 7 course tasting experience with 3 “apps”, 2 entrees and 2 desserts. Some of the bites were the best I’ve ever had. The Jook, branzino and the goguma juak were my favorites. I think this is a must try spot! (They’re changing their menu next week)

Excellent Korean tasting menu for $140, the quality was superior for the price. Caviar Kim was a favorite, excellent amuse bouche. The mulhoe with raw shrimp was cold and refreshing, nice acidity. Jook was very savory and creamy, the branzino had the richest sauce, and the lamb was a gorgeously plated course that was a nice take on Korean bbq and banchan. Every course was perfect. Didn’t love the wine pairing, would have preferred a bottle of full bodied white instead. The atmosphere is a bit cold and cavernous, but overall great experience.

Would have got 5 stars but horrible ipa selection. I only drink good ipa and they only had Laganitas brewed by anheiser bush. Garbage ipa like a Budweiser!  Burgers are legendary with good round fries. Prices are fantastic especially forvthe burgers on the upper east side like $16 with bacon and cheese. Waitress very attentive and kind. I used to live 3 blocks away in the 80s and 90s. The charm of the place still remains. They just need a better beer selection should support a local brewery and have a NY brewing company ipa! Go for the burgers.

If you’re looking for a classic New York burger experience, JG Melon is a solid choice. The food is decent and consistent, and it’s even mentioned in the Michelin Guide, which says a lot about its reputation. The burgers are simple, juicy, and done right — no fuss, just quality.

And the cottage fries are a must-try — crispy, golden, and the perfect side to their classic cheeseburger. The cozy, old-school atmosphere makes the whole experience feel very “New York.”

While visiting my favorite butcher last week two sanitation employees were talking about Skinflints. Being the busybody I am, I joined their conversation & was told if I liked Skinflints then I would love JG Melon. I figured since we liked two of the same businesses I’d give JG a try. I’m glad to say they were correct. It’s 1st come 1st served at JG. Even though it was pretty busy I was able to get a seat at the bar easily enough. (Though I was told it gets much much busier than it was during my visit) Tommy the bartender was a down to earth people person which is always a plus in my book. The bacon cheeseburger I ordered was cooked just the way I like it & cottage fries happen to be one of my three favorite types of fries (four if I count sweet potato). The restaurant is small but the food food & service were amazing. I had two glasses of Jameson neat with my meal & lunch still ended up just under $50. So I’d say it’s reasonably priced. If you’re in the area & you enjoy a great burger definitely check it out. It’s a short walk from  Bloomingdales if you enjoy walking on nice days.

JG Melon – 3rd Ave

Unfortunately, this was a very disappointing experience.

The only positive thing I can say is about the hostess, who was very kind, welcoming, and genuinely tried to help.

Aside from that, the service was very poor. The staff showed no friendliness, no smiles, and no sense of care or attention.

We waited outside for about 40–50 minutes to be seated. After placing our order, we waited almost another 40 minutes for the food to arrive.

When the burger finally came, it was overcooked and burnt. We ordered the burger medium well, but it arrived well done and dry.

Overall, the long wait times, lack of service, and incorrect food preparation made this a frustrating experience. Very disappointing, especially given the restaurant’s reputation.

I love the checkered green and white table clothes and grey poupon mustard on every table.  This place is known for their delicious burgers and I ordered a bacon cheeseburger that lived up to the hype with its size and taste. It's a bit crowded with tables close together but definitely worth the visit. It's cash only, so bring cash with you.

Absolutely amazing. You could not ask for better food, fresh ingredients, traditional, well presented and a fast and efficient service. I could not have asked for more. I recommend the omakase, I could have gone on eating until I burst but had to say stop  eventually. Bravo. The best sushi I have eaten in the US, Europe, and Japan.

In an era where the omakase experience is getting increasingly commercialized, this longtime institution clearly stands out with its professionalism and excellent quality fish. They’ve been around since the 90s and honestly, it shows. It was a breath of fresh air to come here and not eat the exact same pieces of fish you get at the majority of omakase spots in NYC. Highlights include saltwater eel, mackerel (both kinds), firefly squid and more. Even the toro tastes superior to most other places.

We had sushi there yesterday and it was truly an amazing experience. The chef was not only highly skilled and professional, but also very funny, which made the whole dining experience even more enjoyable. The sushi and sashimi were incredibly fresh—honestly the freshest and best I’ve ever had. Every bite was full of clean, natural flavor. Highly recommend!

TLDR: Visiting from LA. Beautiful, upscale sushi bar better suited for omakase or a proper sit-down. Toro and Spanish mackerel were excellent. Pricey for a quick bite.

We dropped a rental nearby and walked into Sushi Yasuda looking for some rolls. It’s really a reservation-leaning spot with a calm, minimalist counter setup, ideal for omakase at lunch or dinner. Staff was professional and kind; the manager felt a bit stressed, but our chef at the back counter was friendly and helpful.

We kept it simple with a few cut rolls and a couple of nigiri. The toro and Spanish mackerel were standouts clean flavor and perfect rice. Rolls were well made. For a light order, the bill was about $120 before tip, so expect premium pricing.

If you want a fast, casual sushi stop, there are easier options. If you want a refined counter experience with top fish, this is a strong choice.

Pro tips
• Book a counter seat for omakase to get the full value. That’s the chef’s specialty.
• Come at lunch if you want a calmer vibe.
• Expect premium prices even for a small order.
Best sushi I’ve had in a long time and I lived in Tokyo for more than a decade. I did the omakase menu and wasn’t disappointed! Everything was fresh, well made, and awesome experience

A true gem of NYC vibes!!
I came without a reservation on, what seemed a pack night, but we were able to sit in the next 10 mins as the service is very quick and efficient. We dined before going to a Broadway show and it was PERFECT!! The pizzas came incredibly fast and were so good. In and out with dessert included in basically 45 mins.
Highly recommended!!

Ps: Don’t you dare to skip the Nutella Pizza! 🤎

Insane! The pizza was off the chain. The fresh sauce and mozzarella were bursting with flavor. Basil...yum!Definitely more New York style crust. Different from the crispy New Haven style that I'm more used to.
I only cut a star because it was just so cramped. They packed us in like sardines. Worth it though. I couldn't recommend any more highly.

Having a pizza from a world champion pizza maker is a unique experience. We enjoyed every bite of every pie we tried!!! Thanks Giorgia for such an amazing xmas taste gift!!!

You should try the diavola and the fried pizza

A beautiful American Italian restaurant in the heart of midtown. Gluten-free options are available and clearly marked on the menu. The gluten-free pizza is excellent, the dough taste just as regular one does. The restaurant can get loud when all tables are filled, the bar area is quieter, even though it’s at the front of the restaurant. The staff is friendly and the food is fast even when the restaurant is full.

Great place just outsidr Times Square. 30 minute wait, but service was very fast. Mostly pizza on the menu. The Calzone Fritte was delughtful - a lightly fried calzone with a soft chewy breading. The pizzas were unique and delicious but did not depart too far from tradition.

First time at a Cambodian restaurant and there were so many good options. Server was super nice and very helpful with selections, although most were the favorites recommended by others. I really enjoyed the Khmer Noodles and got the one with shrimp and thin rice noodles. The Loc Lac is a traditional Cambodian dish and had a nice black peppery zing. The Baked Amok is also a very traditional dish and great place to start the Cambodian food journey. I would recommend this restaurant.

We had a great meal at this Cambodian spot. The atmosphere is lovely—very upscale, like a premium Asian restaurant. The service was impeccable, and the food was delicious. What made it special was dining next to the large Buddha statue, which gave the entire experience a wonderful sense of calm.

It was busy when we got there probably around 7pm. But service was super nice and our server helps us a lot with the food since it’s our first time trying Cambodian food. Love the spicy noodle (almost like drunkman noodle) and we really liked the appetizers with 3 dipping! So good! And we’ll definitely would come back again!

One of the best restaurants I’ve ever been to! Not only did the food blow us away and was clearly made to order, but the staff were incredibly attendant and personable. Excellent meal!!! Can’t wait to return. Highly reco the shrimp & scallops, the pork skewers and the Ari noodle. Chefs kiss!

The restaurant was beautiful decorated with Cambodian temples & photos and the scent of incense smelled like my mom’s home. The host greeted us with warm smiles and the waiter Evan was fantastic! We started off Khmer fish cakes and prakhok crudite both I grew up eating!  I had the chefs special amok!  We finished with corn pudding.  My husband and I Absolutely loved our experience  and will be back!

Unique and delicious meal in a special atmosphere. Friendly, helpful staff. With reservations, we were seated immediately on a Friday night. People without reservations were waiting as CheLi was bustling. Reasonable prices, generous portions. Loved the dumplings, Beggar's Chicken and sautéd green beans. "Crispy Lava", black sweet buns filled with warm, liquid duck egg custard made a wonderful dessert. Would love to go again and try more.

We had an amazing dinner here at Che li! The service was so great and attentive. The food came out perfect timing and everything was delicious. The soup dumplings were the best and the portion were great for sharing. We left so full and they even gave us a complimentary dessert on the house which was warm and delicious. I’ll definitely be coming back here for a date night or girls night out. The vibe is so cute and the drinks are also amazing! The tea is perfect for a cold winter night.

We visited Zhe Li during Chinese New Year and made an online reservation in advance for 8:15 pm. I had confidently told my friend beforehand that Zhejiang cuisine has many delicious dishes and that this restaurant had strong online ratings. Unfortunately, we left feeling extremely disappointed.

First, the seating situation was chaotic. When we arrived, there wasn’t even a proper space to queue — everyone was crowded together near the entrance. The staff were clearly overwhelmed, and despite having reservations, guests were not seated in any clear order. We watched people with the same reservation time — or even later time slots — get seated before us. We ended up waiting about 20 minutes past our reservation time.

Second, service organization was lacking. It didn’t seem like servers were assigned to specific sections. Ordering and paying depended entirely on finding someone available. We had to repeatedly remind staff, and during busy moments it was easy to be overlooked. To be fair, the young staff members were hardworking and polite despite the chaos — the issue seemed more like management and organization rather than individual effort.

Third, the food was underwhelming, especially for New York, where the overall dining standard is quite high. The vegetable shoots had many tough stems and were slightly too salty. The mushroom rice was fragrant and nicely mixed for us by the server, but surprisingly sweet — I don’t understand why so much sugar would be added to mushroom rice. The chicken and intestines were spicy as expected, but again leaned overly sweet and salty. The owner even mentioned to a neighboring table that because many students dine there, the flavors are intentionally heavier.

Dishes also arrived in a very irregular order. The crispy duck was served one hour and fifteen minutes after we were seated — by that point, we were already full. The dessert, however, was decent.

We spent around $140. The price itself wasn’t the issue, but the overly sweet and salty flavors do not represent authentic Zhejiang cuisine in our view. Unfortunately, this was not a good experience for us.

The first time we came, the restaurant was so popular that we couldn’t get in. On our second visit, we were seated in a wonderful spot.

We would especially like to thank the kind and attentive server, Ting Ting. Her detailed introductions to every dish helped us choose exactly what we loved. Her warmth made us want to come back again. During the meal, when we accidentally started coughing, she thoughtfully brought us a gentle warm drink that soothed our throats.

The manager, Jimmy, was also very humble and professional. His service was thorough and attentive, he handled our requests perfectly, and greeted us sincerely. He truly went the extra mile to take care of every guest’s needs.

The level of professionalism we experienced was outstanding, just like the food itself. Thank you all for taking such great care of us. We are already loyal fans and look forward to our next visit.

I love this place so much. The prices are very reasonable for the quality of food you get, and everything we ordered was delicious. My favorites are the crispy duck, pork belly, and the desserts. They were all perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated, which makes the whole dining experience even better. Great food, great atmosphere, and definitely a spot I’ll be coming back to for sure.

I am finally getting around to writing this review after a stellar experience at Dagon back in December, and the memory of that meal is still just as vivid. From start to finish, it was a flawless 5-star experience.
The atmosphere was immediately festive and welcoming with their beautiful Christmas decor, setting the perfect mood for a holiday meal. The service was truly top-tier; our waitress, Mejda, and the entire staff were incredibly kind and attentive.
What really stood out to me were the "little things" that demonstrate true culinary professionalism. I was so impressed when one of the servers, while helping us plate our shared dishes, was careful not to use the same utensils for the seafood and non-seafood items. That level of mindfulness and attention to detail is rare and highly appreciated.
As for the food, every single dish was a hit. The steak skewers, cauliflower, and broccolini were standouts and absolute must-orders, but truly, nothing disappointed. The portions were very generous, and you can tell the kitchen takes great pride in the quality of their ingredients.
I would return to Dagon in a heartbeat and highly recommend it to anyone looking for incredible food paired with thoughtful, professional service. Thank you to Mejda and the team for a memorable evening!

I enjoyed an absolutely wonderful Thanksgiving dinner. Spencer, our server, was truly exceptional, warm, gracious, incredibly knowledgeable, and his wine pairing suggestion was nothing short of perfect. Thank you Dagon and Spencer for an unforgettable meal. Best!

I randomly found Dagon while walking down Broadway and decided to give it a try. I ordered the three mezze plate, and the bread it came with was incredibly fresh—a must for dipping.

I chose the marinated beets, the matbucha, and feta. All of them were excellent, but the beets really stood out; the horseradish yogurt was a fantastic touch and paired with the roasted chickpeas it elevated the whole dish.

Finished with the panna cotta which if you're a fan of rose water, you will love it. Overall, a great find and a fantastic meal!
Excellent dinner here! The food was unmatched in flavor, breads were soft and delicious, soup was hearty and the best veggie risotto I have ever had. The highlight was the dessert - Silan.
Honestly the best service I’ve had in my 8 years living in NYC. The bartender Greth was super friendly and took her time explaining the whole menu even though she was busy. I’ll definitely be back

Conveniently located where we stayed at, it was cold that night and so we decided to eat here. We were starving so we ordered a couple of things that looked appetizing. Surprisingly, everything was delicious!

Big serving for sure, there were three of us with quite an appetite and we had left overs. The rice was $2 but it was a huge bowl enough for four people. Plenty of side dishes too, all of which are good. Personally, I enjoyed the fish.

Wait was fast, we did not make a reservation, it was Sunday at around 7pm. Service was quick and prompt too.

3/7/26 from nyc. went in to try Korean fried chicken, my daughter found this spot after our convention. We find out it’s not the typical Korean fried chicken spot you would go to so we tried something else and I’ll
Leave my curious crunchy Korean friend chicken hunt for another time. Nice service, good eats. Glad we waited to snag a table. Love trying new spots

We waited 90 minutes for a table, and it was certainly worth it! We ordered the Spicy Seafood Tofu Stew, Bossam, Seafood & Scallion Pancake, and the CDG Royal Oxtail Soup. All of the dishes were prepared perfectly, but personally, the Oxtail Soup stood out as exceptional. Its broth was remarkably clean yet flavorful, partly due to the abalone, and the oxtail was wonderfully tender. This has been, by far, the best restaurant experience during our five-day trip to New York.

There’s always a long waitlist (1 hr+), but I don’t think it’s worth it. They make their tofu in house, and it’s pretty good, but overall lowkey mid and overhyped given the wait. Dubuhaus is way better imo

- Cod roe omelet ($14.99): 4/10, everyone on Beli got it, so we got it, but there wasn’t that much cod roe. Skip
- Spicy kimchi soondubu ($17.99): 8/10, pretty solid and flavorful but not mind blowing. Tofu quality was good
- Bossam ($20.99): 8/10, similar to other places
- Banchan: Standard, liked the tofu one a lot

I’ve been wanting to try this place for ages and finally got a spot during lunch hours (the wait was ~30 min)! I ordered the lunch combo (seafood pancake + spicy kimchi & beef tofu stew). Banchan and seafood pancake were so yummy! The kimchi & beef tofu stew was also good but my spice tolerance is so bad that even the mild version was still a little too spicy 😭 Would recommend though :)

Food was good I wanted to try more yet didn’t have time would try again when I return to NYC. Price was stiff for the meals the drinks was fair had a soba old fashion Japanese whiskey definitely worth the taste.

We came to The Lobster Club on a Saturday evening for a celebratory dinner. The restaurant wasn’t too busy, but we were first seated in a high-traffic area and had to ask to be moved. It seemed like booths were reserved, which felt a bit limiting for a special occasion.

The food was very good overall. We enjoyed the Wagyu Shiitake Fried Rice, Crispy Rice, Garlic Chicken, Branzino, and the Wagyu Truffle Sando. The Truffle Sando was absolutely delicious, though pricey at $66 for four small bites.

For cocktails, the Cucumber Shiso was refreshing and memorable, while the Yuzu Paloma was watery and underwhelming.

Service was fine, but there was no complimentary dessert, which many NYC restaurants offer and would have made the evening feel more special.

Overall: great flavors, but celebratory touches didn’t quite match the price point.

I’ve only ever been here to take clients out (I’ve never dined here on my own dime), but every time I’ve been it’s been amazing. The food, service, and atmosphere are all special.

One of my favorite meals I’ve ever had in the city was here at Lobster Club

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an exceptional Japanese restaurant, and it was an unforgettable experience!

We kicked off the evening at the bar with a refreshing Lychee Martini, which set the tone for the night. Once our entire party arrived, we moved to a lovely table and ordered a variety of dishes. Every single item we tried was absolutely delightful—I loved them all!

Our sommelier was fantastic and recommended the perfect bottle of sake that paired beautifully with our meal.

I can't wait to return to this gem of a restaurant! Highly recommend it to anyone looking for an amazing Japanese dining experience!

Amazing food with great service. Nothing more to say. Everything was so good!!

Highly recommend the Acharuli and Megruli. So tasty!!
The Mother Khinkali was huge! The soup base and meat filling was so comforting.
Also ordered the Shkmeruli which had the tastiest sauce. I dipped the bread from the Acharuli in it too.
Georgian salad tasted incredibly fresh and refreshing.

Well worthy of its Michelin recognition! LALIKO is a beautifully curated Georgian restaurant. Between the beautiful wall murals showing points of cultural significance, to the Georgian staff, to the absolutely scrumptious food, this restaurant is steeped in tradition. The staff are very knowledgeable, and are more than happy to share the history of the food with you. The food itself is delicious, and I left eating much more than I expected, because everything was so delightful. Will be coming back here again soon, and bringing friends.

I recently visited Lalico for a brunch event and it exceeded all expectations. The restaurant has such a cozy and stylish ambiance — you instantly feel relaxed and at home.

The Georgian cuisine was outstanding: rich flavors, beautiful presentation, and generous portions. Our group was especially impressed with the wine selection and the overall dining experience.

The staff was incredibly professional and attentive, making sure everything ran smoothly and every guest felt comfortable.

Come here just once, and you’ll instantly become one of their regular guests!

I was a guest at a brunch hosted at Lalico and I was absolutely impressed with this place. The restaurant has a warm, stylish atmosphere where you immediately feel comfortable and welcome.

The cuisine was incredible — everything was delicious, beautifully presented, and full of authentic Georgian flavor. I was especially impressed by the large selection of wines and how perfectly they complemented the dishes.

The service is truly top-tier: attentive, professional, and genuinely friendly. The team made sure every guest felt special and taken care of throughout the event.

I wholeheartedly recommend Lalico to anyone looking for a place with amazing food, a great atmosphere, and excellent service. I will definitely be coming back again!

It was my second time when I visited Laliko Georgian restaurant in New York, and both times the experience was delicious. The food is amazing, my favorite is khachapuri with mint, Georgian salad with so a tasty sauce. This place is great for a big party or a small intimate dinner. highly recommend

Amazing experience at Markette! We had a lovely anniversary dinner here. I couldn’t get a reservation on resy but I called the restaurant and they were able to get us in at a reasonable time. The food and drinks were delicious - especially loved the fish, pita, and rice. The cocktails were amazing and the dessert was out of this world. Exceptional service as well. Will definitely be returning!

Markette is definitely upscale. I dined solo and chose the Braised Oxtail Gratin, it was very well done, layered, flavorful with a bit of a kick. It felt authentic, elevated and enough for a whole meal for me! Drinks were also well done by the lovely bartender Rika, I had the Snake in the Grass! Decor is tasteful, bathrooms are clean and vibey with a designer candle burning. I loved all the details! Would for sure bring girlfriends or family back here.

Food was delicious nice blend of flavors with Caribbean influences. Moody lighting and atmosphere creates a great date vibe. There is also a nice lounge downstairs with a separate menu that’s just as good. The staff are on point with everything keeping the room flowing smoothly. The one and only note I have is the portions are a little small so if there is a few things on the menu you’re choosing btwn just get them all! Plates are meant for sharing so order plenty. We had the cod fish fritters, caviar and hash browns, rock shrimp linguine, and the pan seared dorade with the stracciatella ice cream for dessert. Everything was 10/10. We will definitely be returning!

This was yummy! I liked the lamb a lot. And the cod fish fried ball things. The tuna appetizer was fresh & fun. The pasta was a skip for me. It was fine but very basic. Desserts were also OK but I wouldn’t get again.

Service is a bit odd. You have to add all the food at once so they can time it? Idk sounds a bit like poor kitchen process management.

stunning new spot. upscale and still comfortable. been three times. twice upstairs and once at argyle. the flavors haven’t left my mind since and the staff were warm, human, and approachable. oh and the drinks! the drinks.

I stopped by for dinner here and it was an amazing experience, from the drinks to the wings, ofc the pho and the unexpected incredible coffee flan. Everything came together perfectly. The pho was incredibly fragrant and felt nourishing, the wings had an amazing sauce on it, and the Bahn mi went perfect with the pho as a dip as well. The flan coffee dessert was so good that I ordered another one to go. I’m not a big fan of flan but this one might have opened me up to a new world.

Everything was sooo good! For apps, the salt and pepper squid was super crispy and flavorful. Hawker rice was delicious too. Lemongrass chicken was distinctly lemongrass flavored. Loved every bit of dinner. Such a giant piece of short rib with the UES pho. Definitely a neighborhood must go!

Lyly Vietnamese is a fantastic spot for pho lovers. The pho is excellent — rich, aromatic broth, tender meat, and perfectly cooked noodles that feel comforting and authentic. Every bite shows real care and quality. It’s no surprise that Lyly Vietnamese is mentioned in the Michelin Guide, as the food truly stands out. A must-visit for anyone craving great Vietnamese cuisine.

Really flavorful dishes depending on what you order. Cooked to perfection. The inside has a nice casual atmosphere as if you’re eating at an eatery in Saigon. Prices are usual New York fare with appetizers averaging $10-15 and entrees around $23. Also love their Thai iced tea because it’s not too sweet. Make sure to reserve in advance!

Got here at lunch time and luckily got a table for 4 right away. We have two young ones and the staff were so accommodating with crayons and coloring sheets. They checked to make sure the kids were good and provided kid friendly utensils and cups. Always a huge plus for me! The food was also delicious - my favorite was the crab cake in the hawker rice.

The cutest bar and seating decor. So much character and great vibe. Service was excellent and sever we had was knowledgable, accomodating. Everyone was so friendly and welcoming. Cocktails were not impressive but food was amazing. Chicharron and anchovie is must have if you like those dishes. Price is high for the app portion but so good. Quality here, not quantity. Mandatory garlic shrimp egg app was huge and good for sharing; yummy and well priced. The mushroom or dishes for vegeterians, not so exciting. Ended with a good flan dish.

As a fan of Ernestos, I finally got to experience Bartolo and it exceeded my expectations. The space itself was incredibly stylish and the food was fantastic.

A few standouts for me were the Anchoa Y Matequilla, Champinones Al Ajillo, Huevos Fritos Con Patatas Y Gambas, Callos A La Madrilena, and Chuleta De Buey, amongst others.

Don't sleep on the cocktails here. I would put their martini up with some of my other favorites in the city. I was also a big fan of the Espresso De Brandt which is an Espresso Martini with Pastis and Cacao. Top level!

Really awesome staff, service, and vibes. Can't wait to return.
World class dining experience! It brought be back to Spain instantly! Chef Ryan is using the best ingredients and cooking with incredible technique. Each bites makes you want to try the next!

Sexy, beautiful little restaurant... It's a sprawling but tight space, so newbie fabulous-affective passive-aggressive transplants are fortunately forced to actively engage with and experience actual New Yorkers... It's a great Spanish restaurant, in the West Village, and it's flippin' delicious...

The ajo blanco is one of the best dishes I’ve eaten in New York City. It’s a perfect balance of texture, cream, salt, and sweet.

The anchovies with butter, the chicharron with almonds, and the braised oxtail with potatoes were spectacular. I prefer the tortilla at Ernesto’s, but Bartolo’s thin and runny version was very well done.

The torcino dessert with plums, almond cookies, and a rich crumble was pure heaven.

Our server was great. And the decor is stunning. Every detail—the paneled walls, the rose colored seating, and the matador prints—make you feel like you’re living a Hemingway novel.

Go here. It’s really good.

I had the most amazing experience at La Tête d’Or, from the moment we walked in. The restaurant itself is absolutely beautiful. The food was outstanding. Everything tasted incredibly fresh and high quality. The filet mignon was hands down the best I’ve ever had — perfectly cooked, melt-in-your-mouth tender, and full of flavor. Truly unforgettable. The crab cake was delicious, the popovers were incredible, and the Brussel sprouts were amazing (I’m already thinking about when I can have them again!). My husband had the 28 day ribeye and it  was EXCELLENT. The vanilla berry soft serve was like nothing I’ve ever experienced.. literally the perfect ending to our night. Can’t wait to try the other flavor. The service was just as impressive as the food. Everyone was fantastic — from the servers, to the hosts and hostesses, and even the QUEEN running the coat check. You can tell they take pride in creating a top-tier experience. This was an amazing night all around. La Tête d’Or has officially made its way to the top of my steakhouse list in NYC. I can’t wait to come back!!

Amazing experience at this restaurant. The food and drinks were outstanding, and the service was top-notch. My favorite dishes included the yellowfin tuna tartare, and the filet mignon was the best I’ve ever tasted! Geraldo, our server, was fantastic—very kind, friendly, and attentive, just like the rest of the staff. It made my birthday dinner truly special. This restaurant is excellent overall. I give it a 10/10 and will recommend it to everyone. I’ll definitely be returning!

To start the place was beautiful. As a starter we ordered a bone marrow which was good but the red stuff on top overpowered the taste of the actual bone marrow. As for the filet mignon it was cooked to perfection. The NY strip was also delicious. We finished our dinner with a delicious ginormous coffee Sundae! The coffee taste wasn’t as strong and the different toppings were a great pair with the ice cream.

I had the pleasure of dining at La Tête d’Or by Daniel, and it was an absolutely exceptional experience from start to finish.

Every detail was on point. We began with the hamachi crudo, which was incredibly fresh and beautifully balanced. The wood-fired bone marrow was rich and indulgent, packed with deep flavor. For our mains, the filet mignon topped with foie gras was cooked to perfection — tender, flavorful, and perfectly executed. The Chateaubriand was equally impressive, prepared exactly as requested and simply outstanding.

Beyond the food, the service elevated the entire evening. Our server, Victor, was knowledgeable, attentive, and made excellent recommendations that truly enhanced our experience. The manager, Elvir, personally stopped by to ensure everything was going well, which speaks volumes about the level of hospitality here. Even Jenny at coat check was warm and welcoming — every touchpoint felt thoughtful.

This is not just dinner — it’s a full experience. Exceptional cuisine, impeccable service, and an atmosphere that makes you want to stay all night. Highly recommend, and I can’t wait to return.

Traveled to NYC with a friend to order Chef Daniel’s 34 ounce Cote De Bouef.  It was spectacular!  Seasoned  and cooked perfecty!  We also ordered the Prime Rib which was also beautifully cooked and the best Prime Rib That I have ever eaten.  We had three side sauces, Bordelaise, Bearnaise and Horseradish Cream sauces.  Each were perfect.  The Bordelaise tasted like the pure essence of beef.  The sides were also exceptional, particularly the roasted Marrow Bones.  The service was incredibly professional from the host, bartender and our waiter Thomas.  Food, cocktails, wine and service all aspects of a great evening were exceptional.

We were fortunate to meet and talk with Chef Daniel  for a few minutes and found him to be very welcoming and glad to engage with his guests.  It was an honor to meet with him and have his insight and recommendations on our menu selections.
Just a an all around excellent experience!

Bit of a mixed bag here. The room is cool, chill vibes, good music and lighting and professional, friendly service. We had the “surprise” 6 course tasting menu. There was definitely a problem in the kitchen because there were some extremely long delays between courses, our meal took 2 1/2 hours.
We started with the complimentary focaccia, delicious and we went for the ricotta upcharge, $10 for 2 tablespoons of ricotta. Not sure the value proposition was there.

Flavors were generally on point, the eggplant with some charred greens was OK but didn’t love it.  Favorite dish was the crab agnolotti, scrumptious.

The bucatini served before that was perfectly cooked, but was excessively salty, apparently because of the capers as we mentioned the issue to the server. However, it definitely tasted like someone slipped with the salt shaker. Our main was a kind of disappointing plate of mini meatballs in a sweet and savory sauce. Interesting but for $129 menu maybe we expected more than mini meatballs.

Dessert was a scoop of peach and Prosecco sorbet, refreshing, but a little bit underwhelming for dessert on a tasting menu. I guess as I am writing this I kind of wanted to like it more than I actually ended up liking it.

This place was spectacular! We got the agnolotti and the rabbit ragu along with the salad. I make pasta art from scratch at home as a hobby so visiting here and eating the handmade pasta has been a dream of mine. The service was so friendly and efficient. Everything lived up to the hype! I only visit NYC one day a year and this restaurant is worth it.

We didn’t have a reservation and only stopped by for a glass of champagne. When they realized we were celebrating our marriage, they surprised us with a delicious dessert on the house, which was incredibly kind and thoughtful.
The entire place has such positive energy — great atmosphere, beautiful presentation, and amazing food (looking good on the tables). Every detail felt special. Without a doubt, we will be coming back the next time we’re in New York.

Cozy small restaurant great for groups of 2-4ppl. They have a curated seasonal menu and nice wine pairings.

The Foccacia was so fresh and almost croissant flaky 🥐
All of our pastas were excellent

Wildly, wildly good. Lovely ambiance, quality service, and exceptional food.

We tried the following:
- Short rib agnolotti
- Cacio e pepe
- Linguini & clams
- Dark chocolate gelato

Finally checked out the new Le Veau D'Or for lunch and it far exceeded my expectations. Staff is wonderful, helpful, welcoming, super friendly. I ordered the mackerel, the lobster salad (sublime) and the Il Flottante (the best I've ever had). Also had two gin gimlets and big shoutout for the bread service (really scrumptious). The mackerel was the only thing that, for me, was underwhelming.
I was also extremely happy to see that they have redone the restaurant in a very gentle way that still pays homage to the past. Very warm and cozy ambiance.

I’ve been torn about writing this review but 2 stars it is. We heard about this place through Kaitlyn Lavery, a NYC food reviewer who rated this her #1 spot of 2025. We came here for an anniversary dinner with high hopes and unfortunately left disappointed.

Ambience is great. Small, intimate space that feels like an NYC institution (like 4 Charles or Carbone).

Service was excellent and saved the review. Staff are all extremely friendly and good at their jobs.

Really enjoyed our cocktails though on the pricey end (even for NYC) at $26 a pop.

The food was the disappointment. $135 tasting menu and they were out of the duck. Their most popular dish. Kaitlyn’s favorite dish of 2025. The entire reason we came here. I think it’s just unacceptable to run out of your most popular dish for a $500 meal. The rest of the food was fine - nothing blew me away (and this might just be because it’s French food) but we enjoyed each dish and liked the chicken and steak.

Sadly I think this was a “one and done” spot and the fact that they didn’t have the one dish that we wanted to try kind of ruined the experience. I wouldn’t come back here to take a shot at being able to have the duck when there’s so many other great returants you can eat at for less than $500 and actually get what you want (a meal for 2 at Torrisi is less than this and is arguably the best in the city).

Came with high hopes but left disappointed.

I think there are some pros and cons about this place!

We really enjoyed the service and a few of the dishes. In particular the duck was amazing, and the fries were perfect. Beet and boudin appetizers were good. I really enjoyed the chartreuse ice cream on the chocolate dessert, though the crepes suzettes were too sweet with the tropical addition.

However it’s overpriced in our opinion. $135 for 3 courses (plus one green salad) is a lot when it would be $80-90 at an equivalent à la carte restaurant. The set menu is required for dining at tables. It’s basically like a main dish costs $90 if dessert and app cost $45.

Plus, I thought it was frustrating that there was no wine by the glass menu. Just a verbal list from the waiter with 3-4 options. (No list means no prices unless asked)

It ended up being $440 for 2 people with 3 drinks included.

I can certainly see why people like it here, it just wasn’t the right value to us knowing other options in NYC.

Much hyped French bistro was good but nothing outstanding. Stopped in for $85 two course fixed price lunch. Mackerel was a good starter. The steak frites was ok but nothing outstanding better than the plethora of other French bistros in NYC. Service was prompt and friendly. The space is beautiful though with an old world charm about it and probably the only thing you’re going to remember. Plus at this price point value rating is pretty low too. Place is still very buzzy, completely full at 2p on a Thursday. Verdict: will not return but recommend once for the vibe.

We absolutely loved Le Veau d’Or and would recommend it! Both the lamb and duck were cooked to perfection ,the duck was incredibly tender and flavorful, while the lamb’s gamey taste was handled beautifully.

The escargot was probably one of the best I’ve had in the city. The frog legs weren’t particularly special in flavor, but they were beautifully presented and still enjoyable.

That said, the service left us feeling rushed from the very beginning. Our server came by several times to take our order when we had literally just sat down. Since the menu has no descriptions and we don’t speak French, it took us a bit longer to read. From ordering to finishing our meal, the entire experience was over in just a little more than an hour…even though our reservation was at 5 PM and the place was fully booked, we felt pushed to eat quickly and pay, which really took away from the overall enjoyment.

The tasting menu here is very unique. The mushroom soup was actually the highlight of the whole menu for me! Definitely do the Abalone dish add on. The sea urchin add on was also very interesting to taste. To wrap up, both desserts were very refreshing. Service was very good and the whole restaurant has very cosy vibes, without the “corporate” style that some Michelin stars have.

As a Korean, this maybe very far from the Korean food that I am used to but it was my first fine dining experience so bear with me.

All the dishes were Korean inspired, I wouldn’t say they were necessarily Korean food. All the dishes and their ingredients scream Korean but it didn’t feel or taste like it. The tuna bibimbap I got was good and my favourite of the night but it’s not the one that your family would eat of a communal bowl with literally every single fixing. The banana milk dessert also didn’t taste like banana milk at all, I was chasing that nostalgic feeling the entire night but was left feeling a longing for my mom’s cooking instead.
