We ordered guacamole as well the chips are stale and oily. I hope the management look into it and considering their market prices.

Loved it.  Dropped in for Sunday lunch after Bethel Noho service.

Tostada del mar - super fresh mackerel with a bite. Then pork.  Classic margarita.

Restaurant is light and airy.

Do try Bethel NYC. You can’t help but be changed.

Delicious Mexican spot, loved the pork Al pastor and all the sauces 😍 it was absolutely delicious, all the ingredients were fresh and the service was amazing!

Even with all the tortillas and the generous portions, we (a table of 4) felt full (but not heavy and stuffed) after the meal.

HIGHLY recommend

Came in to kill some time and get a bite to eat.  I didn’t have any expectations but WOW, what I thought would be a basic burrito was really flavorful and perfect.  I added avo, but there was also a side sauce (wish I knew what it was!) and the combination was just delicious.  I ended up getting the churros with dulce de leche - also amazing and just the right portions (you can order 2 or 4, I ordered 2).  I wanted to take the dulce home but I figured I was being ridiculous… The afternoon service was perfect - just a few customers, no wait, and friendly staff.  The place was clean and the tequila selection looked interesting.  I’ll have to try a cocktail next time.  Can’t wait to come back 💕

Cozy and intimate omakase tempura restaurant where everything is fried fresh to serve. Great ambiance with excellent customer service and a rotating menu depending on what's in season. Reserve ahead of time since there is only 6 seats.

Food 5/5
Service 5/5
Ambiance 5/5

My hubby took me here for my birthday and it was such a unique experience. I never had a tempura omakase before! The setting is super intimate with only 6 seats, and the chef explains each piece before you eat it, which made it feel extra special.

The menu starts with 2 appetizers, followed by 8 tempura omakase pieces, and we added on the Miyazaki A5 wagyu (highly recommend) then dessert.

Each bite tasted incredibly fresh, surprisingly light and clean for tempura.

What we had for tempura:
Tiger shrimp
Shishito pepper
Eel
Japanese water eggplant
Japanese Spanish mackerel
Sweet potato
Hokkaido uni
Hokkaido scallop
And the Miyazaki wagyu? Hands down one of the best I’ve had outside of Japan, it literally melts in your mouth.

Dessert was my least favorite part but overall, this was such a special and memorable experience!

This experience really reminded me of Japan. Everything cooked here was made with excellent quality and care.

Food: The course I had ended with a Cod entree, which was very good. Made to perfection. The ingredients were very fresh. I don't know if the food is worth the price, however, it is definitely worth it for the experience if you miss Japan.

Environment: Cozy restaurant that would make you feel like you stepped into a restaurant in Japan. The Chef, kitchen, environment all would make you feel like you're in a different country.

I went Secchu Yokota yesterday for my birthday.  Secchu Yokota, was by far the best eating experience I've had in NYC in a very long time. This was my first Omakase experience and it was delightful. Thank you to the hostesses, Ari, the manager, Diamon, and the amazing Chef.  We will definitely be back!

Best hidden gem in the city!
I had bookmarked this place over a year ago, and I finally decided to try it out for my 30th birthday. I’m so glad I did, I wouldn’t have wanted to celebrate anywhere else. After nearly three years of living in NYC, I can confidently say this was the best dining experience I’ve had (disclaimer: I’m a foodie lol).

The owners, Ari and her husband, Chef Atsushi Yokota, and the restaurant manager Daimu, go above and beyond to create an exceptional dining experience for every customers and you can truly feel their passion. The food was absolutely top notch. Chef Yokota holds incredibly high standards for every ingredient, sourcing them with care to ensure everything tastes like it’s straight from a top-tier restaurant in Japan.

The tempura was phenomenal, we savored every single piece.
Thank you again for the unforgettable experience. We’re def coming back soon!

Awesome food and fun, lively environment. The portions are pretty sizable and everything was mouthwateringly delicious! Gejang (raw crab) was flavorful and didn't have any off flavors. Rose tteopoki was creamy and yummy. Jokbal was solid. The spicy octopous with creamy rissoto was kind of like the rose tteopoki. Spicy flavors alternated with cream/dairy. The banana milk bingsoo also tasted just like banana milk which was fun

My friends and I have needed a spot for girls night and scored a reservation for Seoul Salon. This place was absolutely packed for a Thursday night, so definitely grab a reservation before you go. We were seated in a smaller room allowing for a more intimate dining experience.

We ordered their limited time yellowtail platter, grilled tteokgalbi, rose tteokbokki with gimmari, Seoul salon pasta, and jokbal platter. The yellowtail platter came with a seasonal porridge, cuttlefish, whelk salad, sauces, aged kimchi, and gim. While it's recommended for 2, it easily fed the three of us. Their rose tteokbokki was really flavorful but we enjoyed it even more after it had cooled down and the flavors seeped in more. Their seoul salon pasta was the perfect amount of umami and one of our favorite bites of the night! The jokbal platter was MASSIVE. It was cooked and seasoned to perfection. Needless to say, this is the place to go for good food and drinks with friends! We will be back!

Check out my foodsta @chiuventure for a closer look and more details of my dining experience here as well as other establishments in NYC and around the world!

Seoul Salon has a modern twist on classic Korean dishes, infusing them with fresh culinary twists.

The soy scallop with gim rice was fresh, light, and scallops were sweet and creamy in texture. The rose tteokbokki was very creamy and almost felt like a fusion between Italian flavors and Korean textures. The basil was herby, flavorful, and stracciatella cheese slightly acidic, creamy, and infused the dish with a lightness and break in richness of the rose sauce. The tteok texture was soft, but still al dente to create a great bite. Lastly the spicy octopus with risotto was another blend of Italian & Korean flair, introducing soft, creamy Arborio rice with the crunchy, spicy, and flavor-packed octopus.

Seoul salon’s menu is unique and curated to be filled with robust flavor & great textures.

My only callout is the space is narrow so it can be difficult to have a conversation as it feels like tables are cramped/on top of each other.

Seoul Salon, as described by them, is a Sool Jib inspired Korean restaurant with a modern take on Korean alcohol and Korean foods.

The vibe itself was nice, dim but not too loud, even with the edm/club music playing. The tables can feel a bit cramped, but it wasn't overbearing and we could talk even with all the background noise.

The food was phenomenal, well priced and well portioned for sharing. We got the octopus kimbap, soy scallop with gim rice, and the raw marinated crab noodles.

The Banchan was a ramen snack with ketchup, a good palate cleanser and tasty.

The octopus kimbap was good, we didn’t think it was outstanding but it did taste good. The octopus was a bit uneven in the dish though, as some of our pieces had no octopus while others had a lot.

The raw marinated crabs were a highlight, with a large portion of noodles accompanying it. As per their instruction, we mixed the raw crab meat into the noodles, which elevated the already tasty crab and noodles to make a spicy yet delicious noodle dish. The spice was a little on the spicier side, but nothing too spicy.

A highlight was the soy scallop with gim rice. It had a great taste to it, a great portion of scallop, and each part of the dish worked perfectly together.

The price is also really good for all the food we got, probably one of the highest quality meals we've gotten at the price we paid.

Every winter I waited for their special Yellowtail Platte, its very good deal with full plate of fresh cut yellowtail (which is absolutely delicious), side dishes, three different sources, salad and rice or porridge. The quality just amazing.

Other dishes at this place also very good, potato chips, mala pork sliders, and the special Myung Jak fruit wine, we were happy with everything we ordered.

Run and make the reservation now before the seasonal special dish gone.

This is a very nice Asian fusion Chinese restaurant with a great atmosphere, but you need to make reservations in advance. Overall, the flavors are very solid.

I highly recommend their Foie Gras Custard (Foie Gras Steamed Egg) — it was incredibly rich, and the addition of mushrooms enhanced the overall umami.

However, the Foie Gras on Toast set had a slight flaw: the toast was a bit over-charred, which slightly overpowered the dish, and the Eel component was hard to taste.

The Lamb Ribs were decent but nothing extraordinary. The strong barbecue glaze slightly masked the natural flavor of the meat, though the preparation was quite creative.

The Kung Pao Quail was tasty and innovative — so tender that you wouldn’t even guess it was quail.

The Black Cod Clay Pot with Rice was rather average, nothing remarkable.

Overall, this restaurant is quite innovative. The flavors and techniques are authentic while keeping the creative fusion style. I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a unique dining experience.

I went here with my friends, and everything this restaurant served deserves a standing ovation!
The food is amazingly good—every dish comes with beautiful presentation, and you can really tell they use high-quality ingredients. I loved everything; even their simple cucumber salad was incredible—spicy, fresh, nutty, and perfectly balanced.

I absolutely love this place! The ambience is great, and our server was very friendly and attentive. If you’re looking for a restaurant that serves food made with love, you must visit 53.

Shout-out to Chef Mark, Chef Adam, and the entire team for the amazing food. Highly recommended! ❤️

The food and environment were very nice tho overpriced imo. It’s not a quiet place so expect to talk loudly. Unfortunately the main negative was the spotty service. A restaurant like this needs to do better than with accommodating guest food restrictions by making the experience feel seamless. My partner is Celiac, so gluten is an absolute no. When booking, I made sure to add that to the dietary restrictions section. The lady at the front acknowledge that when we walked in. I would expect that at a restaurant like this, our waiter would also know by the time we get to the table, but he didn’t and we told him ourselves, no problem. He was kind enough to outline on the menu which items he thought were gluten-free, so we only ordered from his list. When the clay pot arrived with table side finish, I had a hunch and decided to triple check with the chef if the soy sauce was infact gluten free… it wasn’t… that is unacceptable considering the potential severity of reactions that Celiacs can have to gluten. The chef was kind enough to take the dish back and remake it with GF soy sauce. It was quite disappointing to see that not only the staff failed to communicate such details, but when specifically told, our waiter failed to communicate that to the kitchen.

I don’t think I expected too much considering that it’s a health concern and this is not a cheap restaurant. I would not expect this at a small casual spot. But a $$$$ restaurant needs to do much better on service to justify its prices on a bowl of rice with a small pice of fish.

Interesting restaurant with good food and friendly staff. I really liked the ground-floor interior — simple yet elegant.
The main dining area, however, is two levels down, so it feels like a basement with no windows or fresh air. While the design is tasteful, you do get the sense of sitting in a box.
The staff were genuinely helpful and warm, not robotic, which made the experience pleasant. The food was tasty and well-prepared.
Overall, it’s a nice place for a business dinner or a quiet evening meal.

Excellent experience at this restaurant. We went for dinner, feom the beggining we loved the ambience and look of the place. We ordered cucumber salad as a starter and followed ordering  4 more dishes, our server explained very well the menu options and her suggestions were perfect in taste and quantity. Everything was delicious, we ended our dinner with an exquisite dark chocolate desert accompanied by a famous monk coctail. Will return on future trips to NY to keep trying other menu options.

This place is fantastic! Every dish was thoughtfully designed and executed. The flavors were on point and I still dream of that ouji bowl. One of things I really liked about their tasting menu was each course came with option so my wife and I could try so many dishes instead of both of u as getting the same meal. Also, service and our server were very attentive and knowledgeable. Will def go back.

We celebrated our 11th wedding anniversary here and the experience was absolutely fantastic. We arrived a little earlier than our booked time, but our table was already ready and we were warmly accommodated, which set the tone for the evening.

The service was excellent throughout, and the food was outstanding — very tasty, beautifully presented, and genuinely artistic. We went with their 7-course holiday special, and every single course ranked highly, making it a memorable dining experience from start to finish.

A special mention for the thoughtful gesture at the end: we were surprised with house-made mini cupcakes, beautifully plated with a handwritten note celebrating our anniversary. That personal touch truly made the night extra special.

An unforgettable experience and a perfect place for celebrating meaningful occasions. Highly recommended.

Opted for a la carte bc I heard there’s some misses in the tasting. Everything we got was great. Lobster ramyun was simple but done well, but my fav dish was probably the sea bass and clams with truffle seafood broth; it was so rich and flavorful

Elevated Korean to its finest!
I can't even begin to tell you how amazing the food was. We had the most decadent food and only ate at the bar. The bartender gave us wonderful suggestions on what to order as well as attentive service. We can not wait to try the formal dining room or Bo.
The beet tartare on toast was delicate and delicious. The chili lobster ramyun had the most velvety flavors. The Oiji bowl with sea urchin was phenomenal. There was so much thought put into these bites and gorgeous presentation.
Highly recommend trying.

Really impressive food, a totally deserved michelin star. The seaweed rice bowl is filled with sea urchin and other seafood - my favorite out of the whole set. But overall the tasting menu is so well-balanced and provides a logical food journey. The dessert was a bit off for my taste - can't say I enjoyed the palate cleansing ice granita, but the sweet potato doughnut was very unique. Also amazing selection of teas (the persimmon one was really great). The service is up to michelin level standards and not snobby.

Great spot! My fiancé booked a reservation for 8282 for Valentine’s Day and it was very nice. We got the Valentine’s special menu as well as two regular menu items. My fiancé and I’s favorite was definitely the beef steak tartare as well as the cheesy tteok-bokki. The flavors were great and the service was excellent. Would definitely come back here to try their other tartares! (The white chocolate matcha pudding was also really good!)

Absolutely amazing experience at 8282. Every single dish we ordered was incredibly delicious — not one miss. The flavors were thoughtful, well-balanced, and memorable from start to finish.

This is the kind of place where you’re already planning your next visit before you even leave. Definitely coming back again. Highly recommend!

Absolutely amazing Korean food—every dish was on point and full of flavor.
The customer service was exceptional: attentive, friendly, and professional.
The vibe and mood are perfect—stylish, lively, and great for drinks as well.
Ideal spot for both dinner and a night out. Highly recommend.

This modern Korean spot in LES is truly a gem, and I absolutely loved it. The interior is cozy but tables are a bit small, so I recommend reservations if you are come with a group. Service was absolutely stellar—they were so kind to talk to, attentive, and patient.

We got their chestnut makgeoli to drink and for food we got their: grilled octopus, ebi ikura uni tartare, clam sujaebi, scallop jjajjang boribap, 8282 steak, and yuzu panna cotta. Everything was phenomenal. Their chestnut makgeoli was creamy and a delightful pair to the meal. Their grilled octopus was probably the favorite of the night as it was flavorful, amazing texture, and had great sauces. The ebi ikura uni tartare was also good and came with seaweed, but there was nothing super crazy/different about it (compared to other restaurants). I also loved the broth for the clam sujaebi but I felt like this leaned on the more modern side—the sujaebi was a bit different than traditionally, and the broth was also more seafood forward. The scallop jjajjangboribap was good but I wish the jjajjang sauce was a bit stronger/more saucey. And, the steak was amazing. The yuzu matcha panna cotta was the perfect way to wrap up the meal, and by the end of this I was stuffed. Absolutely loved this dinner and I highly recommend.

Overall- I loved this place. It’s also part of InKind. The tuna tar tar was one of those dishes where once you have it u almost want to eat a second. It’s a must.

Food - once we order the tuna tartare it was so good. We almost over a second however, the table next to us had the Uni tartare so he said we’ll take that and it didn’t impress me as much as the tuna I loved it still.

We also ordered the KFC chicken, which was good a little relied to heavily on sauce and we got the Wellington, which was pretty impressive. Lastly, we got the butter chicken, which was delicious with the rice however, the rice could be cooked. There was also a cold onion in it, but the dish wasn’t cold

Atmosphere – The place is full. It’s cute. Nothing too crazy or over the top. Dim it everything is back in a red light, which makes it really hard to take pictures of the food, but that’s OK. Please excuse my pictures.

I love this place but people next to us get the kimchi cheese rice with chicken and it looks so good. I wanna go back and get it and of course get the tar tower again.

I also learned what corn salt tea was here also delicious and apparently really good for you

My birthday luncheon! I was welcomed and promptly seated as a walk-in. I was fortunate to have Alexia as my server, knowledgeable, smiling face, prompt and attentive to my food tastes. She was very helpful with her suggestive dishes. Thoroughly enjoyed my first visit. Great ambiance and the restaurant is full of energy. Seemed like a smooth flow auto run place. I had a list of a few IG’s dishes that I realllllllllly wanted to try Chef Lilly’s specialties, but none were available- I guess seasonal. I had a mental palate to try’em all, but was disheartened…maybe another time. Kudos to the team for a very well run operation. 👏😋🫶‼️ Ty Alexia for friendly service.

Mexican restaurant on UWS on the Michelin guide, pretty self explanatory!

Saturday afternoon quite busy, lots of reservations and walk ins. Portions were generous and flavours top tier. The guac had a chilli oil on it that was immense and homemade tortillas.

Homemade lemonade was gorgeous! Sometimes they can be a little tart but this was perfectly sweet and lemony.

Birria quesadilla was a highlight, birria not too spicy which was great for me but my partner would’ve rathered more fire.
The chipotle shrimp taco was lovely and had the spice missing from the birria. Pork taco spot on.

Overall excellent meal!!

The service here is amazing. Our server at the bar gave great dish recommendations and everything was incredible. The cocktails are definitely worth coming for— I recommend the cilantro gimlet. We loved the pork belly carnitas tacos and Zarandeado.

I wandered around the Natural History Museum and happened to find this restaurant, which was rated Michelin 2025. The food was amazing. I ordered fish tacos and chilaquiles rojos, both very authentic, spicy, layered, and full of flavor. Sergio is also incredibly nice, and he introduced the restaurant’s signature dishes and even shared stories about his hometown. Now I really want to go to South America this year.

delivers! All of the food was outstanding. The guacamole ashes looked beautiful and was a little different. The quesadilla negra was exceptional. The sauce and the crema worked so well together, lots of texture. The barbaco tapatia was perfectly cooked, crispy outer layer, rich and tender beef. The tortillas were well made. I thought the rice and the beans could use more flavor. The service was fast.

Joo Ok — a new Korean restaurant that opened last year and has already earned two Michelin stars. The chef originally had the restaurant in Seoul and later decided to relocate it to New York.

The space is aesthetically beautiful, designed in calming earthy tones. The experience begins in what feels like a traditional garden before entering the restaurant, where guests are welcomed with fermented drinks.

The concept revolves around locally sourced and house-made fermented ingredients. The restaurant has its own farm in New York, while many ingredients are also brought directly from Korea.

The 12-course tasting menu was very well balanced, highlighting vegetables and seafood with one meat dish. The staff did a wonderful job explaining each course, which made the meal both delicious and educational as we learned about different Korean ingredients and traditions.

One of our favorite moments was the sochok roasted tea served with the assortment of desserts at the end of the tasting menu.

The ambience is calm and relaxing, with warm and attentive service throughout the evening. We’re already looking forward to coming back.

This was one of the most memorable meals I've had. All the staff were so smiley and welcoming. We each got a welcome drink and shimp snacks; small but packed with flavors. Then we were directed to our table which was prepared with an envelope with the menu inside. We were so excited and our expectations were through the roof!

The dishes did NOT disappoint! Oh my goodness their first course, the yellowtail, was so delicious! The combination of the Gochujang and buttery yellowtail really brought up our appetite. My personal favorite course was the lobster. The AROMA of this dish just made me salivate I secretly wanted to speed up with service so I could dive in! and it was so scrumptious indeed! The main dish, the steak, was actually a big surprise as well because the cookery of the meat was so good even though this place is not a steak house. One of our company is from Texas and he was very impressed.

I can talk about the food forever but what I have to mention was the service here. The staff were so warm, so welcoming, and very attentive to details. Every time someone left the table, the staff would come and refold our napkins. I also noticed that they would serve the food only when everyone was seated, and would clear the dishes when everyone finished. The pace of the courses was also great! 2+ hours went by so fast we thought it was just an hour. They also gave us a small bag with some memorabilia. It was such a wonderful meal for a celebration.

Highly highly recommended!

After your interesting 100 year old elevator ride to the 16th floor of this building right in the center of KTown, you emerge into a serene setting where you sit with a non-alcoholic welcome drink.

You are then guided to your table in the attractive main dining room with an elegant Korean home vibe. I had requested a window seat with a view of the Empire State building, and was kindly granted the requested seating. Unbalanced, I would say don’t bother with this since you are way too close to the Empire State building to actually see anything but its base.

Some of the captions that Google maps AI has added to my photos are weirdly inaccurate, but I’m not going to get down and correct each one. as an example, it added a caption calling tins of caviar “wine on ice”.

The service is crisp and professional with varying degrees of warmth. There were a couple of courses that were introduced by a woman wearing an N 95 mask and it was difficult to understand what she was saying.

We enjoyed a couple of the signature cocktails. The tasting menu was artfully, prepared and thoughtfully presented. Some of the dishes were more interesting and flavorful, some were a little bit bland, but we enjoyed all of them.

In particular, I thought the beef course was fantastic. The meat was cooked too perfection, juicy and flavorful, and a generous portion. Some of the flavors were fantastic and memorable, and there was a lot of cultural pride in the experience. Overall, I would say that we left feeling full, but not overly stuffed in an uncomfortable way. Having been too many Michelin starred restaurants around the world I would not dispute that this restaurant is worthy of two Michelin stars. On balance, I would say that it is perhaps a bit pricey for the experience, but it is definitely a suitable special occasion venue.

Really attentive & friendly service. Pacing of the meal was good, and in my opinion it’s a lot of food (despite the first few bites being small, it adds up quickly). I appreciate the attention to detail in the decor and in each course - everything was presented so beautifully. My favorites were the gochujang hoe, ganjang perilla oil egg dish, gui wagyu set, and the chestnut chocolate black sesame dessert! And all the byung gwa.

wowowow. 3.5 hours spent in food heaven.

words can barely express how unique and memorable Joo ok was over. the menu was meticulously designed and executed incorporating the freshest farm produce  representing Korea’s signature flavors. each course was incredibly well-paced—enough time to actually appreciate and savor. you can really tell there was an immense work invested in every ingredient to stimulating the palate (gradually going from sweet notes to savory)

highlights of the night included the welcome drinks in the lobby that foreshadowed an amazing evening to come as well as the mid-post card during the Pheasant course all the way to the beautiful dessert section to tie it all together.

p.s. sending a whole lot of love to the staff who provided us a special, intimate table to vlog. our corner table was perfect with a view  and made us feel like true royalty without bothering the other guests. thank you so much Joo Ok Team! cant wait to see your way to 3 stars!

the prix-fixe menu was such a good deal!! there 4 courses and you get very different flavor throughout each course, i so so enjoyed it.

i think the bibimbap with oysters at the end with the warm soup was a very filling, warm ending to the whole experience.

staffs were the cutest too!!

I visited Odre NYC with my family to celebrate my mother’s birthday, and it was one of those rare meals that stay with you long after the night ends. We had come for the summer menu a few months ago and were so impressed that we decided to return for this special occasion. What moved us the most was the thoughtful gesture at the end of the meal—Odre replaced the final course’s soup with miyeok-guk, the traditional Korean birthday seaweed soup. It was unexpected, deeply considerate, and genuinely touching.

What sets Odre apart is its ability to surprise even someone like me, who grew up with Korean cuisine. The menu is consistently fresh, inventive, and remarkably harmonious, offering combinations I would never think of, yet they come together flawlessly. Every course is plated with precision and beauty, but beyond aesthetics, the flavors and textures are balanced at a level that’s rare to find.

The seasonal sotbap bibimbap and broth course—which changes throughout the year—remains one of my favorite endings to any tasting menu in New York. The care put into the rice, the depth of flavor, and the comforting warmth of the soup always feel like the perfect conclusion. On this visit, it became even more meaningful with the birthday miyeok-guk.

Desserts such as the sweet potato cheesecake and persimmon shaved ice were equally thoughtful and beautifully executed. Every dish felt intentional, refined, and full of quiet confidence.

It’s honestly hard to believe Odre hasn’t received a Michelin star yet, given the consistency, creativity, and heart in every part of the experience. This restaurant continues to be one of the most memorable and inspiring places to dine in New York.

Dining at ODRE was one of those experiences that stays with you long after you leave the table. From the first bite to the last, it genuinely felt like I was experiencing Korean cuisine in a way that was both deeply familiar and completely new at the same time.

The dishes were undeniably Korean at heart, but each one carried a sense of creativity and refinement that made them feel truly special — not something you can easily find elsewhere. This felt like ODRE’s story of Korean food, not a copy of tradition, but a thoughtful and respectful evolution of it 🌿

What impressed me most was how delicate and precise every flavor was. The seasoning across all dishes was incredibly balanced — nothing too salty, nothing too heavy. Everything tasted clean, fresh, and intentional, making the entire meal feel surprisingly light and comfortable. I never felt overwhelmed, only curious and excited for the next dish ✨

The namul dishes especially stood out. Their flavors were unmistakably Korean — earthy, subtle, and familiar — yet presented in a way that felt elevated and modern. It brought a quiet sense of nostalgia while still feeling fresh and refined, which honestly isn’t easy to pull off.

The white wine pairing was another highlight 🍷 The brightness and acidity of the wine complemented the dishes beautifully, enhancing the freshness of the ingredients and the subtle seasoning rather than overpowering them. It felt like the food and wine were in constant conversation with each other.

Beyond the food, the atmosphere of the restaurant added so much to the experience. The space feels calm, intimate, and thoughtfully designed, allowing you to slow down and truly focus on what’s in front of you. It’s the kind of place where you naturally end up lingering a little longer, savoring each moment.

Overall, ODRE offers more than just a great meal — it offers a unique, one-of-a-kind experience of Korean cuisine in New York. Refined but warm, innovative but respectful, and above all, deeply satisfying. A place I’d happily return to, and one I’d recommend without hesitation 🤍

My husband and I came here for the first time to try their winter pre-fix menu. (it was worth it). I'm so glad we came because the food was delicious and was just on another level compared to what you get to try at normal restaurants. The presentation was beautiful, and the food tasted just as good as it looked! The staff was all super nice and friendly as well, and everything was prepared pretty timely. They really go out of their way to make you feel special and welcome. We HIGHLY recommend the Abalone Mandoo, Citrus Shrimp Naengchae, the Jokpyun, and the Jujube Tea!

This was a 7/10 meal. We tried the Jokpyun, the Citrus Red Shrimp Naengchae as a starter, and honestly both kind of fell flat in favour. For the second  course, the guksu was rich but quite one dimensional in taste. Special mention to the Kimchi Tart, which was quite delightful and special and was honestly one of my favourite dishes of the night. The bibimbap and tteokgalbi were alright, and the fish dish was just okay. The sweet potato cheesecake hit hard though.

Very large restaurant with a really nice decor. Famous dishes are focaccia bread, the gem salad, pasta with amatriciana sauce, and tiramisu. I had all of them, and can say that the rumors are true. Focaccia is very soft, gem salad has the perfect cold and crispy texture, amatriciana tastes great, and tiramisu is memorable. We also had the duck leg parcelles. The tastes were good and well mixed. Also, they carry good wine that pairs well with food. I liked the cream of the tiramisu the most. Also, they make a good effort to make your special day memorable. Suggestion: they should add a sweet bite to the bag they give you when you are leaving the restaurant on your special they - some others restaurants do it so it makes this kind of expected.

Absolutely a must try. Food was delicious served at perfect temperature. Great atmosphere the Waitress was were extremely knowledgeable about the Menu. Tender chicken with a slight light skin that tasted like fried chicken. Salad were robust and flavors combined perfectly. Just go!! Well worth the money!!!

FABULOUS OUTSTANDING food
I am vegetarian pescatarian and very picky. I ordered the cauliflower antipasto and a couple of vegetable cotorni. All spectacular. My mom and my daughter said their pasta was absolutely delicious. The interior is so nicely done.
Great service lovely waitstaff. Thaddeus was our server, very charming and friendly as were many others there whose names I did not get. It was a perfect evening. They didn’t rush us at all. So appreciated.
Highly recommend.
And quiet!!! You can converse!!

Came to Sempre Oggi for a drink at the bar prior to going for a show at Beacon Theatre.. although the restaurant was quite full we were able to get seats at the bar rather quickly. Very friendly service and our mixologist. Kevin gave us a tasting of their house special martini and I wound up getting two more.. great service.. really pretty restaurant.. very clean bathrooms. We didn’t get a chance to eat, but we’ll definitely be back to try. The food smelled and looked delicious.

What a winner.  In every category. Was my first time here, and I was blown away.  Service, atmosphere & food were top notch.  We had the rib steak for two.  Sublime!  Strattciatelli & beets, omg!
Our waiter, Thaddeus was pleasant, fun & on top of everything.

We recently visited Bungalow to celebrate our anniversary, and overall it was a lovely experience.

The ambiance is beautiful and perfect for a special occasion. We really enjoyed the vibe of the place—it feels elegant but still warm and welcoming.

For drinks, we tried the Guava Lemonade and a Falsa mocktail (I don’t remember the exact name), and both were refreshing and delicious.

For appetizers, we ordered the Dahi Kebab and Achari Stuffed Panner. Dahi Kebab was absolutely amazing—definitely one of our favorite dishes of the evening.

For the main course, we had the Okra dish and Old Delhi Chole. We really liked the okra—it was flavorful and well prepared. However, the chole was just okay and didn’t stand out as much as we expected.

For dessert, we tried the Rose Kulfi. If you are a big fan of rose flavor, you’ll probably enjoy it. For us, it was good for a one-time try.

One small detail that made the experience special was the little candy in a red packet at the end. It instantly reminded me of my childhood, which was such a sweet nostalgic touch.

Overall, it’s good to visit Bungalow at least once for the experience.

Today we celebrated my son and wife’s birthdays together at Bungalow. It was an amazing dinner  here. Truly a multi sensory experience! We’ve been following Chef Vikas Khanna on social media and it would have been amazing to meet him, but he’s in India right now to promote the latest season of Master Chef.

We ordered Yogurt Kebab, Anarkali Chicken, Chicken Amritsari, Spice Roasted Pineapple, and Rose Kulfi Falooda. The yogurt kebab was absolutely delicious and highly recommend this unique dish. Both the chicken dishes were really good and all the sauces were tasty with a modern twist. The five cheese kulcha stuffed with Amul cheese reminds you of your childhood for those who grew up in India. Rose Kulfi Falooda was wonderful and it has all the classic falooda flavors and looks nothing like it.

The atmosphere, service, fantastic desi music, and hospitality is unmatched from the moment you walk in. We had an absolutely fantastic experience at the Bungalow!

Bungalow is an experience. The moment you enter, the decor mesmerizes you. Sweet treats are kept for you to gorge on while you wait to be seated. You can grab a cocktail from the bar while you wait. The paan flavored old fashioned was the highlight drink of the night. To start with, the dahi kebabis a must!! That's the best food on the menu. All the other stuff we ordered were also very good but didn't stand out from a slightly lesser priced Indian restaurant. The service is amazing, the atmosphere amazing and overall an excellent experience. We didn'teet Vikas Khanna as he was out for a food show filming and hence missed the best part of the Bungalow experience.

Let me start by giving you important details:

1) Food - Overall 8/10
2) Ambience - 8/10 for us. If you like quiet tables where you can chat, this isn't the place. The restaurant is full for dinner (when we went), and tables fill up quickly.
3) Service - 10/10. Truly a "Atithi devo bhava" vibe. They are vigilant and very good in terms of service.

Vegetarian food - I liked the pineapple curry and dahi ke kebabs the most. We ordered the okra dish and the sweet potato chaat too, but I did not feel "omg this is different". On the other hand, the pineapple dish was fantastic! The mixture of spice, sweetness, and coconutty flavors was worth it. The dahi ke kebabs are famous! If you've seen Chef's Instagram videos, this is his personal favorite on the menu, and for good reason. The yogurt is very well balanced with the dip.

We did not try the lamb as we don't eat mutton, but the chicken and prawns were good. The dal was good too, but in my opinion, not the star dish of the night.

You can take a look at the photos for the dishes, but I would say definitely say it's worth a visit.

Here’s an unbiased review from someone who admires and respects Vikas Khanna as a chef.

Atmosphere, the vibes, the service, hospitality is unmatched from the moment you walk in. Absolutely amazing and kind service people at Bungalow including the humble chef. We celebrated the birthday and it was an amazing experience to enjoy a meal at this place.

We ordered Banarasi puri, yogurt kebab, achari paneer, paan sour, kali peeli taxi, paneer lazeez, roti, mint laccha paratha, chocolate lava cake dessert with chef’s complimentary dessert for the birthday person.

Yogurt kebab was absolutely delicious and worth it. Puri was 8.2/10 because the lack of water and too dry for my taste, great taste though. Achari paneer was okay, cooked well but sauce wasn’t my favourite. Just know all the sauces and gravy on all plates are well done and great infusion of spices and modern twist to it. Paneer lazeez was great, would love more gravy than paneer to balance out the curry aspect of it. No complaints with breads, it’s awesome. Dessert was wonderful and would order it again as the sweetness and cake balance is perfect and not overpowering with chocolate or gulab Jamun flavour.

Overall please go with open mind and take it all in. It’s an absolute treat to sit there and enjoy their service and dishes. Would recommend this place, 9.2/10.

Best Indian food I’ve had in Manhattan, and it’s not even close! Fragrant, satisfying, expansive menu, huge portions with GREAT PRICES and friendly/FAST service. I ordered an aromatic egg biryani, a garlic naan with that perfect crispy-to-doughy ratio, and lamb tikka masala with more depth than your typical. No charge for side of refreshing raita and plain rice. Could not recommend more for takeout or a quick dine-in; they also have a newer and bigger space in Kips Bay. Warning that they don’t serve alcohol. Will be ordering again and again!

The food here is just amazing...You will remember the Biryani here once you try it. We visited from Houston and can safely say its one of the Best Biryanis we had In a long time. Pls open one in Houston !!
Food is served piping hot and fresh...Naan and curries were delicious too...overall very satisfied !!

(June 6, 2025)
We went here as a group of about 10 people for a friend's treat.
I was excited that this restaurant advertised itself to serve Hyderabadi cuisine, and a lot of the items on the menu were indeed what I used to uniquely see in restaurants in Hyderabad, India.

I tried the following.

1. Kubani ka meetha -- sweet jam, nice sourness. Mild spices. Delicious.
2. Double ka meetha -- warm, milky and not buttery, satisfying bread and cashew nuts. Semolina on top is a distraction.
3. Baigan bagaara --- While the name of the dish is in Hindi, it felt closer to the Telugu/Andhra dish that I know as Ennai kathirikkai (எண்ணெய் கத்திரிக்காய்), and it was very close in taste to what is served in Indian Institute of Science (A Mess).
4. Nizami paneer -- mild, thick, and yummy.
5. Dahi kebab -- soft in the mouth to the extent that it was tongue-biteable.

The roti and rice items were normal. I wish I also tried the Irani chai, but I was too full to order one by myself, at the end.

They gave rice with every gravy we ordered, sadly we couldn't even get to some of the several bowls of rice. The waiter was kind enough to request us to take it home parceled, but we were guilty of refusing.

Came here a bit before closing on a Saturday night last week. The Goat Dum Biryani was great! The goat was tender and flavorful, the rice was aromatic and dynamic, and the raita complemented the flavors really nicely. The portion was also huge, maybe it's meant to be shared but I ate it all up myself 🤤. I also got the Chaat Samosa with the tamarind sauce which I really liked too. The pastry was crispy and soaked in flavorful sauce 😋. I would totally recommend this place.

The food is good, had a Chicken 65 Biryani. Surprisingly, the rice offered was less but it had more of Chicken pieces, which was unusual for a Biryani. I suggest them to check the serving size.

Overall, I recommend tourists from Asia to try out their cuisine

We came here to celebrate a friend’s birthday on a Saturday evening and all of us chose the prix fixe menu(they were able to accommodate for a vegetarian version which was a plus!). The meal started off strong — the first three appetizers were served together, and each was beautifully presented. The tomato salad with matcha sauce was probably my favorite, such a simple dish yet it had so many layers of flavor! The pie was amazing, and the dumplings were perfectly al dente.

Unfortunately, the main course was where things started to dip. It felt quite plain and underwhelming compared to the earlier dishes, and the dessert didn’t really stand out either.

The staff were nice and friendly, but perhaps because it was a busy Saturday night, they kept forgetting our drinks. We had to remind them several times. The service felt a bit disorganized, which was surprising for a Michelin-starred restaurant.

Overall, we still had a great time, and the food especially the appetizers were memorable!

one of the best meals I’ve had in NYC! from the oysters, to their everything brioche, and XLB agnolotti - I love how creative every dish was and everything was pulled off with amazing attention to detail

my friend and I also thought the cocktails really packed a punch

and also appreciated how nice and attentive the servers were

The first course; oysters, potatoes, and Hamachi crudo; was unbelievable! Truly a flavor explosion. The Summer Zucchini had the perfect amount of heat and was delicious, and the Everything Brioche was solid. I could’ve skipped the Agnolotti XLB and the brisket, though.

Dessert was very good, especially the matcha gelato, which was out of this world.

It was an odd night overall, when we arrived, only two tables were taken, and by 9 p.m. we were the only ones left. My guess is that the tasting menu price doesn’t quite match the experience, especially given how inconsistent the dishes were.

Wow! What an incredible experience. We did tasting menu which was perfect for dinner. The food was delicious , and spaced apart evenly. The service was knowledgeable &friendly without being overbearing. Ambience was minimalist and clean.

I liked every dish except first one- cucumbers. Other dishes tested really good, especially pasta with black truffles and lobster tail. Drinks were strong and not too sour. Also I liked dessert, but, from my perspective, dishes were really small and I ( small young lady 118 pounds) left restaurant not full. Otherwise, I had wonderful dinner there and tried new, delicious dishes

What a hidden gem! Sami & Susu is charming, intimate, rustic place where one wants to come back again and again. You feel welcomed from the moment you step inside. Dim lighting ambiance is perfect for a romantic dinner or friends get-together. Lets talk about THE FOOD. Freshest ingredients, creative menu and unique flavors! Every dish was delicious and memorable. The dips (seemingly a common staple of many Mediterranean restaurants) were so tasty and flavorful! Tuna crudo with brown butter -  must try. Sweetbread, beef cheeks, risotto - every dish was "This-is-my-favorite"😃 Chicken with tzatziki- juicy, tender, succulent, and perfectly seasoned with spices. Well curated wine list made the evening even more unforgettable. Cannot wait to be back to try other dishes. Oh, do yourself a favor don't skip the chocolate dessert:)

LOVED the whole branzino with leeks (the leeks are super), the risotto and sweetbread skewers - these are recommended by the waiter and they do not miss!
we enjoyed how wholesome and cozy this spot is! the service is amazing as well! please make a reservation or walk in early!

Awesome restaurant! A great place for a date night. The venue is very little but the size allows for a more personal feel to the service. The food was delicate but full of flavor. We had gotten the Muhammara and the Hanger Steak. Both were amazing! We will definitely be coming back again!

We had the sunchoke bureka, rissoto, and tuna and they were all incredible especially the bureka.  They had a good combination of vegeterian and non-veggie options.  They are on inkind.  They also offered to move us to a better table when one become available.

I had not eaten all day at a work event & this was the PERFECT, filling meal for me. Definitely need a reservation btw, this place is quite small but cozy!

Although, I would say it’s Mediterranean inspired, but not necessarily Med food/wine.

The orange wine was a great recommendation by my server.

Pita was fresh and tasty, but too hot to the touch when it arrived at my table. I had to let it cool down a bit. It went great with the labneh which was fantastic! I do wish they had hummus on the menu though.

Hanger steak with the beans was very flavorful and went great with the bed of beans (I’m glad they swapped the corn as I’m not a corn person).

Meyer lemon panna cotta for dessert was sour as expected, with shavings of green apple.

I would return for sure!

Five stars all around. Chef Sergio is one of the best: creative, humble, and warm. My husband and I love sitting at the chef’s counter and seeing the food come together. The atmosphere of the restaurant is modern and sleek but still welcoming. The cocktails are creative and well-made, although the wine selection is even better, and their wines pair excellently with the food. Their ceviches are always good and well-balanced in flavor. Some of my favorite dishes are: the blue crab rolls; the hake chowder; bok choy salad; mussels; eel pizza; skate cheeks; udon noodles; and the miso black cod. Everything here is delicious, and you really can’t go wrong with anything on the menu.

The food was good but nothing else just good, the service was slow. We went for Valentine's Day, and it was not very busy, we arrived late for our reservation, but we were seated right away. Ordered the Wagyu Maki Rolls which was good but again nothing special. Drinks were 2 Chicha Morada which was not good seemed like poured from a bottle and way too much ice I think it was a block of ice. I added a Papa Sour again nothing special it was very sour with very little Pisco. Wife ordered the Pork Ribs which were good and tasty I ordered Wagyu Tri-tip, Yuzu Bearnaise both were very small portions.
Funny thing our neighbors ordered the EEL Pizza and boy did they regret it the smell was strong and their faces said a lot.

We went ahead and ordered dessert which saved the dinner we both shared Lucama Soft Serve and other ice cream can't find the name. Both Ice Creams were good and we left happy, but we will more likely not return.

Weird that this place isnt packed every night.  The location has probably something to do with it, but still considering how good it was.  IMO this is the best one yet from the Llama Group.  While some may not agree with the authenticity of the Nikkei offerings, the flavors were def there.  I tried all the top mentions and the sleeper hit is actually the Mussels.  Some of the best I had in years if not decades.  Def get the Udon as well, and the pizza.  A good choice right now especially to pair with the holiday lights in Hudson Yards.

TLDR: Papa San is the next chapter of the same team that brought us Llama San, etc. Very flavorful but pricey and smaller portions - good for that corporate expense card. Cacio e pepe udon, burger sando.

I was always a fan of Llama San so when I heard of Papa San coming - I was excited. The space is right at the corner of 34th and 10th and it's cool to have a nikkei (Japanese/Peruvian) option available.

The dishes are well thought out and overall tasty but portions are on the smaller side. It also gets pricey quick.

On a most recent visit, the spicy tuna gunkan maki. Basically it's a spicy tuna crispy rice wrapped in nori - solid. The burger sando I think is a must order. It's served on fluffy milk bread that's toasted, the patty itself reminds me of a Dominican chimi. Definitely add-on the fries, I'm not sure what the seasoning is but it's good. For some reason it reminded me of Dorito's ranch seasoning.

Cacio e pepe udon. Mind you this is a modern iteration, so it's not as aggressively punchy or thick as a classic pasta. The udon I'd have preferred a bit more chew but the flavors were good. We added on the squid which is marinated in this spicy sauce - kind of similar to a Korean squid stir-fry. I'd add that in and mix as you go to change the flavor.

Eel pizza, typically this is good. It's very thin and has bonito shavings, the eel, pecorino and chives. It was a bit too heavy on the sauce last time but I'd still order it again.

I'm curious to try the dinner menu one day. Also if you go for lunch, probably one of the greatest potato salads I've had.

This Peruvian-Japanese fusion is such a vibe. I like  it better than the sister (more famous restaurant)  Llama Sun

Love the wonderfully casual but also upscale vibe creating the perfect atmosphere for a fun date night or a lively group dinner.

Service: The service is attentive and genuinely friendly. Some of our dishes came slow, but the server constantly checking on us and giving update.

Food:  full of playful, surprising dishes. Dishes stand out the most are eel pizza. Wagyu robataya and the mussel

Drinks: fun cocktail also with fusion twist.

Papa sun is the kind of place you walk out of already planning your next visit. Highly recommend for anyone looking for exciting flavors in a stunning, upbeat setting.

I really enjoyed dining here. Everything was delicious, and from our seats at the counter, it was so interesting to watch the chefs prepare each dish. It's a 3 course prix fixe menu, but you get several side dishes which are all great. I particularly liked the Japanese sweet potato which was roasted with pineapple juice. I loved the cobia, especially as it evoked memories of when I ate kingfish in Trinidad. Best of all, the staff are all so warm and friendly, reflecting the spirit of the Caribbean.

I went here the other night to celebrate my wife's new job. I stayed up until midnight two weeks before the reservations were available so I could get my pick on Open Table (this was a new experience for me). What can I say about this place that everyone isn't already saying? The space was cool. The service was impeccable. The drinks were creative and spirit forward. The food was plated beautifully and packed with flavor. If I have one complaint, it is the price for the experience. The price is justified because of the high level of service and food quality. It just means I can't go here once a week to eat this delicious, delicious food. Maybe Paul Carmichael will eventually open an a la carte restaurant that uses slightly less luxe ingredients, so then I can bear witness to his genius as often as I please.

Kabawa deserves all the flowers it has been getting from the NY Times and James Beard foundation. It’s inventive but most importantly it’s delicious. Standouts include the iconic goat curry which will be hard to remove from the menu because it’s so delicious. Everything was so good but what sets this restaurant apart is the warm, personable hospitality. We were able to talk to Chef Carmichael and what a kind, funny and incredibly warm human being. His ethos is infused into every part of the restaurant. At the bottom of the menu he puts the phrase. “Love yuh self.”

You will feel the love after dining at Kabawa.

I visited Kabawa on a recent trip to New York. The open kitchen at the bar makes fantastic viewing as you get to see all the prep. The atmosphere is modern, but also warm and upbeat, including the adjoining bar.  The food itself was one of the best meals I have ever eaten. Great balancing of the main (goat) and accompanying sides. Could not recommend enough. I had 1 Plantain/cod/caviar, 2 Goat, 3 Sorbet. Really liked the Tamarind palate cleanser too.
Unique cuisine that is totally worth it. You won’t leave hungry! The coconut turnover is a must along with the goat with curry sauce. Highly attentive staff with a great wine list.

It is very good french food. That being said it's nothing beyond that which i feel like i should mention given the hype around Chez Fifi.
The interior really is so beautiful a total escape from manhattan, it is reason to go. The food was good, salad was good, tartare was not near the best ive had but good, basque crab was very good, not heavy at all actually quite invigorating, steak frites were good and chicken i found to be not as moist as i would've expected from a place like this. It helped to get the foie gras.

My fav dish from the night is the fromage blanc ice cream. I ordered a second one.

The somm was probably doing her best to guide us to what i requested : a unique, flavourful, maybe bready sort of sweet, easy to drink champagne. I felt i was led astray. We ordered a 500 dollar bottle of 2012 Les Mont Fournois Montagne, and we weren't even able to finish it. Not delicious.
Its rare that i go to dinner and have a high budget for a bottle, so on this occasion with Chez Fifi's reputation of having an insane wine list i was very excited to splurge, and for this to be what i end up with is so disappointing. I get 2012 is a good year for champagne, does that automatically make it superb? I don't know. I wish the somm led me correctly with the budget i was working with (sub 500)

If you are a foodie and have been wanting to come, do not set expectations very high. This place really is for looking good, showing off a bit, feeling luxe, and escaping manhattan, all great reasons to go. The food is not worth the visit, nor was the wine in my experience.

So hard to get a reservation but so worth it. Our servers were amazing! Great wine selection. We LOVED the Basque deviled crab, roast chicken with foie gras, and the Filet mignon au poivre, and of course Pommes Fifi. All delicious, and reasonably priced. Our Chocolate mousse for dessert was a perfect ending. Really hope I can get another reservation to come back again!!

Amazing! Probably the nicest new restaurant and one of the only few that will bring us downtown folk uptown. Everyone who works here is so friendly and attentive, service amazing, food was amazing. The foie gras, tuna tartar, steak and chicken are superb. Even the basic green salad had an amazing dressing. Cocktails were also fantastic. Beautiful decor. 10 out of 10

If you’re looking for a dining experience that hits all the high notes: flavor, atmosphere, service, look no further than Chez Fifi. From the moment you walk in, you feel transported: the townhouse setting, the elegance of the wood-panelled dining room, and the buzz

Let’s talk the Steak Frites: it’s a master class in simplicity done right. The steak arrives with that perfect crust, the juices still singing, paired with golden, crisp-on-the-outside, fluffy-on-the-inside fries that you want to keep dunking again and again.
The martinis are no afterthought, they make a cocktail crafted with intention. Clean gin, the right amount of brine, a blue cheese olive (or three) that carries its own swagger.
The service here is the kind you don’t always find—but absolutely want when you want to feel remembered and well-taken-care-of. On that note: a heartfelt shout-out to Markyia, the sommelier whose professionalism, graciousness and genuine helpfulness elevated the evening further. Whether you needed a wine pairing, a suggestion or just someone who knew the menu inside-out and made you feel seen, Markia delivered. It’s clear that the team believes service is part of the craft.

The atmosphere blends the formality of a classic French bistro with the ease of a modern New York dining room. You come dressed, you come excited, you come ready to savour and you leave fully satisfied.

This restaurant was fine overall, but the experience had some notable misses. We arrived right at opening and were the second party in the restaurant, yet still waited about an hour to be seated.

The staff was consistently kind, professional, and respectful. Service itself was attentive, and small details stood out—for example, my napkin was neatly refolded after I used the restroom, which felt thoughtful and polished.

The food was mixed. The fries were soggy, and we weren’t asked for a preferred doneness on the filet mignon, which came out medium instead of medium rare. The beef stew had very tender meat but was overly dominated by Worcestershire sauce. On the positive side, the tuna tartare was excellent—creamy, fresh, and truly melt-in-your-mouth. The salmon with chips leaned oddly tuna-forward in flavor, though it was still enjoyable.

We also ordered takeout and accidentally left without it. No one stopped us, so we had to return to retrieve the order, which was disappointing given the otherwise attentive service.

The space itself is well done. The chairs were comfortable, the silverware felt high quality, and the layout was appealing. The upstairs area is noticeably quieter than downstairs, and the restroom was clean and classy.

We came primarily to use the $150 Sapphire Reserve credit. Without that incentive, we likely wouldn’t return, even though parts of the meal were solid. Overall, an okay experience with some highlights, but not one that stands out enough to revisit.

Great experience! The space felt cozy but spacious. Service was very attentive. Compared with other omakase places at similar price point, you get lots of course. All the appetizer/amuse dishes were delicious, especially the fired unagi and the Japanese amberjack sashimi. Super fresh fish and seafood and you get a great variety, and uni from Hokkaido was sweet and creamy. Ikumi also has two seaweed pieces which I don’t see commonly in other places, and both were very flavorful, and my guess is that these are their way to replace the more commonly-seen hand roll. Chef doesn’t talk too much but is very friendly :) Would love to see Ikumi receive a star soon.

In the age of accelerated inflation, $220pp for quality omakase in NYC w/ thoughtful ingredient selection & top-notch balance between shari and neta is hard to come by. Excellent bang for the buck and would highly recommend.

Been here three times and honestly this is one of the best omakase in the city. Every dish is art and seafood quality is top notch. Service is wonderful, too.

There’s too many omakase doing those “wagyu+uni” or “salmon + turuffle” those kinds of things. I love how Sushi Ikumi only focus on bringing out the best flavor of the fish, and not over complicating it.

Highly recommend.

I had a chance to eat here this weekend and Chef Jeong delivered just an amazing line up of 19 beautiful and delicious courses. He started off strong with an egg custard with sweet corn. We’re at the summer peak of corn season and it just captured the essence so well while wetting the appetite for what was to come. From there we moved on to the fish and nigiri courses and they were just so good. The chefs keeps to a traditional style which I very much prefer - just enough to elevate the fish without too many elements getting in the way. The quality of fish was excellent for the price point - some of the plumpest and delicious shrimp I’ve had, an incredible sea perch, and two cuts of tuna from Montauk among my favorites. One of the new dishes for me were cockles which were served live and tasted fresh out of the ocean. No wagyu on the menu here but I think it’s been overdone at omakase restaurants and again, the fish was divine. The atmosphere was perfect for the experience - intimate with just a small simple counter and the chef working his magic. I will return.

TLDR: Sushi Ikumi should be in your rotation of sushi bars if it isn't already. Reasonably priced, quality omakase, more traditional style. If you're into more edo-mae omakase, you will love Sushi Ikumi.

I'm not quite sure how I haven't written a review about this place. The first time I tried Sushi Ikumi, I couldn't quite figure out why but I wanted to come back. This was in the prime of COVID so I never got to see Chef Jongin's face until quite some time later. Since then, we've been revisiting regularly around every month or so. Sushi Ikumi is a sister restaurant of Hirohisa, so you know they've got great pedigree.

What stands out to me is how relaxed the restaurant is and how unpretentious it is. I've come here in a suit for business lunches and also in workout shorts and a t-shirt. You come here to enjoy quality omakase, amongst other likeminded individuals.

The shari or sushi rice is top notch. It has that nice depth of umami, some sourness, some saltiness, that perfect al dente texture. No matter how many times I've visited, it seems to get better and chef always finds a way to put something new in the mix. Although we can all enjoy the cheap omakases, ballin' on a budget gets boring. That same progression of wet truffles, lackluster caviar and some random sauce on top of the neta (topping) that's too acidic or too sweet - it just gets repetitive. I've had too many lean tuna cuts with that soggy truffle slice with some chives and mid caviar.

There's of course, the signature items. The saba miniature temaki, the nodoguro which is seared just enough to impart that smoky flavor without rendering too much fat. A squeeze of lemon citrus helps make sure that it's a balanced bite. The flesh of the fish is still cool-ish but the outside is just lukewarm. It's not dripping of fish fat with the pillow of sushi rice disintegrating as you rush into your mouth. That final bite of futomaki before you get the house-made ice cream. Yes, I've eaten here way too many times.

Our favorite sushi place and maybe restaurant in NY 🤔. We had high expectations and they were delivered. The service was good, they had good recommendations except that they told us not to repeat and now we want to go again to eat their tuna hand roll. Our ranking was: 1. Tuna hand roll 2. Bagel on Hudson 3. Ceviche 4. Miso Carrot Cake 5. Fish slider 6. Nigiri’s 7. Spicy tuna toll 8. Coconut ice cream 9.Salmon avocado rolls

Took my out-of-town parents here so they could experience fine dining. They had an amazing time—excellent food, phenomenal service and a cozy but not cramped space. Our server was one the most knowledgeable I’ve ever had. She even had anecdotes about the local farmers who sourced one of the ingredients. And don’t skip dessert!

We were not rushed at all, which I find to be rare in New York. I highly recommend this place!

It's no secret that Rosella is an East Village standout, but it's taken me a while to visit finally. I met a friend for an obscenely early dinner, but we were glad for it. There were still plenty of people in the dining room, but the staff were super attentive.

Most of the seating is counter seating, either in the window, at the bar, or in the back over the sushi chef. There doesn't seem to be a bad seat in the house. There is a happy hour menu, which we ordered a couple of things from, but we were primarily focused on the fish.

To get a feel for the menu, we ordered several things. The tuna with pesto and watermelon was terrific, a must-try. My friend said he never seeks out pesto, but this was something special. Next up were two spicy tuna handrolls, which were as promised, spicy and with a nice crunch added for texture.

Next up came the sushi, and while my friends were a little delayed by the kitchen, our server was quick to offer us their cucumber salad with yogurt and microgreens to keep us munching. All were delicious and consumed quickly.

In terms of beverages, we didn't stray from sake, which was offered on the happy hour menu, but there were many options, including a house-made orange wine from LI.

All in, this is a great place to meet a friend, and have a quick bite or sit and chat while you graze the menu. Either way, you will not be disappointed by anything; it's a lovely spot.

What a special dining experience! Don’t be fooled by the small and unassuming format, this place is special. Unique flavors in the best way every time that are different in a good way not just for the sake of being different. Speaking of sake, some of the best sake pairings I’ve ever had! Plus it’s just oozing with an air of cool hospitality that is so rare.

Every dish was incredible I truly can’t pick a favorite. Nothing is “too weird”, it all works way better than you’re expecting so just go for it.

We had the absolute best time! Sean (who doubled as our waiter and chef) was engaging, friendly, and informative. He described every dish perfectly and gave us delicious recommendations. It was some of my favorite food in nyc!

Had our anniversary dinner here. We chose the 5 course dinner and it was great. Food was delicious and service was amazing.
If you have a small appetite like my wife, 5 course might be a lot. She was full by dessert. All of the dishes were amazing.
The server was great and provided good recommendations and later gave us a quick tour of the kitchen.

Fantastic service and overall meal for an upscale lunch. The staff was attentive and kind. The courses were a bit hit or miss for this level of Michelin star for me but overall a wonderful experience. The main courses of lamb and buffalo were stellar. I HIGHLY recommend the wine pairing. That was the highlight for us. It was fantastic wine and brought the food to the next level. Overall a lovely experience. I'll mention most men were wearing jackets even at lunch time though it is not required.

This was my second time dining at DANIEL, and once again it reminded me why this restaurant is so special and why I return every time I’m in New York City.

From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with genuine warmth and gracious hospitality. The host and the manager who seated us were welcoming, attentive, and made us feel truly cared for. Throughout the evening, the service was impeccable ,polished yet friendly, professional without ever feeling distant.

The sommelier was exceptional, offering thoughtful wine recommendations that paired beautifully with each course. The tasting menu was a true work of art: beautifully crafted dishes, elegant plating, balanced flavors, and pairings that elevated the entire experience. Every course felt intentional and refined, yet comforting at the same time.

One of the highlights of the evening was having the pleasure of meeting Daniel Boulud himself. Despite being incredibly busy and on his feet all evening, his passion for cooking and hospitality truly shines through. He took the time to stop, chat with guests, and make everyone feel welcome and happy  a rare and meaningful gesture from a world-renowned chef.

DANIEL is not just about extraordinary food; it’s about heart, warmth, and genuine hospitality. An unforgettable experience, every single time.

I recently visited Daniel in New York City and experienced their tasting menu, and the entire evening was truly exceptional. From the moment I arrived, the service was warm, welcoming, and incredibly professional. The staff guided each course with genuine knowledge and attention, making the meal feel effortless and perfectly paced.

The tasting menu itself was a remarkable journey. Every dish was beautifully presented with meticulous detail, showcasing refined technique and bold yet balanced flavors. Each course felt intentional—textures, colors, and tastes coming together in a way that showed the kitchen’s skill and creativity. The ingredients were clearly top-quality, and the transitions between courses were thoughtful and harmonious.

The wine pairings elevated the experience even further, complementing each dish without overwhelming it. The ambiance of the dining room added to the enjoyment—elegant, serene, and polished without feeling stiff or overly formal. It created an atmosphere where you could relax and truly savor every moment.

Overall, my experience at Daniel was extremely pleasant and memorable. The tasting menu was refined, artful, and satisfying, and the impeccable service made the evening feel special from start to finish. I would gladly return for another celebration or fine-dining experience.

I recently visited with my sister, Tina Stewart, who has raved about Daniel for quite some time — and now I completely understand why. From the moment we arrived, the entire experience was nothing short of exceptional.

The wait staff was absolutely top notch — Zach, Matt, and the bartenders all went above and beyond. Attentive, knowledgeable, welcoming, and genuinely kind. You could tell they take pride not only in their work but in the experience they create for every guest.

The food… there truly are no words. Every bite was incredible. Flavorful, thoughtfully prepared, and clearly made with passion. Getting the opportunity to see the kitchen was an added bonus and only deepened my appreciation for the care and skill that goes into each dish.

It was an amazing night filled with outstanding food and even better people. Experiences like this stay with you — they aren’t just meals, they’re memories.

Until next year, I wish you all a fantastic year ahead. This is an absolute must-go place. If you get the chance, you owe it to yourself to have this experience at least once in your life. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Third time dining. Was a bit disappointed with quality of food. Tortilla was served almost cold and was more of a frittata with eggs and leeks. Shrimp head was good. Calamari also came almost in salad style in winter with cold onions. Off-season temperatures with food disappointed us. Room was also very cold to dine in, we asked if heaters could be turned on but servers just said they’ll see and never turned it on.

Burger was good.

Fish came really buttery… almost excessively. But was fine.

Small restaurant with mostly barstool seating that is uncomfortably close together. Thankfully the food and service is fantastic. Based in Spanish cuisine, the menu has a solid array of seafood options with a few meats thrown in the mix. The burger is well known but not my favorite, the texture of the meat is slightly gamey and with the anchovies it’s approaching over salted. The staples of the menu are strong including the skate fillet and the roasted chicken. The small plates get seasonal refreshes. During this visit the beefsteak tomato salad was beautiful with a surprising spice and the pea shoots were refreshing with a kick of acid at the end. Dessert here could be stronger and feels like an afterthought. The flan is good but doesn’t frequently get updates and the cake is usually not great. I wish things got updated more frequently here but the food never disappoints.

My partner and I visited Cervos for the last dinner of our trip to NYC. Overall we enjoyed dinner but it probably wouldn’t be somewhere we would recommend/return. We ordered the prawns and clams for starter but unfortunately they forgot our clams. We also ordered the sourdough but that was pretty dry and clearly had been cut hours ago. We ordered the skate and chicken for main. The skate was ok but not something we would order again. The chicken was amazing and probably one of the best chicken dishes of this type we have ever had, was really really delicious. The waiting staff were great when our dishes were forgotten (/generally)  we were offered a glass of wine on the house. Being sat on the “chef table” whilst sounded good was pretty awkward/weird when the chef asked us to move, through the waitress, as we had been sat too close to the serving spot. Overall the restaurant had a good vibe but would not recommend sitting on the counter by the chefs.

The food and service were 👌👌👌 i really wanted to try their prawn head but the menu has changed. A lot of food were sour but right level of sourness. This is a perfect date spot. Piri piri chicken and croquettes were mediocre tbh but other seafood options were amazing

It has the casual dining and wine-bar vibe that captures the spirit of Spain and Portugal.
The place is livelier at night than during the day, making it great for grabbing drinks with friends or enjoying a meal with wine.

Some friends brought us to dinner here. It was an amazing experience. The food was incredible & the service was great also. We had pork dumplings & shrimp shumae for appetizers. For dinner we had the marinated chicken & the ribeye. Both meats were delicious. The chicken literally melted in your mouth.

If you’re craving Korean BBQ in the city, this spot is a must. The Prime Marinated Beef Platter was packed with flavor and cooked perfectly at the tabletop grill. We also loved the crispy kimchi pajeon, the kkaenip bulgogi, and the comforting kimchi jjigae. The house-infused lychee soju was a standout. They’re also running a promo free Korean stew with any beef platter which makes the experience even better.

Well known kbbq spot near ktown offering pricey, but delicious marinated meats, casseroles and more. Started with half a dozen banchan, there is a variety of meat set options for the table to choose from or a la carte.

The items are cooked by staff so the usual designated kbbq chef can relax and eat😆. Seating is a bit cramped, and can be an issue for people with accessibility problems. Blue handball is used to hold the burner controls, very random.

At Nubiani (half a block away) you eat better, for less money, and they even give you a free dessert.
The platter came without the usual Korean stew and egg, and on top of that they didn’t bring the rice, which was the only thing that was actually included in the platter besides the side dishes — we had to ask for it halfway through dinner.
Once you’re done eating, they completely forget about you — good luck trying to get the check.
To make matters worse, a 25% tip is automatically added and you’re not allowed to change it.
The meat itself is good, but I’d recommend going somewhere else where you get more (and better) food for the same price.

Perfect place for lunch in Ktown, highly recommend the grilled salted mackerel, beef ribs soup and chicken stew. They also offer different banchan each time. The space has slightly dim lighting with a small bar area. The meat quality is good and portions are generous.

One of the best Indian restaurants in NYC with food and service that’s simply exceptional.

The Vada Pav is divine as they make their bread that’s just fluffy and fresh. The goat biryani and Fish curry are full of flavor and have a nice spicy flavor.

Special shout out to Sunny who’s simply an incredible guy and made our meal special.

Kanyakumari Indian Restaurant was a really great experience. The food was very flavorful across the board, and you can tell the menu is well thought out with a nice balance of dishes. Everything came out fast, which I always appreciate.

The ghee rice was especially flavorful and paired perfectly with the curries. The fish curry stood out it had deep, rich flavor with a really nice charred taste that added something extra. The shrimp curry was very good as well, nicely seasoned and cooked just right.

Overall, a solid spot if you're looking for flavorful Indian food that comes out quickly and is clearly prepared with care. I'd definitely come back.

The dosa was spectacular, I loved it so much I preferred two!! The waiter was wonderful but I want to also give a special shout out to the host because she was such a sweetheart! She did a great job. I loved the chicken curry dish but the fried chicken was not as memorable, I’d say you can skip it. I also loved the vegetable stew but warning it is spicy! I also liked the creativity of the shrimp idli. Great drinks - loved the lassi

Absolutely loved our experience here! The food was delicious, especially the fish dishes—so flavorful and perfectly prepared. Every bite felt thoughtful and authentic to South Indian cuisine.
Our waiter Sunny was amazing—attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely made the experience even better. The atmosphere was everything: vibrant, welcoming, and beautifully done.

Already can’t wait to go back. Highly recommend!

Great tribute to Kerala cuisine. To begin with the staff is really good. Sara got us a table in a min even though we had no booking.

They immediately got the baby chair setup and gave a complimentary dosa for kid.

The welcome drink rasam is great and makes u salivate.

Limited options for vegetarians but each one is looks great. We ordere a vada pav. Kochi stew and malabar parotta.

Taste is absolute on point, kochi stew  comes in generous quantity good to share between 3 pax.

Overall great experience and would definitely visit again next time !

Lungi in NYC is one of those spots you leave already planning your next visit.

The cocktails are excellent, layered with traditional South Indian and Sri Lankan flavors that feel intentional and well balanced. They complement the food beautifully instead of competing with it.

And the food really shines. The beef chukka was bold and deeply spiced. The Malabar parotta came out flaky and perfect for tearing and scooping. The fish cutlet had that crisp shell and soft, flavorful center. The goat biryani was fragrant and rich without feeling heavy. The black short rib kari was slow cooked, tender, and packed with depth.
