This is my third time here and oh my god everything just gets better. Tried their original menu (dumplings are a MUST) but LOOOVED their new Padang-style concept. Tried their Liwetan Feast during Restaurant Week in January & LOVED that too. As an Indonesian, Ma•dé really SERVED all the dishes. Elevated, but surely a fantastic introduction to Indonesian cuisine. And don’t get me started on their desserts. Although the cookies remind me of the ones I had back home as a child, the pandan crepes (dadar gulung) and passionfruit sorbet stole the show. Will definitely be back to try their spring & brunch menu!!! Heard VERY GOOD things on their lamb ribs 🥰

I really really want to like this place, but the execution isn’t fully there. There were great elements but I thought the seafood wasn’t super fresh for the price, and some of the dishes were a bit bland. The hot menu items were actually the best part, and the presentation was beautiful. Loved the cocktails. This is still a newer restaurant so I hope they can get better!

“We heard there’s a birthday at this table”, brought out an ice cream with a candle we didn’t order, and proceeded to charge us for the ice cream.

We assumed it was complimentary, as it is at every restaurant I’ve been to here in New York. It was only $4, but the principle was disappointing. Other than that, a wrong order was brought to us and taken back after we already touched it, a side dish order couldn’t be fulfilled as it was only in the pre fixed menu.. These are minor issues that if done otherwise could’ve made our experience so much better.

Overall the food was 3/5, does not remind me of Indonesia, and service was 0/5, with very little Asian representation. Lobster dumplings (the most hyped dish) was below mediocre with extremely flat flavor.

Fine for a regular meal as it was relatively affordable, but wouldn’t count on it for special occasion. And to anyone running a restaurant- come here and learn what hospitality should NOT be.

Edit: also what’s up with all the recent 5 star reviews that look like they are written by bots!!?
Came here for a birthday dinner, and the fish was incredibly fresh and flavorful. The servers were attentive, friendly, and very accommodating to allergies. Highly recommend!

I can’t think of a more perfect place for an anniversary dinner! The Office of Mr Moto delivered on exceptional high quality food and wonderful service. We had Kenji as our head chef and he is so talented and kind as he prepared 21 courses at the counter for us. Every piece of fish is so fresh and the presentation was so beautiful. The Japanese snapper, king salmon and tuna’s were my favorite. And the oyster starter was the best I’ve ever had. I also loved the truffle and caviar course, it melts in your mouth. I highly recommend the sake pairing - they match every dish perfectly and the apple one was incredible!

You have to check out the speakeasy downstairs before you leave. It is so charming and there’s a piano that plays itself, it’s so enchanting! If you’re looking for a phenomenal and memorable omakase experience, this is the place to go.

Had dinner at Office of Mr. Moto last Saturday, and I have to say I enjoyed the experience. The whole speakeasy concept and backstory leans heavily into branding, but it’s a fun setup and they commit to it. That said, the real highlight was the omakase. The sushi was excellent—super fresh, delicately prepared, and seasoned just right to enhance the natural flavors of the fish. There were some unique and rare selections that stood out. And their uni roll? Absolute bomb. I don’t think I’ve ever seen that much uni packed into one roll. You’re definitely paying extra for the concept though. I agree with other reviewers who’ve said it feels overpriced compared to some of the other high-end omakase spots in the city. Still, the quality was there and I did enjoy the meal overall.

The fish was delicious and the omakase style fantastic.  If I were the proprietor I would probably lose all of the Mr Moto stuff and focus on the food and beautiful dining room. In fairness once you are in and seated that’s pretty much what they have done anyway.

We sat at the bar and went with the classic sake pairing—highly recommend. The whole experience was elevated by the incredible storytelling from both the staff and the chef, which made each course and pour feel special. The atmosphere is intimate and welcoming, and you can tell a lot of thought goes into the details.

Would definitely recommend for anyone looking for a memorable dining experience that’s equal parts delicious and engaging.

This spot used to be a diner and Superiority Burger totally carries the legacy forward with the paper daily specials and slices of pearl pie in the refrigerated case.

That said, the menu here is unlike any restaurant anywhere. Honestly we didn’t even really know what we were ordering but the side of cabbage, fries, yuba sandwich and panelle were mind-blowing. Super wild flavors. Service was phenomenal.

I’m hooked. The pearl pie with fresh passion fruit was amazing.

We went early on a Sunday and there was no wait at all. I loved the vibe and the old photos on the wall...in particular, a photo of Dojo on St Marks which brought back a lot of memories...

Service was laid-back, friendly and quick.

On to the food...three in my party got the Superiority Burger with fries in three different ways. It was all spot-on and after tasting it, it is a strong vegetarian burger. But forget that and go for the TFT - a fried tofu sandwich which was simply outstanding.  The fries are some of the absolute best I've had in NYC.

We also had a side of burnt broccoli which was ok, but nothing too special. Go for the TFT, fries and the vibe.

This place is magic - the founder brings his eclectic taste to create something truly special.

The Superiority Burger (the namesake!) is pure perfection. The tanginess from the pickles, the soft yet crunchy patty… every bite feels special, like I’m blessed or something. And when I’m in the mood to cheat, I’ll pair it with the fries — also perfection. Everything here tastes so fresh and high-quality.

Burnt Broccoli - again, perfection. It comes with a sauce on the side that’s such a nice surprise, and I go every week and NEVER get bored.

The Date Shake… who would’ve thought it’d be so interesting? The founder always sneaks in elements that elevate the flavor profile - the surprise this time is the orange zest.

Their specials are always exceptional and super creative. I guarantee you won’t see anything like them anywhere else.

And the service - truly great. I’ve seen the same staff for years, which brings a sense of community and continuity that’s rare in the city these days.

So yes… I come here all the time, and I’m never bored! Oh yes it is worth the hype btw!

Almost never misses. Love the integration with local and seasonal produce. Phenomenal desserts. Unlike other nyc institutions with staid menus and no variation you can have different food every time or rely on old favorites. Underrated for sure

Vegan restaurant by Tompkins park. The halumi and pumpkin starter was amazing. I had the Yube sandwich, wouldn’t recommend. Their house burger was definitely a better choice.

Good if you’re looking for a vegan or vegetarian option. On the expensive side, and there’s definitely better places in the area.

I’d go back but only for the burger.

Great food, wine, and dessert! Ordered the chicken liver agnolotti, half chicken, chips, and devil’s food cake. We also enjoyed excellent Spanish white wine and a few mocktails.

The service was great from the moment we walked in. Every member of the staff was incredibly attentive and helpful.

We had a reservation, arrived on time and were seated promptly. We never felt rushed but we were just two people and dined on a weekday night so that could be why.

(We did reserve online. I recommend people to check that out as well!!)

Red Shrimp with Olive Oil and Garlic - the best dish of the night. The shrimp was sweet and tender, and the oil underneath it added great aroma and richness. We had like 3 plates of bread to eat w the oil.

Beef tongue w salsa verde - The presentation was nice, but the slices were very thin so the texture was not very impressive. The sour cream in the center was actually good and helped balance the acidity.

Veal sweetbreads w pepperoncini aioli - This was the weakest dish. The frying was very oily and heavy, and the portion was quite small. The flavor did not justify the texture, so I would not order this again.

🐟- This came out last. The flavor was mild and the fish was tender, and it did help us feel full by the end. The lemon 🍋 is an extra bonus. Very refreshing.

Cute place, great wine, and food was really solid. I hesitated between 4-5 stars because the appetizers, which usually are the best in restaurants, where OKish here (a bit too fat IMO). But the ribs were amazing, and the chicken liver pasta was out of this world. So definitely a 5 stars.

PS: oh and unlimited bread like in civilized countries? that's also a 5-star deserving thing to do

The food was good but not as good as I feel like my friends raved about. The pork stood out to me, really liked the sauce that was on top. Mille feuille is a total skip, was seriously flavorless and basically just a some puffed pastry sheets stacked on top of each other. Other things were just okay. We ordered a ton of food and drinks just between us girls but didn’t really have time to enjoy it all. They were very adamant about the 2 hour time limit even though we spent a lot and rushed us out of there.

We went here for my birthday dinner and I just wanna say from the start. The interior of this place is adorable. It is super cozy feels almost like a very rustic cavity. Feel kitchen is wide open for you to see everything that we were cooking which I love I had pretty high hopes walking in here and it has a pretty good reputation. They also own the sister restaurant a penny upstairs who I think has one of the best desserts in New York City so I put this place pretty high on my expectations.

Everything my hand was decently good it was good. Nothing was mind blowing though. The pit was a starter. It was strong good portion for you get for pate and went great on the bread

The jamon or prosciutto was also really strong and delicious. However, after that, I forgot what these dishes were I can’t even name them looking at the pictures anymore. The pasta was decent. The problem is after I left this place. I almost forgot this meal totally if it wasn’t for the atmosphere. It wasn’t for the space that I loved so much. It would’ve been quite forgettable for me.

Of course, the one of the most famous things they have. Here is the chocolate cake. It is huge decadent delicious I’m not really a chocolate cake person and we definitely have to take home, but I really love eating it the next two days.

I do remember also having some kind of steak with blueberries on it. It felt great Thanksgiving and I don’t know it’s like berries on my steaks personal choice. It’s a personal choice.

A nice tapas place.  Service was friendly and very fast.  I think we were in and out in 45 min on Sunday night.  The two of us had four tapas dishes (see photos).  The popcorn chicken and oxbone cereal pasta are def worth trying and very tasty.  The tuna tartare and seoulsbury steak were fine, seemed pretty standard.  We weren’t really sure what the Korean twist on those two dishes was.  We didn’t order any drinks, but they did give us two small shots on the house.  I would go back to try other tapas.

Incredible experience. Food was amazing and made with finesse and deep flavors. Service is quick friendly and you feel welcome right from the start. Menu is well explained. Atmosphere is packed but cosy - a very lively NYC neighborhood experience. I would come back any time - our highlights were the Steak with a cream that was outstanding, the Popcorn chicken, Pasta and Mushroom Bibimbap (little marinated button mushrooms for extra pops of deep flavor which we found genius) - must tries when you are there!

We were incredibly impressed at C as in Charlie. Every single dish we had was very good - 3 of them were exceptional. The mozzarella/green pepper with soy balsamic was insanely good, the ribs were melt in your mouth and the prawn roll delicious too. Service was excellent and the restaurant had a real buzz/warmth to it. Absolutely shouldn’t be missed. Surprisingly reasonably priced too.

While visiting the town, we met up with friends to catchup. I saw this place listed on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list and snagged a reservation.

They do enforce a two-hour time limit for parties of four. As my friend was running late, the servers frequently reminded us of the time constraint. Fortunately, we finished our meal within the allotted time; I have never encountered a restaurant that did so many reminders about the dining time. This was the only minor drawback; otherwise, I would have given it a perfect rating.

The mushroom bibimbap was exceptional; I could have easily eaten just a big bowl of that and been happy. The potato nuggets were also quite delicious, with the truffle aioli. The popcorn chicken, however, was not my favorite, as it seemed excessively sauced.

The food portion sizes were ideal for sharing among our group of four. It came out at a pretty good price point per diner, especially for the area.

Pretty good food and surprisingly great service! The food wasn't very frou-frou, just simple small plates done very well.

Oxbone cream pasta was delightfully rich (but not overly so), seoul'sbury steak was peak comfort food, and the popcorn chicken was pretty standard chicken with a good gochu glaze. The dessert was also really delicious although a bit hard to eat. Drinks were good too, server brought out little samples of each thing which was great for my decision paralysis.

An underrated and underdiscovered elegant restaurant with amazing service. A Well deserved Michelin star, they went out of their way to make my friend's birthday a fabulous experience. The burger (not on a tasting menu) was top class and tasting menu was also a hit, especially caviar topped scallops. The dessert was a bit too sweet though.

Came here with my friend on the second day of my NY trip and it was great! From start to finish, every dish was creative and beautifully balanced in flavor. I ordered a drink that was a bit too spicy for me, and when they asked how it was, I jokingly said that I liked my friend’s better. They immediately offered to make me a new one. I didn’t take it because it was honestly fine, but I was genuinely touched by their generosity :)

The pacing of the dishes was just right, they gently wiped our table between each course. They were super thoughtful. I had a truly wonderful experience, and this was definitely one of the highlights of my short trip.

9.30.2025

i celebrated my birthday here with mom & i can say with full confidence that this is the best meal ive had this year.

comparing to other michelin french fine dining establishments, i would pick this as my top 1 for overall hospitality, food and price point. essential offers a truly unique seafood-focused menu with every course being as memorable or even better than the last. the flavor combinations are rich, perfectly well-balanced & all-around luxurious. dont underestimate the simple presentations because the taste will blow you away.

alfonso was our server—he was AMAZING! very attentive & made my night feel extra special with personal touches, check-ins throughout the meal as well as assisting me with my annoying vlog/photo sessions.

cant forget to mention that the dining room is extremely gorgeous with its warm yellow hues, flowers & intimate table settings—perfect for date night. im already looking forward to revisiting & telling all my friends about it. simply exceeded all my expectations—wont be surprised to see essential gain another star soon. thank you so much team!

Absolutely Exceptional Dining Experience

We had the most incredible experience at Essential by Christophe. We were there celebrating the newlyweds, and choosing the Chef’s Room truly made the evening unforgettable. The level of service was unlike anything I’ve ever experienced, every single staff member made us feel welcomed, comfortable, and genuinely cared for. They anticipated what we needed before we even asked and made sure every guest had exactly what they wanted.

The food was outstanding. The Wagyu beef cap was melt-in-your-mouth perfection, the scallop was a clear highlight, and the mushroom cappuccino was one of the most unique and delicious dishes. Every course was beautifully executed and thoughtfully balanced.

If you’re looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion or want a dining experience that exceeds every expectation, I cannot recommend this restaurant enough. Absolutely five stars.

Very much enjoyed this meal. Pro tip is that you can order à la carte if you sit at the bar, great if you want to keep it more casual than the formal dining room. The must gets are the lobster pasta and the burger — the Wagyu steak was great, but didn’t stand out versus other versions of it I’ve had. The desserts also stood out and were probably my favorite part of the meal.

Service was great at the bar. can’t speak to the dining room, but I’m sure excellent as well.

Value for money was excellent, we spent about $180 post tax & tip for two people. Also, we’re were given a couple small complementary bites.

came here for my last dinner on my nyc trip and was very impressed. we dined on a monday and the restaurant was still quite busy and had a great ambience. the wine list is extensive and their chilled red is honestly one of the best that i have tried. we ordered arancini, the grape salad, tagliatelle, and radiatori. all were incredible, i especially loved the radiatori. the pasta tasted very fresh and the service was attentive. we also tried the date cake for dessert which was delicious. i wish we had somewhere like this in australia but i will definitely be returning on my next nyc trip.

Here’s the thing… I find nothing more appealing than when a restaurant has high principles and strong technique but does not show them off in flashy and attention grabbing ways. We walked into Soda Club off the street, drawn in by perfect lighting, cozy decor and that feeling that these folks knew exactly what they were on about. Service was 💯 on point and friendly. The herbed ricotta was creamy, decadent with jammy confit cherry tomatoes. The watercress salad sang with perfectly complimentary silky feta and sweet roasted grapes. The light, crisp Roman style carbonara pizza was perfectly balanced with gently fried artichokes, smoked mushrooms and bright, lemony arugula. We finished with gigli pasta showcasing white truffles, crispy leeks and a velvety cream sauce. Overall, a spectacular, thoughtfully prepared, soul satisfying feast. Now… here is the twist, half way through the meal, we asked about the spice level of the chorizo on another pizza. The server said, the -tofu- chorizo… wait… what? Tofu chorizo… is this place vegetarian?? !Vegan! We were shocked and delighted. And this brings me back to my opening gambit. This was the best vegan dining experience we had ever had (and we have enjoyed many) and there was not a hint of the virtue signaling that drags down most of the field. —Nothing— about the experience was sacrificed to promote ideals or a lifestyle imperative. There was clearly some masterful chemistry happening in the kitchen but no floating spheres or insubstantial foams. The meal was decadent yet sat lightly with us. Not a sliver of texture or flavor was compromised in the pursuit of healthy living. This was a delightful dining experience, executed with style, finesse and attention to every detail, and, oh, by the way, the food was vegan. Also noteworthy is the substantial, well curated natural wine list from which a glass of the Georgian Sapervani was a perfect compliment to our meal. Hats off to everyone involved. We could not be more impressed.

Service super, vibes are immaculate. Congrats to the chef for those dishes and flavours … wow wow. Never had these kind of combinations before. Highlights for us were the Carbonara Pinsa and the Date Cake (accompanied w the Hungarian Furmint which balanced perfectly)

I am going to attempt to relate what a delightful, even joyous experience. It was eating at soda club last night.

I think I could be classified a carnivore, in that I don’t remember going to a vegan only restaurant. But when I was doing my research for new places to dine here last week, I was so intrigued by the menu, I somehow missed  the fact that it was vegan only. Honestly, I don’t think I would have chosen it. Now… I’m considering going vegan. But I’m not sure there’s another place like this.

It didn’t start off good. We had gotten up at 3 AM in Austin To catch the flight  and were beat And ready to eat dinner early. After a cold walk/ long cab drive from where we staying near the park. we found ourselves at an innocuous corner a bit early a few minutes before it opened at 5:00. It is difficult to see before they open the door, but at five, a young man walked up and rolled up a graffiti covered garage door to reveal the inviting entrance.
We walked across the street to the friendly Niagara bar for a drink before ( recommended- great Village vibe )
Still unsure as to what we would find, we walked in to a wonderful cozy spot. We started off with a delightful French  cab , exquisite.
By the time we had the focaccia, we knew we were in a kind of a magical space. We’ve had focaccia bread all over the world from California to Italy. This was undoubtedly the best. Dipped in a fresh garlic sauce that I can only describe as divinely inspired.
I had the carbonara which had an incredible smokey  flavor with mushrooms and artichokes tempura . Uniquely delicious. My wife loved the Butternut Squash Medaglioni, and I was lucky enough to get a few bites. Never had anything like this.

The intimate dark setting is small but very well designed, and clean.

Our server Owen was gracious and very helpful with selections. After dinner, Katy stopped by our table and we went on even more than this review about how much we enjoyed the experience. She obviously really cared about our experience, as was evident by every detail of this restaurant.

I’ve never read the review this long. Bordering on a short story. But I was inspired …  I think you will be too.

This place is amazing. For starters, my server Madi and the bartender Manu were great company. Manu played great music, made delicious drinks, and was a fun conversationalist. Madi showed me a bunch of great wines from across the world with super detailed flavor profiles, truly a fun wine-tasting experience. From Italy, to Slovenia, I tasted notes of strawberries, chocolate, raspberry and more.

She also made impeccable food suggestions and I was blown away by the focaccia, ravioli and arracinhi. We topped it off with a tiramisu.
Focaccia- crispy on the outside, soft, warm and buttery on the inside. The garlic and chili pepper paste to dip was a nice contrast to the usual olive oil at most spots.
Arracinhi- also very crispy. The star of the show here was the tomato sauce. Sweet and savory. Just straight up some great tomatoes.
Ravioli- Wow. Just WOW. A very happy marriage between lemon and creaminess. You would never guess it’s vegan. While it only came with 3 pieces, it was pretty filling. It also had these juicy mushrooms and sweet grape tomatoes that really added to the deliciousness.
Tiramisu- Delicious. Not too sweet, surprisingly a bit chocolatey. Great way to end the meal.

I don’t eat a lot of vegan food but after this meal I’d like to add some vegan spots to my rotation. Even my boyfriend, who said he didn’t want to eat vegan food, will most definitely be coming back. I would be more than happy to try the rest of the food, cocktails, and wines at this spot. Soda Club is my newest obsession and go-to elevated date spot. The vibe is homey, romantic, and intimate, while also being funky and innovative with their menu.

Terrific dining experience at ITO. This restaurant is one of the finest omakase dining in NYC. It's my second time eating here, and the quality of food and service remained very high.
Fresh and delicious food, masterfully prepared by our chef. Each dish was like an art both visually and taste wise. A vast selection of fresh ingredients. Service was top-notch, alway attentive and cordial. The setting was also very pleasant, sinmple, elegant  and welcoming.
I highly recommend this restaurant.

Dinner at ITO was an amazing experience. The omakase was outstanding—fresh, high-quality sushi with incredible flavor in every bite, and the fish was truly exceptional. They also offer a great variety of sake, and the tea is so good as well.

The atmosphere is intimate, and I loved being so close to the chefs, they explained each dish in detail, which made the experience even more special. The service was attentive, welcoming, and knowledgeable from start to finish.

I highly recommend this restaurant. Unforgettable experience.

One of the best omakase experiences I’ve ever had! I came in with very high expectations after dining at Ito in Las Vegas at the Fontainebleau Hotel—which was phenomenal—and I was excited to see they had a location in NYC. I’m happy to say this experience exceeded my expectations.

From the moment we arrived, the staff was warm, welcoming, attentive, and prompt. We had the honor of meeting Chef Kevin, who was incredibly gracious and truly an artist in his craft. Every course showcased the highest quality ingredients, with a burst of flavor in every bite. From the appetizers to dessert, each dish was beautifully presented and thoughtfully crafted.

I especially loved that we were given the option to add additional pieces at the end of the course, and that Chef Kevin offered this before dessert—it was a thoughtful touch that elevated the entire experience. The drink menu is also very well curated, with an excellent selection of sake and other alcoholic beverages to complement the meal.

This is absolutely a place I will continue to visit every time I’m in town. A must-try for any omakase lover in NYC.

Very delicious meal with quality fish. The cod was soft and paired nicely with the miso. The standouts for me were the truffle mushroom soup which was just nice on a cold day and the mushroom tasted so fresh. The seared otoro had a smokey flavor to it and melted in my mouth. The truffle Wagyu was definitely my favorite because what’s not to love?? Truffle was strong and freshly shaved. Wagyu torched to the perfect fatty level. The dessert was very lovely liked the buttery cream on top with the crunchy popcorn and miso base. The counter does get quite crowded and seats more than the typical amount of people at an omakase

We have dined at multiple Michelin rated restaurants around the world and can honestly say that this was the best dining experience that we've ever had. From the start, the concept of only opening the doors 5 minutes before seating allows you and the rest of the patrons to gather outside in anticipation, it's a nice way to meet everyone you'll be dining with before sitting down. Once the doors opened they immediately checked us in, took our coats and commented on the reservation notes, wishing me a happy birthday. I was again wished a happy birthday as I was being seated and then a third time by our Omakase chef. The food was incredible and the staff was so friendly. Important note: if you don't like group dining experiences, this is not for you. If you like sitting with and meeting new people with delicious food and attentive service, this experience is well worth the money. While it seems that some reviews comment that they didn't like the food, I am getting the impression that at last parts of the menu change, for example we had a mushroom and truffle soup whereas others mention a miso soup. The rice for the nigiri was warm and fresh, and wasabi was grated right in front of us before being added to our food. Will recommend to everyone I know!

Chef was excellent. As far as nyc high end omakase goes some of the best, if not the best, rice preparation there is. And his use of the abalone in both dishes was amazing. Loved talking to him about sushi and food in general. Highly recommend!

What a great night for my 64 birthday.  I get there and tell them I'm 64 by singing verse when I'm 64 and the gut says I love the Beatles, anyway we seat and Kazu starts serving us appetizers then sushi . It was so much food I was stuffed and happy I will leave pic of menu to see what I had . At end brought bday candle and played when I'm 64 on speakers.  Brought tear to my eyes .

I had my good bye dinner with my manager here. It was absolutely amazing.

I like how the food is not strictly traditional. I feel that the chef put a lot of heart and feeling into each of his dishes, which is very special.

We tasted an abundance of flavors for all the dishes and absolutely love the chef’s touch of modern innovation. The atmosphere was fun and friendly, which we enjoy as well.

My favorite is definitely the unbelievably delicious beef, the Uni and crab pasta, and the melon dessert, which are all refreshing and very enjoyable.

Very nice place! A bit hard to find given being on a Main Street. The interior is welcoming and modern. There were a few minor odd choices for a Michelin star restaurant: disposable chopsticks, and laminated plastic signs on the doors.

The food was a fusion of Japanese and Italian cuisine, and felt completely unique. Flavors that i I didn’t know worked together were delicious. Would definitely return.

The food was all delicious, beautifully presented, and well timed. The service was accommodating, even reseating my party after arrival at my request. The restaurant itself is very subdued on the exterior, so be careful not to walk passed it.

Overall, this place is cute. It’s above a car dealership, which is still a little strange but it’s cute. The first time I went the drinks were just OK so I personally won’t get mixed drinks so the second time I went we got wine. My experience here have always been good when it comes to staff and the space. The drinks is iffy, but the food is also good. I may actually consider coming back here again for a third time which is very rare for me.

Food – everything I ate was good and everything looked very presentable, beautiful even however, they stand out here with the tuna tartare. However, the tuna tartare does not come with chips or bread, which is kind of annoying, but the staff did recommend to get these crispy chip appetizer as a great side for that and honestly kudos to the staff that was a genius idea and it made me very happy. They should literally be served together. It doesn’t make sense. Everything I have was good. Everything made me happy. I think I made noise noises delicious noise noises every time and it made me very happy. The wine pairing was good. See the pics I attached because come on. It’s beautiful.

Atmosphere – ambience -  the space is cute however, I always find it quite empty and a a little too quiet. But at night time it was during the day and it’s really comfortable. It’s a huge space and as I mentioned, it’s above a car dealership so after you’re done, go look at cute cars the staff here is always attentive and always amazing and honestly they really set up the standard. However they took my jacket and they didn’t didn’t take my friends jackets so strange.

Go for the food go back for the food. It was so good.

What an experience! Talk about the total package - this place has it all. If you aren’t familiar with the Genesis House (i.e. me, despite walking past by many times), the lobby is the showroom for Genesis, the basement has the special exhibition throughout the year, and the 2nd floor is the dining room. If you have a dining reservation here, you can visit the exhibition before or after the meal. Jose, our friendly host, helped us with navigating the planning.

The menu features a tasting menu and à la carte. For a restaurant that deserves a Michelin star, it is truly a gem to discover a very reasonably priced tasting menu. Since the four of us aren’t particularly hungry, we ordered a bunch from à la carte to share. Our server, Patrick, was great at recommendations - beef tartare (order with the lotus chips), rice cake, pork noodles (daeji guksu), and short rib (tteokgalbi). Not only were the dishes beautifully presented, despite the simplicity of the name, each dish was carefully executed with traditional Korean cooking while adding a modern twist to it.

The beverage menu was very fun too! We had the k-town soju pear + perilla (tasty and sweet), Hanbang (balanced), and two different kinds of makgeolli (try mixing both into one special kind).

The service was outstanding! Our water glass was never empty, the service was attentive but not overwhelming. We had a wonderful 5-year anniversary celebration with our family at Genesis House. We will return for the tasting menu next time!

Absolutely gorgeous restaurant and unique experience. We started with the light show downstairs prior to dinner. The food was all beautifully presented, however we only really enjoyed the first few dishes. We had a tasting menu and probably would have been better ordering a la carts, as duck and the spare ribs were not something I would typically ever eat. That being said, the spare ribs were macerated into an almost meatball and I don’t think that presentation is something I would ever want to see again. Desert was good. Restaurant was incredibly cold inside, which also made the experience a little less well received.

Honestly the lunch set here was one of the best i have had. It was so clean and 정갈해. You could tell there was a lot of thought that went into everything from the rice, main protein, to individual side dish 반찬. Dessert was ok but the lunch really did impress me. Pretty good service and the folks down stairs were super friendly explaining the cars and the Genesis house itself. Worth a stop if you are in the area.

I have travelled the world extensively over 40 years. I ate at all restaurants ranging from pop & mom’s to Michelin three stars. This is my honest review of the Genesis House in meatpacking district in New York, NY, USA.

Genesis House is truly a hidden gem — located on the second floor of the Genesis car dealership, which you access through the showroom, either by stairs or elevator. The restaurant offers both a tasting and an à la carte menu; we went for the latter.

We started with the beef tartare with egg yolk, beautifully seasoned with chili and tomato. It was spicy, creamy, and perfectly balanced — an absolute success. The lobster rice followed, served with a salmon roll and a generous piece of lobster. Presented in a striking, almost artistic way, it revealed even more depth of flavor once mixed together.

The short rib with serrano pesto and broccolini was likely the highlight of the evening — tender, flavorful, and simply outstanding. For dessert, we tried the banana puff pastry with candied banana and banana milk ice cream — a delicious explosion of flavor.

We also enjoyed a soothing ginger and citrus infusion to finish the meal. Every dish was executed with precision and creativity — worthy, in my opinion, of a Michelin star.

The interior design is spectacular — rich wood tones, refined architecture, and even a library seating area where guests remove their shoes and dine close to the floor in the traditional Korean way. The kitchen is semi-open, and the staff are warm, attentive, and professional.

Considering the exceptional quality, the pricing is very reasonable. Some tables offer a lovely view over the Hudson River, just steps away from Little Island. Genesis House instantly became one of my new favorite restaurants in New York.

Every dish was a surprise — not only beautifully executed, but genuinely making us discover new flavors and combinations. The food managed to be both creative and comforting at the same time, with each plate presented like a small piece of art.

The service was truly exceptional: attentive, knowledgeable, and perfectly paced, making the whole evening feel effortless and special.

A must-visit for anyone who loves gastronomy and thoughtful fine dining. We’ll definitely be back

Most of the reason for taking out stars is the price. I think the food was good, but was a little flat for me. I appreciate the presentation and I liked the courses, but I left hungry and I didn’t think the flavors were all that creative or delicious for a Michelin star which such expensive prices. The bread was cold, the butter was cold. I got the petite tasting menu, and I’m glad I didn’t do the full tasting menu. There’s only really three courses that are very very small and dessert. They had a nice place card and gave me a candle for my bday which was nice. The host and the waiters were also wonderful. I think the food just fell flat. For the very very high prices, it just wasn’t worth it for me. I was not impressed unfortunately. For an almost $300 meal, i should be astounded

I knew within the first 30 minutes of this experience that it was going to be one of the best meals of my life, and I was not wrong. I have eaten at many great/Michelin starred restaurants throughout the United States and Europe, and L’Abeille just catapulted its way into my top 5.

The space itself is fantastic, beautiful and intimate yet not overbearing, and the service even better. The sommelier was extremely knowledgeable about the wine list and was able to provide us with a bottle that gave us exactly what we were looking for within our price range. And then the food. Chef Mitsunobu walks the line between indulgent decadence and childlike creativity in the greatest way. It is rare that a menu is able to be clearly committed to giving you the best versions of food you have had before, while also introducing you to completely new flavors and culinary ideas. A rarity at most restaurants, the most memorable dish may have been the chicken course. Granted, it was helped with foie gras and whisky infused jus, but still, some of the flavors found on that plate made me stop to reconsider the possibilities of a what a chicken dish can provide. Some other highlights include the most incredible combination of prawns and grilled eggplant inside the flower of a courgette, then a peking duck au poivre with intense peppercorn, and a citrus-forward dessert that played with temperature, acid, and sweetness like not many can.

I cannot give any higher praise to Chef Mitsunobu and his team at L’Abeille, and I cannot recommend it enough. My only regret is that I wish I could’ve thanked him myself after the meal.

An incredible dining experience for our birthday! We visited l'abeille recently and every dish had its own personality. The stuffed squash blossom was full of flavor and impeccably plated. The tile fish with tomato sauce vierge was sublime. Loved how the scales were cooked crispy. The desserts were awesome too, the celery popsicle was playful and refreshing — such a fun way to begin the sweet part of the meal. The lemon dessert was creative, bright, and the perfect finish to the evening.

well deserved the star! all the food comes so pretty and delicious! our server is also very nice and informative! the space is also clean and very intimate for a nice cute dinner:)

went here for my birthday and they give me some complimentary chocolate sandwiches, sweet! thank you for making my birthday feels special! i’m definitely going back for another season!❤️

Location: very accessible via public transit .If driving in make sure to check for a parking lot in the area (it a busy area and might not have street parking)

Service: Just one sound - WOW .The staff is incredible and looks like they truly enjoy their craft which makes it a delight to watch them work. The team knew it was my friends' birthday and allergies,even had a special birthday menu printed so she could have a memento which I found very thoughtful

Ambiance: Very intimate and relaxed, we sat at the counter and enjoyed seeing the team at work.The space is very welcoming

Now to the most important part- the FOOD. We had the chef's tasting menu.

The starters were light and fresh . The first starter with egg and caviar was so beautiful it was a shame to eat it, and it tasted like a hug.

The handrolls were magnificent.Each one had layers of flavors and textures condensed to a single bite. My favorite ones were the Spicy Tuna with a crunch and the Chef's special with sea urchin.
The handmade noodle and soup were a very nice savory dish , great on a cold day like today.
For dessert there was an assortment of items, my personal favorite was the Coconut sorbet and lemon curd.But all were wonderful, not too sweet and perfect ending to a greateal

All and all 10/10 definitely recommend for special occasions

Very special tasting menu! The first course was immediately one of the bests - caviar over an egg cake in mentaiko butter sauce. All 7 hand rolls were layered with flavor and so elegantly plated. Works of art! The noodle + banchan course was a simple contrast to the rolls and had the most perfectly cooked shrimp. Lastly, the desserts were excellent. The service was very gracious, but the pacing a little slow so I’d recommend sitting at the counter to keep the momentum.

Such an amazing place, perfect for any celebration! They made the night so special for us, we were celebrating a birthday. Highly recommend making reservations and doing counter seating (set menu). Food was beautiful and delicious.

Staff was incredible. Thank you for the detailed touches and thoughtfulness!

Note: Service was a bit slow in the beginning so don’t arrive starving.

Very good food. It is inevitable that one might compare it to an omakase although some of the offerings might be more unique. Price wise you could probaby do two omakases for the price of mari. I was not a big fan of the sorbet but the rest of the desert was great. The egg +rice cake appetizer was the standout dish of the evening.

Always found my self walking by this restaurant and it looked so intriguing. Finally decided to try it and had such an amazing experience. Everyone was so friendly. The food was exceptional. Tried a red makgeolli which was new to us and delicious.

But who really stole the show was our server, Jin. She was so knowledgeable, warm, personable, fun and enthusiastic. She made sure we had the best evening and we did!! Will definitely be returning to Mari and requesting Jin!

I stopped by Chick Chick with a couple of friends for a quick bite, and omg what a find! The chicken sandwiches and tenders were incredibly flavorful and juicy. The portions were generous, way more than what you’d get at most places in the city. And the honey bread? Chef’s kiss. Definitely coming back to try more items on the menu!

The chicken was huge, juicy and flavorful. Service was super fast, takeout until closing. I got the Nashville and Korean BBQ. The sauces were not huge flavor, was hoping for more of a punch with the big piece of chicken.

Chick chick was a seriously fantastic place to eat. Its in the city, Upper West Side, so parking is on the street and its close to public transit. The service was friendly, quick and knowledgeable and the food....... oh goodness, the food.
I wanted to try every single thing, literally. I would have been thrilled to have that ability.. what I did eat was absolutely incredible and the pictures are attached. The chicken bites had these amazing pops of spice and flavor, and the waffle chicken sandwich looked as good as it tasted; each bite was simply delicious. Next time, and believe me, there will be a next time, I'm simply going to use the menu as a food check list! 10/10 highly recommend!

Chick Chick delivers a mouthwatering fried chicken experience that goes beyond expectations, both in flavor and service. The Nashville fried chicken sandwich was a highlight, crispy, juicy, and perfectly spiced, nestled in a soft, buttery bun with creamy slaw that tied it all together. The chicken and waffles brought a delightful balance of sweet and savory, with golden, fluffy waffles and crunchy, well-seasoned chicken. The truffle fries were crisp and addictive, with just the right hint of truffle oil to elevate them without overpowering. The fried chicken and mac n cheese combo was pure comfort food bliss, featuring creamy, cheesy pasta paired with more of their signature crispy chicken. On top of the fantastic food, the service was incredible, friendly, fast, and genuinely attentive, making the whole dining experience feel warm and welcoming. Chick Chick is a must-visit for anyone who loves bold flavors, hearty portions, and top-notch hospitality.

Crispy saucy delicious chicken and sides. Stopped in randomly and got myself a half chicken with gochujang sauce paired with a crunchy pickle. The sauce and crunchy breading on the chicken was delicious and the chicken was flavorful. Wasn’t thee most tender chicken but it was still great. The street corn was pretty good and easy to eat. The kimchi slaw was really incredible especially pairing a bite with the chicken. Sooo good.

TLDR;
Original Brooklyn style Chinese takeout with a little flair.

The vibe in here is great, maybe a little too many things hanging from the ceiling, but otherwise the design and decor was nailed.

For the order we got two drinks, which were really good- interesting flavors with Lyle pops of spice and flavor.

The good here was cooked extremely well….. BUT!!

The good dishes we tried:
- egg roll was stellar
- cold noodles were good but the noodles are pasta🤨
- shrimp and broccoli are great
- daiquiri and margarita were good

The flavoring was off…not in a bad way, but I’ll explain.

- Chicken wings: cooked perfectly, the salt/pepper was not existent
- tuna crudo: sauce was amazing, cut of tuna was good however it was not great- mating the cut could be thinner, but the texture more resembles tuna steak
- crispy crab Rangoon: this was a complete miss here. The mozzarella in the Rangoon is not a good idea. The texture inside doesn’t align with the name, and the flavor spent hot on any level. The crab inside also is unevenly placed. The whole dish needs a rework, otherwise this dish is a DOA.

A true neighborhood gem! The cocktails are fantastic, and the food — though a bit salty for my taste — is still worthy of a Michelin Guide mention.
Excellent service, a cozy ambiance, and a spotless bathroom make this spot a definite must-visit!

Sal Tang’s is an excellent addition to the neighborhood. There is comfortable seating outside, however the interior of the restaurant is worth checking out and might provide an even cozier atmosphere. The menu has some delicious dishes that mix Cantonese, American, and Italian. This is Chinese-American comfort food done really well.

I really liked the salad and the crispy tofu. Good dressing on both of them. The beef pancake disappointed me, it was too salty and sweet, and I could take neither the pancake nor the beef. The ambiance is strongly American Chinese and upscale in a good nostalgic way. However, it is very loud inside and the tables are packed together, so it's hardly a cozy place to eat. I had eaten at a restaurant that used to be in the same location and it was a much more welcoming space.

Sal Tang’s serves favorite Chinese comfort food and snacks and is a popular destination in the Cobble Hill neighborhood in Brooklyn.

It was busy when we came here for Sunday dinner and was unable to accommodate us inside even when it was raining (we had booked for outdoor dining).

Our group shared some appetizers such as scallion pancakes and cucumber salad with a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc. The cucumber salad was light and very refreshing.

We then ordered four dishes and shared them family-style. We had beef and broccoli, crispy branzino with black bean sauce, their signature sesame chicken cutlets, cumin lamb over rice, sautéed pea shoots, and shrimp fried rice.

Overall, the dishes are decent and with good portions. The dishes are served in a timely fashion, and we enjoyed every single dish that was presented to us. We had a lovely time here. With good food and awesome customer service, you won’t be embarrassed to recommend this place to family and friends.

We celebrated our anniversary at L’Adresse, th staff made us feel so special. They offered complimentary sparking wine & macaroons. We ordered a focaccia & crispy calamari as appetizers. My main course was a seafood risotto which was pretty good. The desert was great too. It is nice ambience and our server was helpful and friendly. I would definitely come back.

I searched it up… Walked a short U… and walla, I entered a restaurant that looked like a Hotel at 1st glance! Inside ambiance matched my mood and the 3 people that spoke with me were all pleasant! LOBSTER CARBONARA w/ Gold Caviar topping.
Natalia & Hita were my servers & both very polite!

Upscale and worth it, I tried the truffle burger and it was delicious. Beef tartare too, and seafood risotto. The bartender is also too quality - mixed me a Monkey 47 martini with a dash of orange bitters and a slice of orange peel, the perfect complement to the meal!

My girlfriend and I had a great time at ladrese and even more amazing and delicious food. The salmon was cooked to perfection. However, the most pleasantly surprising items on the menu were syrniki and sea buckhorn tea which were my true favorites as well as Frank (who was not on the menu unfortunately ) but he provided not only a great service but he also knows some Russian. definitely coming back! 🌸

Erick our server was amazing. Vibes was great and beautiful. Service was 10/10. Came for my birthday brunch and food came fast and was delicious they gave us complimentary cookies, cake and a really nice booth. Overall a great weekend brunch spot and date night.

My family and I walked in over Labor Day weekend for brunch on Sunday and loved everything about this place (the food, the garden) except for the service. My boyfriend and I both work in hospitality so we appreciate great service, but we're not unrealistic with our expectations. We just appreciate kind people who aren't overbearing or pressing, but the woman who served us was so cold and rude, it truly made us feel uncomfortable. There was no warm greeting, not even a smile, she barely spoke a word to us the entire time we were there. We were one of two tables in the garden and there were 3 tables in the front, so it's not like she was busy or anything. The 3 of us ordered the dandelion salad, French toast, poached eggs entree, zucchini blossoms, bacon and hasbrowns. Our server didn't check on us once. Never asked how our meal was, if we needed anything, literally not a word. She literally just took our order, put the plates down and we never heard from her again. The service was very robotic, truly it was like a robot was serving us, because there was just nothing personable about it. There are a lot of places in NY with good food, but it's the service that sets it apart. I dont think we'll be returning or recommending this place.

Sam, the general manager, made this an unforgettable night for my mom and me. We agreed it was one of the best meals we’ve ever had.

The bread and the halibut were delicious beyond words. The tuna with greens was surprisingly delightful (more my mom’s taste than mine, but I’m glad I tried). We could have done without the chilled shrimp crudo, missed the mark for us.

The drink list was incredible, and our bottle (the Patapon white) was perfection. Well worth the trek to Red Hook! Thanks to Helen Rosner for the rec and lovely write-up!

I’d say this place is really good value in NYC. For me, everything pictured here (split with my friend) represented about $75 (including tip).

The experience is very similar to eating in a Parisian bistro, with the tables being right next to each other in a small environment. The upside to that is that the service was very good—shout out to the staff who were consistently filling my water since I drink a lot 😂

For the food, I was very impressed by the “toast” which is just a grilled baguette. I really like the charred flavor that was imparted onto the bread, which I would gladly have eaten on its own.

We were both surprised by the cafe salad, where the cheese blindsided us. We assumed it was going to be something like butternut squash, but were pleasantly surprised by how everything came together. It was a rather unusual combination that just worked.

I really enjoyed the swordfish due to how deeply charred it was.

One thing that my friend and I do at the end of these types of meals is to rank the dishes. Something that he pointed out with this establishment was that the variance of the enjoyment of our dishes was actually quite low—our favorite dish was not too far away from our least favorite dish. This observation I believe perfectly encapsulates the experience to be had here: everything is very well executed, and it’s unlikely that any individual item will leave one unsatisfied.

I give this place my recommendation, but be sure to make a reservation in advance.

this place is such a gem! i love how intimate and cozy it felt, it was perfect for date night. highlights on the menu were the baguette with seaweed butter (so good), yellowfin tuna with blood orange & avocados, and the apricot cake (a must). will have to come back to try their spring menu next.

The ambience at Cafe Kestrel is lovely — warm and stylish. We sat at the bar, though, and it honestly felt more like sitting at a workstation than a comfortable dining spot. The music throughout the night was great, but since the speakers were right above our heads, we had to raise our voices to talk.

We both really enjoyed the wines — they were well chosen and paired nicely with our meal. Unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to the setting or the prices. The fried mussels were drenched in oil to the point that you could barely taste the mussels. The salad verte was the best dish of the night, and the beans with anchovies were also very tasty.

We also ordered the scallops, chicken with dates, and trout, but every single dish was heavy with oil. We ended up drinking a ton of water just to get rid of the greasy coating in our mouths. When I walked by the kitchen on the way to the restroom, I noticed other plates going out looked the same — all shimmering with oil.

Overall, the vibe and wine are great, but the food quality and execution really miss the mark for the price. Hopefully they can refine the cooking, because the place itself has a lot of potential.

We visited here following the 13th annual momo crawl in Jackson Heights which this establishment did not participate in in 2025. Looking forTibetan cuisine on Yelp, this place came up.  There are actually 2 locations on the same street, right across from each other. One location upstairs and the other on ground level. This is for the newer ground level spot.
Small dining area, but 1 or 2  tables for groups available.
Full bar and bottled bear selection.
This are some tradional Tibetan dishes,and they do have momo,  but dishes seem more a fusion of the Himalayan regions and and other fare.
I really wanted to try the laphing appetizer, a spicy, cold noodle dish. I liked the texture of the noodles. The filling was super hot! I am not sure if chili oil was the only thing inside, but seemed like it was.
We also had the stirred fried beef with radish which did have a nice flavor,  although some of the meat slices were chewy. The chicken lollipops, which were originally ordered dry, came to the table with sauce and were not dry. The owner seemed perturbed with us, asking us if we were sure we ordered it dry. They took it back. The other main dish came out and the correct chicken dish took a good amount of time to arrive.
Service was cold. There were no checks ins and we did feel a little ignored and had to ask for drink refills and the check when someone walked by. We were told the check had to be paid at the bar (it was never brought to our table) but when going to pay, no one was at the bar. Little confusing.
I did not look carefully enough at the check to see if the automatic 18% tip was charged as other reviews pointed out. We left a generous cash tip.
Cozy atmosphere and the restroom was relatively clean.

First of all people need to understand food and culture. There isn’t a “maitre d” here this is a homely hole in the wall with great food. If you sant to be waited on hand and food this isn’t the place for you. If you appreciate good food and culture this is a perfect representation of such.
Authentic to it’s theme and the amazing food speaks for itself
Momo’s are amazing and juicy and bok choy and beef stir fry top tier.
Visit Eat Enjoy

Hello everyone,
I want to share one of the worst experiences I’ve had this year. I’ve been to many restaurants in my life, with both good and bad experiences, but I have never encountered service this terrible before.
•	The ordering process was a complete disaster. They didn’t even bother to listen properly, brought the wrong order twice.
•	The waiting time was ridiculous. It felt like they forgot about us, and we had to remind them multiple times.
•	The staff were extremely rude and careless. Even to simple questions, they gave cold or disrespectful answers. A smile? Forget about it.
•	The place was messy and poorly maintained. Tables were dirty and the overall atmosphere felt neglected.
•	The food quality didn’t match the price at all. The dishes were tasteless, and the portions were surprisingly small.

Honestly, this place was nothing but a waste of time and money. When you go to a restaurant, you at least expect basic respect and decent service—here, you get neither.

So my advice is: if you’re looking to enjoy a nice meal or a pleasant evening, do yourself a favor and stay away from this place. For me, it will always remain the restaurant with the worst service I have ever experienced

It’s a very simple yet pretty place. Has minimum decoration but it looks neat n clean. Service is fast n good momos we’re really good. They were with potato and Veges. A very different combo but would just slither in the mouth

Phayul Restaurant offers a cozy, albeit compact, dining experience with a lively and constantly bustling atmosphere. The space is small, and it’s common to find yourself waiting for a table, which is a good sign for their business but may cause some inconvenience for guests looking for a more relaxed experience.

The service was satisfactory, considering there was only one server handling all the tables. This may be due to the restaurant’s limited serving area, but the staff remained efficient despite the busy environment.

As for the food, it was a mixed but generally positive experience. The Chicken Shapta was delicious and cooked to perfection, while the Lhasa Chicken stood out with its rich flavors. The fried rice, while decent, didn’t particularly shine. The Momos were enjoyable, though not remarkably different from others in the city. However, the Mokthuk and shredded potato was somewhat disappointing compared to the other dishes.

Overall, Phayul Restaurant delivers on flavor with its standout dishes, but could improve on the dining experience, both in service and space. A great spot for flavorful Tibetan cuisine, especially if you’re not in a rush.

Best food, service, and quality in the neighborhood and beyond! Every dish we've had here, both dine in and take out, have been incredible. The butter chicken (it's shredded for maximum flavor), lamb chops, biryani, garlic naan, all appetizers, all the curries have been hits.

Their desserts are also underrated. You have to try their homemade pistachio ice cream and if it's on the menu, carrot pudding.

The owner and staff are warm and friendly, so you always feel welcome and taken care of. Highly recommend this spot!
We love this place — we’ve been here more than 10 times, and every time it’s a hit! Our friends enjoyed it too! We love everyone who works there! Bahut bahut dhanyavaad! 🇮🇳💛

My favorite Indian in the neighborhood, the food is always fresh, hot, and delicious. I love hoe crispy the naan is when you dine in.

This time we got the garlic naan, chicken caldeen, cardamom mix grill, lemon and garlic shrimp, and lamb potato croquettes.

A friend and I had dinner at Cardamon last week, and we both agree it was some of the best Indian food we have ever had. Very flavorful and absolutely delicious! Our experience was only made better by the restaurant team. Everyone with whom we had contact was exceedingly helpful and friendly, although special mention needs to go to Ashma, our server. She is exceptional at what she does!

This cozy neighborhood spot happens to be not only some of the best Indian fare in the area, but in the greater New York area. Never disappoints. The naan is perfection. The curries are perfectly balanced, and the saag is so thick and luxurious. Can’t wait for my next visit.

Everyday on my way to work, I would glance at the restaurant on my left named Mango Bay. It is located inside a beautiful Brownstone building. I checked the menu and decided one day I'm going to visit. Well, on 2/6/26 my work family celebrated my 65th birthday/retirement from The Brooklyn Hospital Center. The atmosphere is sheer ambience. As I sat there relaxing with my work family enjoying the smooth music, the waitress took our drink orders. We all had the Mock Drinks, the favorite was The Mango Baby. I had the ice tea with pineapple juice.   The menu had been pre-selected. Everyone had a chance to enjoy every dish that was selected. We started with the salad and short ribs, then the oxtail and two different types of rice, then the fish (becareful of the bones), then the leg of lamb with whipped sweet potatoes. Everything was delicious, everything was delicious, and again everything was delicious. Since my birthday was being celebrated I expected the "surprise" slice of cake, but nothing came. I figured, oh well, but to my surprise a whole cake was presented to me and only my work family sang happy birthday. Don't worry, this is a swank establishment, no birthday song and clapping hands by the staff. That is totally up to your peeps😄. I wish I had gotten everyone's name but from the Greeter, Waitress, Busser, Bartender  and Chef the service was very good. I highly recommend Mango Bay. We had a great meal, and a wonderful experience.

Mango Bay is a charming Caribbean-themed restaurant that truly stands out. The ambiance is delightful, with a cozy and upscale vibe that feels like a warm, inviting home. The venue features both a downstairs area and an upstairs section, which is beautifully decorated with a bookshelf and a "Do the Right Thing" sign, adding a unique touch.

The service was impeccable; our waiter was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed. As for the food and drinks, it was nothing short of exceptional My favorite drink was the Brooklyn love .The ackee and saltfish egg rolls were a standout, and the whole fish was cooked to perfection. I also enjoyed a ras pasta dish that was absolutely delicious.

We visited for a friend's celebration, and the experience was memorable for all four of us. The pricing was reasonable, making it great value for money. I thoroughly enjoyed my time at Mango Bay and will definitely return in the future.

As an afro-latino, New Yorker, and foodie, I had very high expectations for Mango Bay. There are tons of spots in Brooklyn that often sacrifice ambiance for what we actually go to the restaurants for, the food, and this place surpassed my expectations.

Starting off with the decor and ambiance, this felt like dining in an authentic NY townhouse, with art that represented the Black diaspora and the culinary experience one was going to embark on. The spiral staircase, the large windows, and the open space filled the room with some much energy and visual interest. By far one of the most well designed restaurants I've been to in some time.

For the food, this is where they really shined. Every app hit harder than the last, our favourite was between the pork ribs and the  special, baked oysters. Think oysters Rockefeller but on STEROIDS. The flavor was as if the Caribbean and high society  had a baby. And as for the pork ribs, tendernism was an understatement and the pomegranate glaze made me want to walk into the kitchen and bribe the chef for the recipe. The entrees were delicious as well, I will certainly have the braised oxtail again the next time we go, as well as the Ras and Pasta. The lamb shank was delicious but a bit too game-y for me.

Lastly, as for the service they were very attentive despite what seemed like an understaffed evening. We went 2 days before Valentines Day, what I would assume is one of the busiest days of the year, and we had to wait a bit for our waiter to get back to us a few times for orders. Someone from the staff did come check on us periodically so I can tell they take great care of their guests even at their busiest!

Overall, this was a great experience and Mango Bay has quickly shot to the top of my favourite spots to eat in my city.

Everyone in both dining rooms were dressed to impress including the very good at their jobs servers. Perfect place to bring your family and friends or enjoy date night. Watch Chef Maguette and her team rise to fame in real time, cause it’s only up from here. Well done Chef, congratulations!!

Service was moderate, they made sure to check in on our table & clear it off when needed. The prawns, red snapper, and lamb shank were the star of the show! The jollof & rice & peas rice could of had way more flavor, I would love to see the recipe change in the near future. I was also excited to get the Bronzino and Collard Greens but they said it wasn’t featured on the menu until the weekend. Its important to update your menu if you’re featuring different items for the day! I rate Mango Bay an 8/10, overall amazing food, presentation, and ambience. I’m very excited to see their journey, there is lots of potential and room for growth.

Service was great. Very friendly and patient server. However, I’m docking a star as it’s not 4.9/5 standard for food and overall experience compared to others in the city. The high rating here is little overrated. Generally good Thai but I wouldn’t travel here for Thai.

Pad see yew had no wok taste, very ordinary 3/5.

Branzino was good with a slightly spicy yellow curry sauce. Nicely grilled with crispy skin. But again I’m not blown away. 3.8/5.

Mangosteen salad had mango, nuts and shallots which was sweet and yummy. Very unique fruit blend. 4/5.

I dine at this Thai restaurant over the holidays and I can see why they were selected to be in the Michelin Guide 2025. The floral decorations and creative wallpaper give ease and relaxation to its patrons. The low lighting and music makes this a perfect opportunity for birthday celebration, date nights, or just a fancy night out with friends and/or family.

The food were phenomenal! My family and I enjoy the Ghang Phed Ped Yang (Duck Curry) the most. The curry was sweeten by the coconut milk, but it was not overly creamy. The bell peppers and basil gave it a nice kick, but did not make it too spicy. The curry was perfect with the rice and the crispy duck was tender and juicy too!

Another favorite of ours was the Kra Pow Nuer. The Short ribs are crispy and flavorful. You can definitely tastes the various seasoning and spices used.

The Crying Tiger was the dish that surprised me the most. I was worried that the grilled strip loin would be chewy or dry, but it was actually very tender and juicy! The spicy sauce was a nice touch to the meat, adding more flavor to the rice powder and fried garlic.

I was disappointed that the Ghang Som Goong (Southern Curry) was sold out. Hopefully, when I return, I will get to try it!

My friends took me here to celebrate my birthday, and everything was amazing. The food was absolutely delicious, full of flavor, and beautifully prepared. The atmosphere was great, cozy and perfect for a special occasion. The staff were very friendly and attentive, especially JB, who provided excellent service with a warm smile and made the experience even more memorable. Overall, everything was perfect. Highly recommended! 🌟🍽️

Glin Thai Bistro truly lives up to its high ratings. From the atmosphere to food quality, service, and overall value for money, everything is impressive and well above average for a neighborhood Thai spot.

Here’s what I ordered:
•Thai Dumpling: Thick and flavorful with a nicely seasoned filling. The only downside is the dipping sauce, which runs a bit too sweet.
•Chive Pancake: Crispy on the outside and soft inside. It can get a little greasy after a few bites, but the dipping sauce helps balance it out.
•Tom Yum Hotpot: Generous portion with shrimp, squid, mussels, and assorted mushrooms. The heavy use of cilantro adds a unique aroma that sets it apart from typical tom yum soups. The flavor leans slightly too sour, but overall it’s still worth trying.
•Pad Thai Goong: This was the weakest dish, not much wok aroma, and the flavor felt somewhat flat.
•Crab Curry: Packed with plenty of real crab meat and a richly flavored curry. Excellent when paired with rice, and arguably the standout dish of the meal.

Overall, Glin Thai Bistro is a solid choice for anyone seeking Thai food that’s comfortably above average in every aspect. It’s a place I’d gladly return to.

Wow! Outstanding everything! From the moment we arrived, the service was warm and attentive. The food was absolutely spectacular—bursting with incredible flavors in every single bite. You can truly taste the freshness and care that goes into each dish. The best feeling is leaving a restaurant completely satisfied yet feeling like you just enjoyed clean, high-quality food. We can’t wait to go back. Glin Thai Restaurant is a must-visit!

Walked in and luckily we were able to be seated at the bar (best to make reservations ahead even if it says there are time slots open)
The beet salad was delicious, especially with the bits of dates to add a touch of sweetness. The Caesar salad was a nice portion (not pictured). The rigatoni was excellent, really love how large the pasta was, and the sauce had a great butteriness to it; nice short rib flavor as well. The coffee and creme desert was a highlight; the description also said small lady fingers but it resembles Rice Krispies to me, either way, delicious.

To be honest I wasn’t expecting much, I think there are way too many of this kind of restaurant out there, but I was SHOCKED at how good everything was. The delicata squash tempura was FANTASTIC. It was so unassuming but the light batter leaves room for the sweetness of the squash to come through.

The focaccia was fantastic although $3 extra for a singular tablespoon of salted butter is kind of off-putting.

The half chicken was INCREDIBLE. It might’ve been the juiciest chicken I’ve ever had in my life. The fries were really well salted which is HUGE

And the spicy rigatoni is not to be slept on! Pasta was the perfect doneness and the sauce was really perfect. I was worried it would be a throwaway dish but for a classic it was UNIQUELY good.

Amazing! Can’t wait to come back
The pastas were delightful. Really loved the textures and different combinations of flavors. The menu is definitely small. It would be a better place for an intimate meal for a smaller group.

While I came just before closing after being denied service/food at Les Mars (Thai)-which closed at 10 (I arrived at 9:50) so I applaud the kitchen/bar for serving me just before kitchen closing rendering  service until the closing hour.  So had a quick meal of a Caesar Salad-excellent, Tanqueray Martini and an Iberico Pork Chop with a seared cabbage and pear soubise-very good.  I think my only observation is that if you serve a guest(s) just before closing, you accept the responsibility of giving the same service for a 7 pm reservation at nearly 11 pm walk in.  I’m a professional chef and while I’m not being as critical as in the 80’s or 90’s, service should not taper off-at the bar where I sat or  at a table to be lackluster at best.  I will return as I have always had a curiosity about this place since it opened-so I took a chance.  I’ll return at a more decent hour and Jackie-thank you.  I enjoyed my food and experience.

Daphne’s is a true neighborhood gem. I had my birthday dinner here for a group of 10 and everything was fantastic—from the vibes to the food and wine. The pasta was especially delicious and flavorful, crudo was beautiful, and pork chops were juicy and tasty.

The staff were incredibly accommodating and helpful in hosting our group, and the personalized menus were such a thoughtful + tasteful touch. A great spot for special occasions and everyday dining. Can’t wait to come back!

I came to have my birthday brunch on Saturday the 21st & wanted to sit at the bar. They had a seat waiting for me and the bartender, Lindsay, greeted me with a warm birthday welcome and a glass of Prosecco. :)

To start, the drink with the rum and lemongrass was strong but also perfectly balanced. Really enjoyed that. She made me a gin cocktail, which I also loved and the prosecco was good!

Since I was by myself, I ordered the croquettes, the shrimp & their famous french toast. The shrimp?! ORDER 2 ORDERS OF IT, insanely flavorful and an underrated dish on their menu. I wanted to lick the place. I would have loved bread with it to dip in the leftover sauce ;)
Their french toast is now made with milkbread and what a smart choice!! DIVINE! Order that. They even put a candle in it for me - again, a small gesture that meant a lot.

Shout out to Lindsay who took great care of me. She was attentive but not in your face. And she makes a fantastic cocktail! Thanks, Lindsay ;) & the manager, I forget her name, she was also very lovely and kind.

I'd like to come back and try their dinner!!!

I’ve been wanting to come to MADRE for quite a some time so I finally snagged a reservation a few weeks before. First off, the vibe inside is so cool - I love how they used the lights to give an intimate yet fun vibe. The service was great and the food was good, just good however. The lamb chops were the best dish of the nights for us but tasted like good quality chops, nothing special. The flavors were okay but I wish they did more with the dishes. The drinks were strong which is a plus, you just need one for the evening. Not sure if I’d come back or recommend someone to come out of their way for a meal. Still a great place but the food was just okay.

We sampled nearly every item on the menu and loved it all, from the creative cocktails to the delicious appetizers, entrées, and desserts. We even ordered two of the chocolate soufflés to finish the night. It was a fun evening of great food and company in a trendy Greenpoint, Brooklyn restaurant.

First & foremost, both the bartender HK & the waitress Francesca were absolutely lovely- personable & attentive without being overbearing.  On top of the amazing service, the ambiance of the place is great and the food is top notch as well.  I only tried the miso brussel sprouts & truffle croquettes but both were great.  I also had the Formula One drink which was unique and tasty as well.  Last but certainly not least, I had the soufflé which is 110% well worth the wait.  I will definitely be back again, hopefully for their brunch!

Stopped by on a weekend afternoon for a light brunch. Ordered two cocktails along with the hamachi and a salad, the cocktails were strong, and the food came out clean and delicious. Really enjoyed the whole vibe!

11/10 experience at Sarantom Thai!!!! My bestfriend recommended this restaurant for girls night being that it has 5 years straight of Michelin awards!
We didn’t have reservations just walk in and were seated within 20 minutes! All with smiles and patiences we were ready to feast!
Our waitress Cream was phenomenal, personable, and knowledgeable! She made our experience even more memorable. The cocktail glasses were too cute for words too (definitely Instagram worthy)!! As a vegetarian I was able to order plenty of options and the food was A+!

We already decided we will be coming back for another girls night! Thank you for the hospitality 🙏

Everything we tried from appetizers to entrees were amazing. The restaurant brought us back to our Thailand trip from the food to the amazing Thai hospitality. Sadly, we were too full to try their desserts, but there will be a next time. Prices are very reasonable for a Michelin Bib restaurant as well. Highly recommend but get a reservation if you can.

It was decently good but for the wait and the hype, it didn’t really live up to my expectations. Not that I was expecting too much but I thought they might have an edge over other Thai restaurants. The dishes were still tasty, a little on the sweeter side. Don’t think I’d actively go again but wouldn’t stop anyone from trying it out.

I came here for a weekday dinner and was seated right away. I ordered Pad See Ew noodles, fried oyster pancake, and an iced Thai milk tea. We waited about 10-15 minutes for the dishes to arrive. Everything tasted delicious. The prices were affordable. The waiter was attentive, nice, and friendly. This is a great place to check out if you’re looking for authentic Thai food.

After seeing this place all over TikTok and realizing it’s close to my house. My friend and I finally decided to try it. We arrived around 12:15 PM. Online it says reservations are recommended, but I couldn’t find any online booking option; turns out reservations are only by phone. We walked in, put our name down, and were seated within about 30 minutes.

The space is small, but the service was excellent and very welcoming.

We started with calamari, curry puffs, and a ginger lemon drink - all of them were really good. For mains, we ordered fried pork with watercress, tom yum soup, and drunken noodles. Everything was amazing - bold, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned.

For dessert, we got the fried ice cream. The portion was huge and absolutely delicious. We couldn’t finish everything, so we packed some to go.

Overall, it was a really nice experience. Great food, great service, and definitely worth the hype. Would happily come back.

Amazing gem in Bushwick. As a native New Yorker, this is the best Mexican I’ve ever had in NYC. Food combinations are stellar and pack a punch of flavor. The shrimp tacos were top notch, get those and the quesadillas with steak and also rajas leave you happy and satisfied. I wish my stomach could handle more food, I will be coming back over and over to this one.

My mom and I were visiting a family member at the nearby hospital and we wanted to get some lunch. She specifically wanted shrimp tacos and when we asked if they had them we were in luck because it was on their specials that day! We sat down around 2:30pm on a Saturday and we had a calm delicious lunch! I had the chicken tacos with some guacamole on the side. My portion was filling for me. The staff were upbeat and kind which we always love to see. I would definitely recommend a stop here!!
