The food was great, chips and salsa variety were a nice touch (loved the garlic salsa the most). Their Michelada was exquisite and extremely flavorful. The tacos and pulled pork tacos hit the spot. Service was good too — would totally come back.

Ordered here only to wait an hour and for my entire order to be incorrect. Did not receive my vegetable tamales (the main reason i placed this order) received 3 funky greasy smelly kale tacos that were squished and cold. The fish tacos were bland, greasy and squished as well. See pictures I attached. The icing on the cake is no one at this establishment apparently answers the phone.(odd for a place that sells food?) After 5 calls I decided to go through grubhub for my refund instead of trying to give them the chance to remedy this like I initially was.
Maybe some of the best Mexican food I’ve had in the entire north eastern United States. Extremely friendly staff and not a single bad item on the menu.

Bookmarked this spot for a while and finally paid a visit. I completely agree with the other reviews about the dreamy pitas — soft, fluffy, and freshly baked to perfection. The aroma alone was incredibly inviting.
Our favorite dish of the night was the special: the smoked cabbage. Such unique, layered flavors from the combination of sauces. The lamb ribs were just okay for me, a bit too sweet and saucy. The whole dorade was unfortunately disappointing; despite the heavy spices and sauces, the fish tasted quite fishy and didn’t seem very fresh.
There are still many items on the menu we didn’t get to try, like the lamb baked pita pie, so would love to be back again.

Overall rating: 4.5
Price: $62 pp (total 2x w/ tax & tip)

Leans more fusion than I was expecting. I didn’t like my drink and my waitress was able to swap it out easily. She was so sweet! Items my friend and I ordered:

- Green with Envy cocktail: 5/5 delicious
- Muhammara/ Rstd swt ppr dip: 3/5 not worth it
- Little Gem: 6/5 obsessed
- Lamb Ribs Shawarma: 3/5 too small for price

Seems to serve more seasonal items so doubt you’ll be able to get this. Recommend giving it a try!

Love this place. I’ve been 4 times and holds the crown of best Lebanese food in the city. On top of the amazing food, it’s cozy in the winter and the backyard patio in the summer is unbeatable. You can tell the owner Samaya works hard to make the place filled with amazing food and love, everyone is so sweet and welcoming.

Sawa NYC is hands down my favorite Lebanese restaurant in New York City. The moment you walk in, you’re welcomed by the warmth of their brick oven and the irresistible aroma of freshly baked pita. The staff is genuinely friendly, the décor strikes a perfect balance of simple and elegant, and the atmosphere feels cozy and inviting.

The service is warm and attentive, and the cocktails are creative, unique, and absolutely delicious. Every dish bursts with authentic Lebanese flavor. I highly recommend the Hummus, Muhammara, Tabbouleh, Batata Hara, Kafta, and Lahm Meshwi — but my absolute favorites are the Lamb Ribs and Beiruti Samke Harra.

If you’re looking for a true taste of Lebanon in NYC, this is the place to be.

Sawa has two inside seating spaces but we sat outside in the garden on a large table. The ambiance was lovely on a summer evening -  sitting under the string fairy lights as the sky darkened.
The food was delicious. We devoured 3 of the dips between six of us (my favorite was the baba gannouj) which come with warm fresh pita. We ordered extra pita for one each but I don't think it was necessary as they are large.
The tabouleh was nice and refreshing. The heirloom tomatoes were also tasty and served with a chili oil and garlic toum.
We enjoyed a few lamb dishes and all the lamb is from Australia so it tastes nice and not gamey. Lamb ribs and skewers were very good.
The whole fish was also super nice, no bones and well cooked.
The osmaliyeh was my favorite dessert.
Service was a bit slow and weirdly timed with some odd breaks between.

Tong in Bushwick is where you go to experience authentic Thai small plates known as kub klaem. The sleek dining room wrapped in rustic metal walls captures that raw NYC energy while still feeling clean and cozy with lighting that mirrors how vibrant the food tastes. Tong does not hold back on spice and a simple medium Thai spicy is no joke, definitely not for first timers and even seasoned spice lovers might find it daring but that heat brings out the true and unapologetic deliciousness of Thailand. From cocktails to small plates everything is thoughtfully crafted and plated like edible art. If you love Thai cuisine or crave bold spicy flavors, Tong is the perfect spot for incredible food creative drinks and warm hospitality with genuine smiles that go the extra mile.

Came here to say with my brother and his finance. Pretty nice restaurant. The prices were decent. Large portion sizes. The tom yum soup was amazing. It was spicy but full of flavor and texture. I had the green curry with tofu and it was one of the best I have ever had. The curry was smooth and the rice was fresh and not sticky. I’m he tofu was the perfect texture for the broth. My brother and his fiancé got the drunken noodles and I know they loved it because they finished the bowl.

Went on a date night to Tong, a Thai restaurant in Bushwick recognized by the Michelin Guide. Because of how popular it has become, it’s definitely best to make a reservation ahead of time since the space fills up quickly and many people come specifically for the food.

The atmosphere makes it a really nice date spot. Dim lighting, warm wooden tables, and thoughtful plating give it an intimate feel without being overly formal, and the staff were warm and welcoming from the moment we walked in.

To start, I ordered the Jolean cocktail made with gin, lychee, butterfly pea flower, orange blossom water, lime, and egg white. It was light, floral, and well balanced, with the egg white giving it that silky foam texture. My boyfriend kept it classic with a Thai iced tea, served in a mason jar with the familiar gradient of dark tea and creamy milk that gives it that rich sweetness and deep caramel color.

For appetizers we started with the Som Tum Thai, one of Thailand’s most iconic salads. Traditionally from the Isan region in northeastern Thailand, som tum is all about balancing the four core Thai flavor elements: sour, spicy, sweet, and salty. The dish came with long strands of shredded green papaya piled high with peanuts, cherry tomatoes, long beans, dried shrimp, fresh chili, and a wedge of lime on the side. The green papaya itself is mild and crunchy, almost like a vegetable version of a green apple, which makes it perfect for soaking up the lime heavy dressing. The dried shrimp added a deep umami note while the peanuts gave it texture. It was refreshing but still packed with flavor, with the dressing lightly pooling at the bottom so everything could be tossed together.

We also ordered the Truffle Spring Rolls, filled with glass noodles, shiitake mushrooms, and oyster mushrooms. Glass noodles, made from mung bean starch, absorb flavor really well and give that slightly chewy texture that works perfectly inside crispy spring rolls. The mushroom filling was earthy and rich, and the truffle added an aromatic depth that made it feel slightly more elevated than a typical vegetable roll. The fry was clean and crisp without feeling greasy, which made them really enjoyable.

For mains, I ordered the Pad Cha Talay, a seafood stir fry known for being bold and aromatic. Pad cha refers to a style of stir fry loaded with herbs and spices that create a fragrant, slightly spicy dish. This one had shrimp, squid, and mussels with bamboo shoots, eggplant, long beans, kaffir lime leaf, fresh green peppercorn clusters, and krachai, also known as fingerroot, a traditional Thai herb with a peppery, ginger like aroma. The seafood was cooked well and the vegetables still had a nice bite to them. The bamboo shoots and eggplant absorbed the sauce nicely, while the fresh peppercorns added small bursts of spice throughout the dish. It was served with a dome of fluffy jasmine rice that paired perfectly with the aromatic sauce.

My boyfriend ordered the Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup from the Chiang Mai region known for its rich coconut curry broth and the contrast between soft noodles and crispy noodles on top. Flavor wise, the broth was really delicious, warm, creamy, and comforting. However, the presentation and balance could definitely be improved. The chicken was mostly hidden under the broth and noodles, and the portion leaned heavily toward noodles compared to the bean sprouts and other components. If the ingredients were distributed more evenly, visually showing the chicken, noodles, and bean sprouts, it would elevate both the presentation and the overall balance of the dish.

Service overall was great, though water refills could have been a little more attentive.

For a restaurant recognized by Michelin, the food here is already strong in terms of flavor and execution, but there are small areas where things could be elevated further, particularly presentation and balance in certain dishes. With a few refinements, it could better match the level that the pricing suggests. I would definitely come back to try more of the menu.

Food was ok, not the most flavorful, warm. I would not come back. Great service though

Update: upon paying the waitress was rude and annoyed at us asking for a fork. It was the reason why I lowered my score.

Get the oysters! They have an amazing sauce and garnish which sets them apart from other places. The Massaman curry was also different than other Thai places and the shrimp curry was perfect. I think this place is comparable to some of the other famous Thai places in the city

Good food and a nice atmosphere. I do wish the Szechuan food was a little more spicy, but the dishes we got, like Shrimp with silken tofu, Szechuan fish fillet with tofu, Dan Dan noodles, and Green Beans was very good. Prices are a little high and portions were small compared to Flushing, but the difference was not extravagant, and for three people we were able to be full for about $90 pre-tip, which is respectable.

Spent a chill late afternoon here.
The cocktail is soooooo good! Highly recommended.
The Chinese food is authentic although the chicken dish is bit plain. Tofu with beef is the best one out of the 5 dishes we ordered.

I had a such a satisfying experience here. Everything tasted freshly made and well-prepared. The mapo tofu stood out the most. Soft tofu in a rich, savory sauce with just the right amount of numbing Sichuan spice. I also got the ma-la wontons another favorite Everything felt well-seasoned, comforting, and combined with the quick, efficient service, HUPO is definitely a place I’d return to when I’m craving bold, comforting Chinese food done right!

been going here for years but the portions have gotten so much smaller... Not sure if I can justify the price anymore.

Ordered a dry Hotpot for $36! This was the portion. Laughable. 3 pieces of beef, 3 pieces of fish tofu and some mushroom. Will never be ordering here again.

11.19.2025 Update after the restaurant’s response:

The claim that these were “enoki mushroom fibers” is simply not accurate. The pieces we found were inside the fish meat, not in the broth, and were removed by pulling them out of the flesh. Cooked enoki does not appear as a single long, round, elastic tube — nor can it be extracted intact from inside a piece of fish.

We found multiple pieces with the same worm-like appearance and texture, all inside the fish flesh. These characteristics are completely inconsistent with mushrooms and entirely consistent with parasites commonly found in raw fish before cooking. Throw the picture to GPT and you will see it is parasite.

This is clearly a raw fish sourcing issue. We are not unreasonable customers; we just want restaurants to take food safety seriously and not dismiss concerns by attributing them to unrelated ingredients. I hope this feedback helps improve transparency and handling of similar situations in the future.

Original post: parasite in fish, called the restaurant, they were not surprised, only told us to refund with Uber…

Delicious delicious delicious. I’m so glad we decided to dine here on our trip. The food was phenomenal. I don’t think there is a bad thing on the menu. The tortellini and the lasagna were so good. The fish was fresh and so yummy. The polenta bread with the chili butter was so good and the mortadella was delish as well.

I went there earlier when it first opened and they had their fresh pasta market. But I recently came back for my birthday and was pleasantly surprised on how everything tasted. Definitely get each of the polenta bread as the appetizers are small portion sizes. I had the ravioli pasta dish and it was only like 8 pieces which was disappointing of a portion size. Food was however delicious. They also do not do complimentary dessert.

My best friend and I have been frequenting Rolos since we watched that one video about how their lasagna is made. It's been a special treat when we can manage to get a table (one that's well worth the wait).

The staff here is truly incredible. A lot of restaurants in the city can be condescending and rude, but the entire staff at Rolos is beyond kind and accommodating.

If you're able to snag a res, which we were today, you're in for a real treat. When I put in the res notes that this would be our last dinner together given my leaving NYC, the staff made it truly special!

Standout dishes: chili polenta bread, cheeseburger, skirt steak, and of course, the lasagna!

While we went back and forth about where to have our "last supper" as our server called it, we knew Rolo's was the only right choice. The food is always consistent, outstanding, and a memorable experience.

I couldn't have imagined a better way to close out my NY days. Thank you so much to the Rolos staff for such a considerate, caring, and extraordinary experience.

Made reservations walked in and was pleasantly surprised..this is a busy establishment reservations are recommended..Natalie who was our waitress was an absolute doll. So informative with a wealth of knowledge about the food. The food hands down was a ten out of ten. We ordered the crispy potatoes for the table, yum and yum. A second order was made immediately don't judge. I ordered the eggs with the polenta bread sooo good.my friend ordered the French toast which was to die for..need I say more. The food is very filling and so very delicious.

For a relatively small brunch menu, I was impressed by the diversity of dishes - from more traditional brunch items to some Asian-inspired touches, it serves a wide palette and consistently delivered. The cocktails were also amazing! I loved the espresso martini (surprisingly heavy on the espresso, but not in a bad way) and the carrot drink (tasted like a health juice, also not in a bad way). Definitely deserves the hype and will be back to try other food + drink items.

Noel was more than accommodating this evening. Give that man a raise. Your polenta fries were outstanding. The beet and farro salad perfection. The half red half spicy vodka topped the list. I would dare someone to eat this pizza and not fall in love. Welcome to the neighborhood.

Seppe Pizza Bar in lower Manhattan is great. Friendly service, with all hands available to keep guests comfortable and happy. The menu is creative and the food never fails to delight. Everything I've tried so far has been well prepared and thoughtfully presented. And the House pies? To die for. My faves are the Aunt Honey and the Spicy Vodka. The wine list offers a good range, and the cocktails are creative and delicious. Seppe is a sure bet if you're looking for a good place for appetizers, pizza, and a nice dining experience.

We enjoyed this restaurant so much, we went back the next day! Pizza was amazing, bolognese and cacio Pepe were delicious! Staff were very attentive and friendly! We went as a family of six and everyone was happy!
Have a great pizza! Not New York pizza but great pizza nonetheless. Great ambience, excellent service from Thatcher, excellent wine. Right behind our hotel.

Had a big afternoon party for the end of our daughter's soccer season. I was immediately impressed by the design and ambiance of the restaurant. Food was great and staff were super friendly and attentive. Will be going back often!

This was easily one of the best steaks I’ve tried. I’ve had similar preparations in many places, but this one truly stood out.
From the moment I walked in, the aroma of smoke and perfectly cooked meat immediately caught my attention and set the tone for the experience.

The atmosphere is very pleasant and comfortable, making the whole visit even more enjoyable.
I left very satisfied and will definitely be coming back again.🥩❤️

WHAT DO THEY DO TO THIS NACHO CHEESE DIP TO MAKE IT SO PERFECT?! It’s perfect. I’d never order this of my own will but my friend ordered it and what a great decision that was.
The cornbread is great.
All the meat is great.

A 1/2 lb of meat per person is definitely enough, especially if you get 1-2 sides.

This isn’t the cheapest spot. 2 sides and 2 1/2 lbs of meat was $75 (fed 2 people and was a lot of food).

I LOVE that they have Stiegl! And they have special really great mugs for the radlers.

Lots of seating. There was a long line on a Saturday at 7pm and it moved slow.

Absolute hands down best BBQ joint in NY and perhaps best I’ve ever had. All the hype about Hometown is on point. Super casual and super friendly staff. You have the choice of both indoor and outdoor seating.

Every item on their menu is to die but the ultimate is the pastrami sandwich. YES you heard me right! This sandwich is even better than Katz’s. More bark, more tender, juicier and let’s not forget the buttered rye bread.

Bottom line, there is not a single item on their menu that is not worth devouring.

10/10 experience. Food, drinks and service, seriously all outstanding. I like the laid-back atmosphere and the fact that they have good quality napkins. Meat was beautifully cooked and so flavorful. The sides? Perfection. As a  southwestern girl I could dream of nothing better. And they were playing steely dan 💯

The brisket and ribs are melt-in-your-mouth and fall-off-the-bone and juicy. Perfect American BBQ. The pastrami bacon is worth it and full of char flavor. We loved the cornbread and the mac and cheese. Atmosphere is very southern. A bit pricey but definitely the best BBQ you can find anywhere in and near the city.

Absolutely, undeniably, incredibly spectacular!! We had 7:30PM reservations on 12/27 with two adults and three kids. Joe was so nice and kind; he knew us by name because we made the reservation directly with him. Nonna Maria herself greeted us and told us a bit about her. She was delightful! We ordered her perfectly made meatballs and scrumptious lasagna. We also ordered from the Puerto Rican menu (fried fish cod — it was delicious). The food was fantastic, the wait staff precise and friendly and the atmosphere was everything we expected. Our recommendation is to contact them via phone because reservations are always needed (and rightfully so — the food and people are amazing). This is worth every penny and we will be coming back again!  Remember!! It’s cash only! Thank you Joe & company!

We came in during the snowstorm getting lucky calling for a last minute reservation. If you have not been here please go. What a  idea to have different foods prepared by Nonnas. A delicious opportunity to try unique dishes from all over the world. The service was just beyond warm and inviting. I cannot wait to come back- already looking at the Nonnas calendar. YUMIKO thank you for coming and chatting with us- the chicken Katsu just wow- it was a privilege to meet you. We loved seeing you in the kitchen prepping!!  Everyone there was lovely. The burrata was so beyond creamy, basil so fresh, the meatballs were like my grandma made them - really I do not have enough words for this review !!!! Please go try. Staten Island gem.

I first heard about this place from a documentary, then saw the movie last year, had to make sure I got over to Staten Island for a bite. The food offered today was Italian, Japanese and Sri Lankan. It all looked amazing. The owner is still taking non-stop calls for reservations.  I was lucky to have gotten in since I came in on my own. I was sat at the counter and enjoyed watching all of the hustle and bustle in this cozy kitchen. The size helps you feel like you're waiting for your Mama to finish cooking your meal as you watch.
I ordered the lasagna which was very good, but really, the star of the meal was the fresh banana pudding. Never have I enjoyed such a delicious, creamy, well-balanced and fresh pudding. It was divine.
The cost is a little high but it is so worth it for the freshness. They serve some alcohols but they offer good pairings for the meals offered.
I am so happy to have been able to enjoy this meal I had waited so long for.
They only take cash and for now reservations are done in person or by phone. From what I heard they will soon have an online platform to do these. Also, they only take reservations on a rolling, monthly basis. If you get to go, I hope you enjoy it too.

The heart warming film staring an amazing cast made us want to come here to see it in ‘real life’ all the way from the UK 🇬🇧
It did not disappoint. We were greeted by the fabulous owner ‘Joey’ and we got to meet today’s ‘Nonnas’ who were cooking.
The food was of the highest quality and the service was second to none.
We had the Mozzarella starter which was beautifully presented and tasted superb.
For mains we had the lasagna and meatballs again absolutely top notch!
THIS FOOD IS MADE WITH LOVE ❤️ and that’s the difference…….
The wine is of excellent quality and it truly represents great value for money 💰
The service again gets a 10 out of 10 for us so well done 👏
We enjoy good  food and wine and Nonnas was as good if not better than anything we could ask for! Thank you Joey for your beautiful concept and following your dreams!
You are an inspiration.

Imagine a simpler time. You’re at your Italian friend’s grandmother’s house, where dinner is made the slow way because there’s nowhere else to be. It’s a long weekend, time is generous. You’ve already had her signature tipple, the one she still argues about with her doctor, and a little wine she schlepped back from Napoli.
Her Trini friend drops by, bringing family recipes and big energy, sharing stories and food with her adopted New Yorker grandkids (you and your goober friends). This table is everything: cozy, welcoming, eclectic.
You eat a hearty meal. She teaches you how to eat lamb brains, how to get every last bit of meat from the head. When you finish, she tells you she’s proud of you.
Then the bill comes, and some of the magic slips away. You take a little home with you.
This is what the world is supposed to be: a place where people are welcomed in, where differences are shared, and where you leave more open, more curious, more human than when you arrived. There’s plenty for everyone. We just have to learn how to share.

This is such a beautiful place with amazing traditional Sri Lankan décor that makes the dining experience feel special. The atmosphere is warm and unique.

I had the lumpice and kiri pani, and both were superb. The lumpice was very flavorful, not too spicy, and wrapped perfectly in a banana leaf. Everything tasted fresh and authentic. The kiri pani was creamy and lightly sweet, a perfect dessert.

Highly recommend Lakruwana if you want authentic Sri Lankan food in NYC

When I first saw the exterior of this restaurant, I was absolutely intrigued. The ornate carvings, majestic statues, and shimmering golden doors beckoned me to come in. The place was crowded and everyone seemed to be enjoying their meal.

Upon being seated in one of the elaborate chairs, I had to pause and take in the visual feast around me. The cozy interior was adorned with 360 degree of stunning ornate collectibles from Sri Lanka, exquisite tchotchkes adorning the walls and hanging from the ceilings, creating a continuous visual stimulus.

The hostess greeted me and explained that I could either scan the menu code or enjoy the wonderful lunch buffet for $21. (Since I visited during the weekend lunch hour, I'm unsure if the price changes at other times.) Noticing that everyone else was enjoying the buffet, I decided to follow suit, and I'm so glad I did.

I'm a huge fan of Sri Lankan cuisine, and the buffet was a delight. They have hot entrées in shallow cauldrons that are constantly being refilled. The spread consisted of many vegetarian delights alongside a few meat entrées, such as deviled chicken and pork curry. My personal favorites were the eggplant, dal lentils, and the kale and coconut salad. Their papadam was light and delicious, so definitely don't skip those! Along another wall, the dessert station featured sago, chocolate, caramel, mango, and gooseberry puddings. The latter two were my absolute favorites.
A pleasant Sri Lankan authentic spot on staten island.  Nicely decorated with delicious food and pleasant service. I suggest to visit. Enjoy!

An amazing exotic atmosphere adds to your dining experience. Food is presented well and almost like eating art. Friendly staff. It would have been better if the waitress could have explained the dishes. As a 1st time , it was tasty and well presented. I’d like to try the buffet to be able to experience a variety of options.

We had a great time here! We went for the buffet and got to try a bunch of different dishes — everything was super tasty. The coconut curry was definitely a highlight, so flavorful and comforting. Prices were really reasonable too, especially for the variety you get. Plus, the interior is beautiful — cozy, stylish, and full of character. We’ll definitely be coming back!

My wife Yuni and I walked by Il Gigante out of curiosity, and one day finally decided to take a break from work and try it. We only had a short time to dine, but we were so glad we did. The pasta was incredible.

A week later, we were craving brunch and looked at a few spots, but honestly, we just wanted to go back. That’s when I met their lasagna, and it completely won me over. We went back again the next weekend with my in-laws just so I could have it again. We all shared our plates, as you should at an Italian restaurant, and every dish was fantastic.

Since then, Il Gigante has become one of our favorite places in Ridgewood. The food is amazing, but it’s the people who make it special. Everyone we’ve met has been kind, genuine, and welcoming.

When you work long, stressful hours, meals like this remind you to slow down and enjoy life. Ridgewood’s lucky to have a place like this.

Ps. They’re very dog friendly!

A divine dining experience. The friendliest staff. Amazing dishes. Phenomenal wine list. Cozy, warm interior. Baby friendly (they brought us a high chair) and babe loved the meatballs. Do not miss the cotoletta, it’s unreal. We were very excited to find a place with northern Italian dishes — the gramigna alla sasiccia is absolutely incredible! A solid choice to end on the panna cotta. We will be back again and again.

Il Gigante has a piece of my heart. It genuinely feels like a home away from home. The kind of place where you walk in for the first time but you’re treated like a regular.

And that doesn’t just “happen.” You can feel the care in every detail, the consistency, the hours, the pride. It’s the kind of spot that reminds you what hospitality is supposed to feel like.

If you haven’t been, go soon. If you have, go back and bring someone you love.

So happy I finally tried this place! Came here on a recommendation from a friend and it did not disappoint! Our server Elena was brilliant - take her reccomendations when you come! We let her decide our appetisers and they were just fantastic! The pecorina salad was my favourite. The food was so good that, as a vegetarian, I was even tempted to try the lasagna and it was so good. Don’t skip the drinks, the espresso martini and Bianco spritz were 10/10. Will definitely be back.

Wow, I am blown away! Firstly, when I walked in the door I loved the ambiance. Felt like a real classic NY joint (similar to Eddie’s Sweet Shop, iykyk). The service was impeccable- we had a really sweet waiter and bus staff. Each of our dishes were delicious and they have a specials menu, which I appreciate. Each dish was simple yet full of flavor. Next time I’ll have to try the drinks!

3 out of 5 stars

Rose Marie has a super cozy atmosphere and the kind of warm, welcoming energy you want from a neighborhood spot in Williamsburg. The staff was genuinely great and made us feel right at home the entire time.

I came in knowing they are well known for the patty melt, but we didn’t try it on this visit. I went with a drink to start and it was a little watered down for me, so I ended up switching to a beer which worked out better.

For food, the pork chop had good flavor but it was slightly overcooked and could have used a bit more seasoning. A sprinkle of flaked sea salt would have lifted the whole dish. Portions overall felt like they could be a touch bigger. The little gem salad was fine but missing something. Some beets for contrast would have helped, and the cheese they used didn’t really complement the greens.

The chicken cutlet was really solid. Crispy and well seasoned, but it still felt like it needed one more element. Honestly it would shine in a brioche bun as a sandwich.

Overall it was a decent first visit but a little underwhelming. I would come back to try more items on the menu because the place itself feels great and the service was excellent. Just hoping the food hits a bit stronger next time.

I know this is popping up on all the lists right now but it is soooo deserved. The patty melt was really spectacular and so are the potatoes. It’s sort of classic American food but done so well. Everything is full of flavor and I loved my pickled tomato martini! Definitely a great addition to the neighborhood!

Overall thoroughly enjoyed my experience here! It was a really busy night so we walked in and sat at the bar. Can’t remember the bartender’s name, but he was such a fun person to chat with. Also really kind. There was one drink with gin that I didn’t end up liking and he switched it for the passionfruit spritz (10/10 drink).

My friend got the patty melt, which was solid dish for $18. The star of the night was 100% the flounder perfectly fried and the sauce was everything.

Would also recommend the corn and loaded potatoes for apps

Loved everything about this place! The food, atmosphere, wine, and service! We had the absolute pleasure to be served my Margret! She was amazing, attentive and welcoming. She really elevated our experience. The food was divine, the party melt was next level and all must try.
Amazing spot! Everything is delicious, but the saltine crusted cod and the olive oil cake with whipped marscapone, cherries and vanilla ice cream was incredible!

Loved our dinner at Hungry Thirsty. Every dish was incredibly flavorful, loved the pad krapow and moo waan. They aren’t joking about the spice levels they denote, so if you’re sensitive Mae sure you pay attention. They have a really large beer menu, so you have plenty of fun options to choose from to break the heat. The service is fast and super friendly. They seem to change the menu often, looking forward to trying more of their wonderful dishes!

We stopped into Hungry Thirsty on a freezing night, and boy did they warm us up! The people are so genuine and welcoming, and the food does not disappoint! It’s some of the most authentic Thai in the city, the chef specials are to die for, and the spice level is real. If you wanna go to Thailand, but not spend the money on the ticket, this is the place for you!!!

The menu was unlike any other Thai place I’ve ate at before. The branzino dish was phenomenal with perfectly crunch garlic topping and a zesty sweet sauce. The prawns were massive and paired very well with the tamarind s sauce. Our server Sherlyn was very kind and helped us navigate our dietary restrictions and provided great recommendations. Loved this meal and will be back to try other things.
Food is authentic as it could be! Can’t wait to try their other dish in the menu. Good selection of dishes and very friendly staff! Will definitely come back :)

Service was quick friendly, on a Friday evening, food however was not as good as ugly baby (The prior store) I was expecting great things from the reviews and the michellin guide and all but was let down. Everything we ordered was quite sweet overall. Not alot of savory or tartness that the food needs. They did give us a complimentary soup which was nice but still quite sweet.

It’s great for shareable plate and date night, so get 4-6 dishes will be idea! We loved salad, freshly grated cheese created a umami taste and it was very refreshing! Pork was juicy and tender which we also enjoyed. Ragu was alright - way too al dente and salty in our opinion.

We LOVED our dinner experience in their cutest backyard, super peaceful and memorable! We also really enjoyed the food, the butter was out of this world, the baguette was amazing, the eggplant sesame dip was delicious, the smoked date provolone farinata was insane, the Caesar salad was perfect, the cabbage dish was soooo mouthwatering and my favourite dish of all, followed by the bean purée and the crazily yummy sourdough bread next to it as rank two! I didn’t try the rib chops but my friends were dying for it loool
The only thing I didn’t like (but the rest of tbh party did) was the trout crudo, for which I blame Theodora for shooting my expectations for crudos to the roof! Also I couldn’t get my head around the price for that little amount of harissa, which wasn’t even that special, neither were the fries (and this one, everyone else was on the same page as me)
Oh and there was this empanada shaped dumpling bread dish that we loved but don’t recall the name.
Overall, we really enjoyed our meal and we will be back :)

Delicious and refreshingly original take on lunch and brunch. Every dish is refined and inventive, blending different cuisines and flavors in a way that really works. Most of our dishes had a subtle kick.
The experience felt energizing compared to the usual predictable brunch scene.

Very interesting place with not too big, but very creative menue. You better ask the server or Google some terms that they using to describe their dishes. But don't get me wrong,  this sophistication matches the taste. Everything including bread was a top notch.  Personally my favorites were the pasta, skate wing and the pork. Unfortunately I was so full that had no space for a dessert,  but from what other people having it looked very interesting.  The place has inside seating as well as outside on the backyard.  They are quite popular so reservation is highly recommended.
Delicious food, we were 5 people and got around 10-12 dishes as our server recommended. Everything beautifully made & ever sauce that came with the dishes was 10/10

Pierozek is one of my favorite polish spots in the neighborhood. The food is consistently great and their servers are always patient and friendly. It’s awesome they do local collabs on pierogis. Solid vodka selection. The interior is adorable and warm. Their weekend special grill bowl is my favorite on the menu. In the warmer months, their back patio space is quiet and chill.

This was my first time having pierogis. This spot was so cute, clean, menu was comprehensive and not overwhelming. I was recommended to try the cheese & potato first; which were a generous 6! There was a side of sour cream and sour cream with dill. They were so delicious and filling I only got through half. I ended up ordering other pierogis to go (Bacon & jalapeño and pork), which were also delicious. The staff were friendly smiling and attentive. Menu reasonably priced. They have a cute back patio lots of seating indoor; clean, cute and id definitely come back!

A wonderful dining  experience.  The kielbasa and pierogies  were delicious!  The pierogies are made on premise and the kielbasa is made in NJ.

The restaurant is small and nicely decorated.    The staff is friendly and efficient.  This is a Michelin rated restaurant and certainly worthy of their rating.

I highly recommend this  restaurant in “Little Poland” in Greenpoint

Absolutely delicious! Pierozek is such a gem — everything tastes homemade and full of love. The pierogi are soft, flavorful, and perfectly balanced (you can tell they use quality ingredients). The staff is warm, welcoming, and happy to share recommendations. The atmosphere is cozy, making it feel like a little slice of Poland right here in the city. Whether you’re a pierogi lover or trying them for the first time, this place will win you over. Highly recommend the potato & cheese pierogi and the dessert options — pure comfort food heaven!

As most polish people I’m in love with pierogi and was missing a great ones in US.
We went at dinner time and we get table with no problem. The food is amazing we tried pierogi and red borscht with sauerkraut croquet it was to die for.
Can’t wait to visit again! Thank you for great service!

Food was phenomenal. Portions were kinda small for the price (everything is pricey ) I recommend the ceviche appetizer and the rice with seafood was amazing.

One server was super nice but the one with the long hair had an attitude. Then there's the whole, machine is broken cash only thing which was not cool. Other than that the decor is amazing.

The chef is crazy. The food even crazier...in the BEST way. Ceviche second to none...can and do drink the tigers milk by the glass. Chicken? Stupid tasty, marinated with peruvian magic. Pisco sours are very solid. The ambiance feels like being transported to a different realm, forgetting one is in queens and not lima, peru.
My wife and I went to Caleta 111 and had the ceviche mixto,and the arroz con mariscos. The food was amazing. I haven't had ceviche that was so fresh in a long time.

Ordered ceviche mixto, arroz de mariscos and lomo saltado for take out. I’m Peruvian and this food was awful. The lomo tasted like vinegar and it didn’t come with rice. The ceviche didn’t taste authentic at all. And the worst dish was the arroz de mariscos. Soggy rice and barely any flavor. This place is overhyped. The worst part is how expensive the food was

Caleta 111 is a culinary gem in Richmond Hill!

This place NEVER disappoints. My husband and I have dined here a few times, and have ordered takeout just as much. Honestly, if I could eat this every day, I would.

The menu offers a journey through vibrant, sometimes unexpected, yet surprising flavors and thoughtful dishes. My personal favorites are the Tiger's Milk, Lomo Saltado, Chica Morada, and cancha - which is a perfect snack on its own! The Tiger' Milk is an explosion of fresh, tangy and savory flavors that excite the palate, while the Lomo Saltado is the ultimate comfort food - perfectly seasoned, tender, and packed with bold flavors.

If you're looking for something different, order the Chaufa de Mariscos. From the very first bite, we got instant dopamine hits - the unexpected flavors were a sensory experience that left us saying "ooh!" with each bite.

Don't leave without ordering the Chicha Morada. Its a definite must-have. This refreshing, cold Peruvian purple corn drink is lightly sweet with hints of cinnamon and clove that make you feel at home. It's like a non-alcoholic mulled wine, but better - comforting and reminiscent of Christmas, pure perfection in a glass.

[I think they rotate desserts, but if the Peruvian ice cream is on the menu, definitely try it. I'll be back to try the others.]

The staff is always attentive and friendly. Whether it's your first time or 10th time, they'll ensure you have a great experience. If you're unfamiliar with something on the menu, ask and they're more than happy to explain and recommend dishes that suit your tastes. This definitely adds to the cozy vibes of the restaurant.

The decor is another standout feature, most of it seemingly handmade - I think I've seen them working on a few pieces in the past (I live in the neighborhood). Every detail feels intentional, with a personal touch that perfectly complements the amazing food.

From the appetizers, to the desserts, you can taste the quality and care that the chefs put into every item on the menu. Whether you're dining in or ordering takeout, Caleta 111 is more than a meal - it's a flavorful adventure I know I'll return to  time and time again.

Got the chicken, mashed potatoes and sautéed greens platter $20. A bit overpriced for portion size.

I don’t like how you can’t seamlessly sub out different sides without incurring lots of extra cost.

Additionally the house made aioli doesn’t seem to be the right dipping sauce for the chicken if it doesn’t come with crispy potatoes or fries or anything.

The sautéed greens were fairly tasteless but the mashed potatoes were good. I def recommend that.

I picked up dinner to go, the platter with roasted chicken and everything was amazing. It was a lot of food so ended up making two meals out of it. I especially loved the hummus and cauliflower that was included. The food is well worth the price and it's a super cute place inside.
Love! Our food was amazing, and we will be back! The chicken and waffles are...*chef's kiss* and I highly recommend stopping by for brunch.

I could eat this place every day. Hands down one of the Best restaurants in New York. Juicy Rotisserie chicken .. Best Mac and cheese ...roasted veggies... creamed mashed potatoes. Love the dining and atmosphere.  Everyone super friendly.

Food was great! We tried a good variety of the menu items. They were attentive to dietary restrictions and made sure the dishes we had were without sugar. The bowl called The Healthy One was very filling and had nice flavors. We especially liked how they cooked The plantains. The backyard seating area was lovely and unique.

I stopped in here with a group of 4 on Saturday for brunch, our group had a reservation and was seated promptly. The server came to our table not to long after we were seated and took our drink orders. We ordered beers, coffees and Bloody Marys ,which were the star of the show. As for food we ordered the chicken Caesar sandwhich, quiche, chicken liver pate, gigante beans, pancakes and chips with aioli. The star of the show was the chicken liver pate, it had a great rich savory flavor with a hint of sweetness and was served on a nice soft piece of sourdough. The Scottie Pippen of the food order had to be the pancakes, they were savory and sweet with a hint of lemon. The only weak link of the bunch was the under seasoned gignate beans, which had an off day. Would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a brunch spot in WB or Greenpoint.

I really enjoyed this place a lot. The screw driver with tangerine juice was awesome and strong. The waiter was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu. The country pate looked kind of like spam but tasted magical. The chips (French fries) and aioli was outstanding reminded me of the ones at 4 Charles or Au Cheval. The Shakshuka egg and tomatoes was fire too. The sausage biscuit in the gravy was really good. The star of the show however was the pancakes they were perfect. Crispy edges but fluffy and the perfect amount of syrup. The cutlet that was with the Cesar salad was awesome too. I definitely would return.

Finally got here for one of their famous brunches and completely lived up to the hype. The food was outstanding, the sausage gravy and biscuits was pepper, creamy delicious with every bite. Honestly every plate that arrived on every table looked magazine quality.

The service and atmosphere were perfect for a group or table for two. Looking forward to coming back again and again

Been here for both brunch and dinner. Love the elevated takes on simple, European-style dishes.

My pork shoulder this evening came out purple and impossible to cut. The team happily refired it, delivering a dreamingly tender cut with a deep pink blush. Beautiful piece of meat in the end, and they even took it off our check. Thanks for being on top of it. Duck was beautiful too.

Can't wait to come back for another neighborhood meal.

We all agreed that the pancakes were good for first bite, but afterwards it was just too heavy and oily from the butter. Maybe some people love it, but it’s too much for me 😮‍💨

I did like the fries though..but overall the experience was quite hectic and we felt we were somewhat being rushed.

I wasn’t a big fan of pork belly before I found this restaurant. I highly recommend to try their pork belly. So good, so good, I LOVE IT!!!!!!
Every time we went there, we ordered at least four plates of pork belly, I never get tired of their pork belly. Kimchi is great too!  The fired rice , the way the mixed the ingredients is so perfect to eat as the last meal of that moment. Also, the way the set up their grill pan makes me feel like they are taking me back to retro korean bbq spot in Kdrama.

I have been going to this spot for years. The old couple who used to own the place sold it, and currently in the hands of new owners. Great food, great vibes, reasonable prices. Wait staff is great, especially the petite Hispanic lady very attentive and generous with portions. My go to spot when I'm craving for some Pork belly bbq. 100% recommend.
Not kid friendly though, young kids / toddlers can easily burn themselves in the hot plate in the middle of the table.

We came here for lunch on a Saturday and our party of 2 was seated quickly. The service here is no frills, very to the point, getting the job done (which was fine) but I felt a bit confused at times.

For food, we got 2 servings of the pork belly, fried rice w/ cheese, and the cold noodles. Overall, I thought the food was okay. The banchans were good and had a bit of variety. The servings of the pork belly were decently sized although for the price and the area, I thought they could've been a bit bigger. If I came again, I would pass on the cold noodles - felt store bought and the ice bowl felt like a gimmick.

Another place for authentic Korean BBQ! The meat portion was not a lot but various side dish options to enjoy with.

🥄✨Fried rice: this will be the one I recommend the most, adding rice and some topping to fry on the pan at the end of the meal. The rice took the oil from pan, mixing with egg, and what we ordered (roe, cheese.) super flavored and tasty.

🥣🥢Cold noodles was outstanding too. The soup was refreshing!

If you like kimchi fried rice and fatty pork, this is the best small town korean barbecue you can get in queens. We are regulars here because the flavors and creativity in their menu are unmatched. The atmosphere makes you feel like you are in Korea and the owners are very nice. They own the shop next door as well and you can order raw marinated crab. I recommend this place for 4 people if you want KBBQ without feeling overcrowded and they have the best pork and kimchi.

We had to try Peter Luger while in New York, it just iconic, so we made a reservation for lunch. Service was really good! The steak was also amazing, being from an Alberta ranch I have to be partial to Alberta beef, but this was a close second 😁. We also got the German fried potatoes, which were good. The house steak sauce was different than I was expecting, similar to a cocktail sauce, but it went really well with the perfectly cooked steak. We were happy we had made a reservation as there was quite a lineup otherwise. Thanks so much for the amazing lunch!

I went to the famous Peter Luger steakhouse in Brooklyn, and honestly, the food quality was excellent. We ordered a few different cuts to try them out, along with the burger, which I’d seen highly recommended.

As expected, the meat was top-tier full of flavor and cooked to perfection. It met all my expectations, as did the burger.

A special shout out goes to the French fries; they were spectacular. Obviously, you come here for the steak, but the fries were on another level.

While I have nothing but praise for the food, the service didn't come close to what you'd expect from such a famous restaurant. The waiters are almost rude to you, as if it’s part of the 'style' of the place, which I just don't get. You have everything you need to be the best, yet you fail at customer service.

In short, I think the price to quality ratio is fair, and the food/portions are very generous.

As always a great experience. I love the beer hall atmosphere.
Our Server “Aloisius” was the absolute best!
Incredibly attentive and accommodating.
The Steaks of course perfect as always. Bacon appetizer is always a good start. The Luger Beer is great, wish it came in a bigger glass though.
Dessert was the hidden Star, the Apple Strudel with a tower of whipped cream. Delicious as if you were in Salzburg to eat it.
Love this place!
They accommodated our 11 month old and he loved the steak too. Servers were entertaining him and making jokes and read every wish for him off our minds!
(If you read this, thank you to all the Staff for being so awesome)

I've been going to Luger for several years now (including for my birthday twice) and I've never had a bad experience. I truly don't get the hate it gets. I've never had a rude waiter (they can be no-nonsense though, which I actually respect) and I've never had a bad steak here. Yes it is expensive, but which steak house (that isn't a chain) isn't?

My piece of advice is to order one size steak below your party size. The steak for two can feed 3 and the steak for three can feed 4 easily. And don't forget to order the bacon. And every dessert comes with their famous "schlag".

And remember to bring cash as they don't accept credit cards.

The steak is phenomenal in every sense. The dry age is perfect and the seasoning is just right. It truly is a quality steak. The portions on the salads, appetizers, and sides are large enough to share. The German hash browns were particularly delightful. The atmosphere is somewhat stale and the service is good, not great. Overall, one of my favorite New York steakhouses.

What a great spot!! We came here for a lovely dinner that most certainly did NOT disappoint!

Sunday in Brooklyn is a delightful little corner spot that seems small initially, but actually has plenty of seating throughout - including in an upstairs space.
Regardless, we were promptly seated (without a reservation) in a table downstairs, and had very friendly, hospitable service throughout our visit.

While dining, we ordered a few of the cocktails, and I found each one I tried to be a good amount of strength while also creative in the flavors and heat.
My personal favorite was the Ski Lift, which is a hot cocktail with bourbon, coffee, and other ingredients - soooo soothing, STRONG, and flavorful!

Now on to main event - the food!
My wood-fired lasagna was INCREDIBLE - so much flavor, texture, and uniqueness to each bite.
My partner's chicken pot pie was similarly unique and yet familiar in its excellent textures and taste!

Sunday in Brooklyn had a wonderful ambiance, lovely food, and great service - I highly recommend!

The service amazing. For 2 people they offered a 2 person table, outside or inside, they sat us right away. The food was Fast and tasted fresh. Eggs were done perfectly, soft scrambled, bacon crispy, potatoes were a little too salty, and the shakshuka was a little disappointing, like salsa with pouched eggs, but the bread was crisp and yummy when dipped into the bowl. However, the Sunday pancake was amazing. It’s was like a mini fluffy yellow cake with delicious buttered maple all over. not a maple taste but like a chocolaty buttery nutty flavor. “It was like a reward”. We enjoyed it the most. Overall we understand the hype and definitely recommend to try it for yourself.

Visited Sunday in Brooklyn for brunch and honestly, wow. We got the pistachio hummus with wood-fired flatbread — probably the richest, most flavorful meze I’ve ever had. A total must-try (and so generous we couldn’t even finish it!).

Also ordered the warm grain bowl, and it arrived in what felt like 5 minutes — unbelievably fast service. The bowl itself was pure comfort: warm, rich, and beautifully balanced. The eggs were cooked like a soufflé — soft and melting — topped with a gigantic half avocado and a generous handful of pepitas (which I love and rarely see done this well). The rice underneath was so delicious.

Finished with a cappuccino, served instantly in a lovely porcelain cup — the perfect touch to end brunch.

Our server was incredibly kind and attentive, checking in often to make sure everything was perfect. Honestly, one of the best brunch experiences we’ve had in

I've been to Sunday in Brooklyn several times for both brunch and dinner. Brunch certainly gets busy but its a fun time - make a reservation. The food, service and drinks are always lovely - Thomas the bartender is incredible!
I recommend trying the Sage Fright brunch cocktail, the Wood Roasted Half Chicken for dinner and the S'mores soft serve for dessert. The S'mores latte is fun too for all the s'mores fans.

The food was a bit hit-or-miss. The burger was good, but the fries were overly salty. I felt pretty indifferent about the pancake, and the French toast wasn’t great. Both the latte and coffee were served lukewarm, which was disappointing. That said, the service really stood out our party arrived late for our reservation, and the staff was very accommodating. Server was great. The inside was also nicely decorated for the holidays, creating a warm atmosphere.

Overall, I wouldn’t be reluctant to go back, but it wouldn’t be my first choice either.

I really wish we could give 1/2 stars. Food was more of a 3.5.

I love spicy food. Szechuan cuisine specializes in that, going for a mouth numbing spiciness. So I had to come here.

The atmosphere is nice. They were playing country music, which I thought was funny. And the service is great.

I got the lunch special, triple pepper chicken (as you see in the photo) with pork fried rice and wonton soup. The soup is perfect for a cold, winter day, and was absolutely delicious. The chicken, meanwhile, was nice and spicy (though I was expecting much spicier for 3 hot pepper emojis). Though, when I asked, they told me it was more "mild" — I gotta ask for spicier next time! But please get something milder if you can't handle spice — my spice tolerance is VERY high.

Excellent food, excellent service, funny random country music. Five stars.

We’ve visited this restaurant well over a dozen times across the years, dining in regularly. It has also received Michelin recognition, which was part of what initially drew us in.

Based on our most recent visit, while the food was not bad, it felt noticeably different from what we remembered from earlier visits. The flavors were more restrained, and the dishes lacked the boldness and depth that previously stood out.

I wouldn’t say the food is poor — it’s still solid — but based on our past experiences, the dishes felt more moderate and less distinctive than before. Given its reputation and history, there is room for improvement, particularly in terms of flavor intensity.

A consistent and authentic Sichuan style in a local area. The lunch specials are tasty and their chef specials are also great. I recommend the braised fish filet in chili oil as well as the fried fish filet in with ginger peanuts. Great for takeout and always fast delivery!

I’ve ordered from Legends of Taste a few times and thought it was decent at first, but my last order of orange chicken was absolutely disgusting. The pieces were mostly fried crust with barely any chicken inside, and what little meat there was was dry, rubbery, and chewy like jerky. It was inedible ! The sauce tasted bitter and off, almost medicinal, and the broccoli was dull and lifeless, clearly cooked hours before.

This meal made it clear they don’t care about quality. It felt like leftovers reheated and thrown together at the end of the night. After this experience, I’ll never go back — they lost me as a customer for good.
It was so bad I threw the entire meal straight into the trash.

The flavors were delicious. We had a 9 course meal, catered as part of a group. The food just kept coming! The location is in a neighborhood and only a few tables inside. The staff was wonderful. I thought the group price was a bit steep at $150 each but other than that we were kept very full and had a great experience here.

I honestly wish I could give the service a 6/5, but I will make do with what I got! My fiance and I came here on NYE to do the pre-set menu of house favorites. The place was decorated so cute and they had little party favors everywhere for NYE. When we arrived, we got seated at the bar even though we made a reservation at the back patio on Resy. When I let the manager know, she was so apologetic about the Resy app incorrectly placing guests into the wrong areas of the restaurant and asked us if she could purchase our first round of drinks to make up for it. No problem! So we are eating dinner at the bar and she kept coming up to us after we were done with the cocktails offering us wine, refills, and even a great dessert wine that the bartender recommended with the babka. When I tell you this is some of the best food AND service i’ve ever experienced- what an incredible way to end 2025!!! At the end we expected to pay for the drinks completely and were told they were all on the house. Shocked and on cloud 9, beyond full, we left the restaurant so happy and a little tipsy.

As for the food, obsessed with the hummus and ricotta cheese, as well as the kofta was the best I’ve ever had. Babka was amazing and everything else was so yummy, my fiance never had Israeli food before and was cautiously optimistic going into the dinner I chose, and left saying that was his favorite meal from our NYC trip! Thank you so much to the team of Miss Ada!! highly highly recommend!!!!

Celebrated my husband's birthday and had the most wonderful experience!! Every single bite of food was absolutely delicious. We especially loved the short rib hummus, halloumi skewers, falafel, and pita bread 😊 Super friendly and sweet staff as well. They even surprised us at the end with a little cup of gelato with a candle in it. This was our 4th time dining at Miss Ada and we will definitely continue to come back!! 🧡🧡🧡
This is now one of my favorite steak and eggs.  The whipped ricotta is so good and very similar to Theodora’s though it is served with pita bread. Service was great!

Cute and cozy vibe. Food was delicious, the fish was super tender. Good selection of wines and friendly service. Great example of what to expect in the fort Greene neighborhood. Verdict: will return and recommend!

Came here for my friends birthday brunch and we had amazing experience. Service was excellent & atmosphere was warm and inviting. Food was very good and I especially loved the whipped ricotta. Thank you for the babka treat !

I had high hopes for this place. After trying Schwartz’s in Montreal and Katz’s in New York, I didn’t expect to be served supermarket-style pastrami. We ordered the smoked meat sandwich, Caesar, and poutine, and then tea and chocolate babka. Everything except the smoked meat was fine. The smoked meat itself was very disappointing, I’d probably give it one star. it’s also over priced.

Update (two days later): Since eating the smoked meat sandwich here, my husband has had an upset stomach. I don’t know how long the pastrami had been sitting, but this made the experience even more disappointing.

Got the flight of latke and they were all great. We also got the brisket poutine, I would have it again but I really want to try some of the other poutine they offer. Will definitely back if not soon then for Hanukkah next year. Oh yeah and the chocolate babka was fantastic

Mile End in Brooklyn has been on my list of places to check out for a long time, and it did not disappoint at all!

I got a couple of sandwiches to go, but the inside looks like a family-run, hospitable, and cozy diner... exactly what you want! Love the Canadian soul too!

I followed Ali's recommendation and tried the Montreal Smoked Meat sandwich (their special), and I also got the one with chicken liver. Both super Yummy!

Will come back to dine in 10/10 See you soon :)

I’m a big foodie for brisket, pastrami, and corned beef — give me all of it! My go-to is the Reuben, and they’ve got a double-meat version called the “Eli Reuben” that’s an absolute must if you go.

The ambience is cozy and classic diner-style. Their breakfast menu looks top-tier, too. Service can be a bit on the slower side, but with this Montreal-style smoked meat deli, it’s absolutely worth the stop.

Poutine was mouthwateringly good! i got mine with smoked meat and it tasted a lot like what I had in Montreal, super authentic! If you like salt, this for you. It's also good for two people. The servers were very kind, but they're a little understaffed so be understanding of that! I sat at the community table and everything looked delicious. Very excited to come back!

The atmosphere felt very intimate, it was dark but inviting and a great spot for a date. Service was phenomenal, they were very attentive and gave great recommendations. The cocktails were a 9/10, I had a spicy mango drink. The arepas were incredible but the number one dish was the bollitos pelones. Highly recommended. The baby shark dish was our least favorite but each dish was plated with care and very aesthetically pleasing.

Tried Venezuelan food for the first time and it didn’t disappoint. The whole spot had a warm vibe with a really inviting ambiance. Drinks were flavorful and a little strong in a good way. The food was the star though. The red snapper on tostones was fire, perfect coating and great flavor. The brisket with black beans and egg was incredibly flavorful and the meat was super tender. Overall, a really nice experience.

We went to Casa Ora last night to celebrate my birthday, and I’m still thinking about every single bite. The asado negro alone deserves its own love letter. If you’ve never had it, imagine a piece of beef that has been brined, marinated, and slow-cooked for hours until it becomes as tender as butter, then finished with a deep, glossy caramelization of papelón that gives you that slightly charred, smoky sweetness. It is the kind of dish that stops conversation at the table, an art piece with soul.

And everything else? Perfection with nostalgia woven in.
The plantains, the mini cachapas, the tequeños, and a pan de jamón so good it could make your abuela cry, warm, tender, slightly sweet, salty, comforting. Every plate felt like someone was inviting us into their home, letting us taste the food their family grew up on, the food that fills the kitchen on a Sunday afternoon.

Casa Ora is full of heart. You can feel the love, the purpose, the passion in every corner, not just in the dishes but in the way the team carries themselves. It is rare to find a place that feeds you and moves you at the same time.

This is the restaurant you will rave about.
The one you will bring friends to, brag about, and keep thinking about long after you leave.

An unforgettable meal, and a perfect birthday.
Thank you, Casa Ora. 💛

I came all the way from Manhattan to meet friends here for dinner, and it was absolutely worth it. From the moment we arrived, we felt incredibly welcome. We ordered a variety of dishes from the menu, and I had the chance to try almost everything, every single dish was delicious and beautifully prepared.
The atmosphere is very cozy and inviting, making you feel comfortable right away. It’s the kind of place where you want to stay longer and truly enjoy the evening. A big thank you as well to the lovely staff for their warm hospitality and excellent service. I can wholeheartedly recommend this place and would definitely come back again.

My family and I went to celebrate my parents 36th anniversary and my brothers 24th birthday. The staff was amazing. Super quiet for a Sunday. The place is dark and intimate which I loved personally. The FOOD?! 100/10. The drinks? Just as good 100/10. So much flavor in each dish and appetizer. I only got a picture of my paella but let me tell you, BEST paella. I’ve ever had. I’d recommend the shrimp appetizer as well because the sauce with it?! OUT OF THIS WORLD. Most definitely coming back again!

Cozy & intimate spot w/ solid plates & great drinks. Reasonably priced, ambiance suited for conversation, a bartender that crafts bliss in a glass(ask for Eric), a well maintained restroom, suitable for small & extra large groups & a relaxing playlist.

Check them out!

The ambiance at this restaurant was lovely, with the added bonus of outdoor seating. The service was exceptional—our server was incredibly patient and attentive throughout the evening. However, the food did not meet expectations. The pasta dishes, priced around $25, were served in very small portions, slightly undercooked, and the flavors lacked cohesion. We left quite hungry! While I appreciate having had the opportunity to try it, I likely wouldn’t return.

Honest Review of Ammazzacaffè

Atmosphere & Service: 10/10

We grabbed a late 10 PM Saturday night Resy and the space still felt welcoming. The bar was spotless, the decor stylish but comfortable, and the service was excellent. Josh was warm, attentive, and service never felt rushed. Presentation on every dish was elegant and thoughtful.

Starters : 9/10
•	Sunchoke ($22): Beautiful salt-baked prep with hazelnut pesto, yogurt, and apple. Creative, layered, and earthy.
•	Barbabietole ($19): Roasted beets with smoked ricotta and pickled figs. Gorgeous on the plate, subtle on the palate. It was balanced but leaned more refined than bold.

Mains : 8.5/10
•	Cavatelli ($30): Crab, corn, Sungold tomato, coral butter. Fresh, seasonal, and well-executed. It was light yet rich, a summer-forward pasta.
•	Linguini ($30): Cockle clams with ramp pesto and yuzu kosho. Briny and bright, with a nice pop of citrus. Well-made but didn’t quite deliver a “wow” factor.

Drinks : 8/10
•	Hazy Tropics ($17): Tropical, refreshing, and slightly smoky. A solid cocktail.
•	Espresso Martini ($17): Smooth and well-balanced. As expected, no complaints.

Value : 8/10
Subtotal: $135
With tax + tip: $179.32. For two people, it’s on the pricier side, but aligned with Williamsburg dining standards.

Overall Impression : 8/10
Ammazza Café delivers excellent service, gorgeous plating, and a stylish, clean setting. The food was thoughtfully prepared, but none of the dishes quite leapt off the table as unforgettable. Still, it left us wanting to return and explore more of the menu. A great dining experience. The experience was elegant, and enjoyable, even if the food didnt completely blow us away.

Such a cute, cozy spot for lunch. The food was genuinely delicious. We did the prix fixe menu which was way more than we could eat (great value and super generous portions). Everything we tried was really well done, and the vibe felt relaxed and welcoming.

Would definitely recommend for a bite to eat, and it also seems like a perfect place to swing by for a glass of wine.

Used to be one of my favorite weekly spots but the portions keep shrinking and the prices keep rising multiple dollars per dish. ~$30 for a protein-free very small pasta dish. Service has declined in the last year or so as well. Overall, I no longer recommend it and have stopped returning.

This was my first Michelin experience, I went here a couple of months ago.
The food is immaculate, absolutely exquisite. The Sea Oak was by far the best bite of food I've experienced, tied with the Oscitera Caviar. I was blown away, physically reeling from just how expertly crafted each bite was, down to the placement of sauce and the variety of textures.

The service was excellent. The waiters worked together beautifully and they were very kind and attentive. My only gripe is that they seemed more interested in explaining these dishes to my Michelin savvy friend instead of myself, as they would turn to him and I'd be hearing every other word from them on account of low volume.

The atmosphere was beautiful. Peaceful and calm, lighting was perfect for pictures, and seeing the cooks in front of us operating at such a high level with no stress was awe inspiring.

The wine selection was also excellent, with each wine being selected to pair with a dish from the tasting menu, we tasted many kinds and it was great hearing stories about each one.

The ingredients at Aska are undeniably fresh and of very high quality, and you can tell that a lot of care goes into sourcing and preparation. However, the overall experience wasn’t quite for me.

The environment is extremely serious and almost austere, which sets the tone for a very focused dining experience. The flavors throughout the tasting menu were very subtle — almost too subtle for my personal taste. The cuisine leans heavily into natural, earthy elements, and at times it felt like there was a bit too much nature on the plate.

While it wasn’t my personal favorite, I can absolutely appreciate the craft and precision behind it. If you’re curious about experiencing Nordic cuisine at a very high level, Aska is definitely worth trying.

Had what I feel to be the best Michelin experience in NYC to date. Every dish was so incredibly on point with a few that will be stored in the memory food bank forever. The majority of the ingredients are sourced within 60 miles of the restaurant with the exception of a few items (mostly Nordic) that were imported. I thought the notes of each dish were clean, delicate, and beautifully balanced. Nothing was a smack to the palette with too much intensity which I think is exactly the story that Aska is trying to tell, it's clearly hyper-focused on the seasonality and quality of the ingredients. I will say there was a Madagascar caviar used in a dish that tasted like Serrano ham- like nothing I've ever had before.

We did both the wine and non-alc pairing and both were very well suited for each course. A million extra points for continuously topping us off throughout the night.

Ambiance is dark and intimate with an open kitchen to admire throughout the evening. Service was next level, with Missy the beverage director and her team seamlessly flowing about throughout the evening. The team was so warm, kind, and genuine- absolutely nothing felt sterile or forced, which is always a breath of fresh air. Not sure what more a restaurant needs to do to merit that third star.

Also an awesome touch, my wife has a thing for beautiful dinnerware/flatware and was admiring theirs for the entirety of the meal. To our surprise, they printed out an extra menu with each dinnerware vendor they used for each dish. Pretty cool stuff.

This is a very late review because I was too lazy to write reviews. But even after more than half a year, this restaurant is still easily in my top five places in NYC after a few years of living here.

The food was excellent. I had the best caviar I’ve ever had at this place. I remember the server specifically mentioned that the caviar was carefully sourced and brought in from Europe, though I’ve forgotten the exact details over time. Everything else on the menu was also very well executed. The only dish I personally couldn’t finish was the venison—not because it wasn’t good or fresh, but simply because it’s not a protein I enjoy.

What truly stood out was the service. I was unsure about which wine or cocktail to order, and the server patiently offered multiple tastings of different wines and cocktails before I made a decision. At one point, my friend and I were discussing the beautiful tableware in another language and I briefly picked up a plate to look at it. At the end of the meal, the server brought us a dedicated tableware menu without us asking, simply because she noticed my interest.

A friend who visited on another occasion mentioned feeling slightly cold, and a server immediately brought a blanket without being asked. I have never experienced this level of attentiveness at any other Michelin-starred restaurant—whether in NYC, elsewhere in the US or in Europe. Even now, the service still stands out in my memory as genuinely impressive.

Many restaurants blur together for me after the meal is over, but this one hasn’t. The presentation of the dishes was distinctive, and the overall experience left a lasting impression. It’s one of the very few places in NYC that I still remember clearly—and one of the even fewer that made me want to write a review at all.

An absolutely exceptional experience.

The service was truly top-notch, and most of the dishes weren’t just delicious - they were genuinely MIND-BLOWING!

A memorable evening from start to finish, it is definitely one of the best dining experiences we had in the city.

We can't wait for an excuse to be back here for another magical evening!
The staff and service in general is great! The food was average-good Mexican but very expensive. (We had two Plato Dons and mixed fajitas. The guacamole and flan was everyone’s favorite!

My friend and I dine in with our kids and we had a great time. The food was amazing. The drinks were great. The atmosphere was a breath of fresh air. We enjoyed our stay. It was so great that my boyfriend and I along with our daughter went too. We had an awesome time. We enjoyed our food. He was amazed with the food , drinks and prices. It is definitely a top pick for me.

Oh talk about staples in the neighborhood,  Chavelas is definitely one of them. A great place for brunch, lunch or dinner they have been serving great Mexican Food from their corner on Franklin for years now. I had the pleasure to dine in for lunch recently.

Our server (Oscar I believe) was incredible.  Knew the menu in and out and provided impeccable service. The staff overall were kind and made you feel welcomed.

The food was good as usual. Chilaquiles, smoked ribeye quesadillas and a few other items were order. The smoked Ribeye Quesadilla was a major hit! Keep that as a staple guys.

If you happen to be around the Brooklyn museum and looking for a place with great value, go support Chavelas

Apologies!  Food was so good couldn't take pics!
Outstanding - great service and server. No wait on a Sunday night. The Beef short rib special was incredible!! Also had the fajitas which also were spectacular. 10/10

Incredible ambience! Great food and super attentive staff. Had the specials; hot toddy, mussels, steak quesadillas

Also had the molcajete de carnitas and sopa azteca from the regular menu.

We go down to Arthur Ave for dinner from time to time and always like to try a new place.
Tonight we decided on Tra Di Noi.
It's on 187th street around the corner from Arthur Ave.
The restaurant is small and cozy and has the old school Italian restaurant  red checkered table cloths.
We were greeted warmly by the hostess and seated at table against the wall in the dining Area. The table had salt, pepper, bread dishes, utensil set ups with a napkin and an olive oil bottle.
A waiter came over and explained the specials to us and took out drink order. The waiter then brought us bread and water to start. They only have beer and wine and I asked for a non alcoholic beer but they don't serve it.
The menu is small but has something for everyone and the specials more than make up for the smaller size menu.
We ordered fried calamari and a mussels special for the appetizers.
The calamari was ok. It was fried a little harder then I like but it was a nice size for 2 people and came with tubes and baby octopus. The Marinara with it was a little bland for my taste.
The mussels in white wine appetizer was fantastic and a great portion.
For the entree we had an order of the pork chop with vinegar peppers specials and a rigatoni special.
Both entrees were delicious and they came with a small plate of fingerling potatoes and string beans that were nicely sauteed with garlic and oil.
We split a piece of homemade Italian cheesecake and I had an espresso and both were absolutely delicious.
The staff was friendly and knowledgeable and attentive. The waiter came by and offered us more bread which a lot of places dont do.

This is a real Italian restaurant owned and operated by real Italians which is something that is hard to come by these days in the Italian restaurant business.
The food is as close to homemade as you can get.
It's not mass produced so you are not going to get heaping portions like you may get in other places but what you do get is a dish that is crafted with care to be as authentic as possible.
The restaurant is quiant and cozy and is staffed by friendly people.
We left the restaurant happy and you will as well.

Delicious and totally legit – I could eat here every day.  The waitstaff are extremely attentive and knowledgeable. The old-school tablecloths and classic tunes create the perfect nostalgic vibe. Easy to hold a conversation, and overall a great experience every time. Whether you’re popping in for a quick lunch or kicking back for a chill dinner, Tra Di Noi always hits the spot. Totally worth it.

Phenomenal, Exquisite, Delicous. The best Veal Limon I have experienced. Traditional home-cooking style meals. Quick service. Quaint but sophisticated. Very friendly staff. 10/10 reccomend this hidden gem.

We had an excellent lunch here, having found our way from the Botanical Garden’s orchid show (Mr Flower Fantastic this year.) We were given a lovely table by the window, and everything that followed was perfect—attentive waiter, interesting specials, good food.

Went here for the first time today to have a leisurely lunch with my parents. We sat by the window, so we got to take in Belmont’s street life while enjoying the best Italian-American food I’ve had since living in NYC. Everything was prepared simply and packed with flavor. The staff was very attentive, and the owners, who were both sitting in the dining room the whole time, were very welcoming.

Speedy Romeo has some of the best pizza in the city.  The crust is just PERFECT.  Thin but with enough consistency, crunchy in all the right places… just wow.  We order a pizza approximately once a week and are always impressed.
We like eating there too - it’s casual and the food is delicious.  Good wine and craft beer selection.  Their Caesar salad is top notch. Just go and thank me later. 🍕

As a St. Louis transplant, I’ve spent decades searching for a St. Louis style pizza in NYC to poor success, but everyone pointed to Speedy Romeo as my last, best hope. So, for better or for worse, I’m going to endeavor to compare this pizza to the square beyond compare. The wood-fired crust at Speedy Romeo does not resemble the cracker-thin St. Louis slab, but it sure is tasty. These sauces and toppings feel too high falutin to be found in my favorite St Louis takeout, but, oh, I enjoyed them, too. The cheese- I made sure to order a pizza with provel cheese- the cheese instantly took me back home. It hit the mark and even made me a little homesick. I loved it and will be back soon. In the end, Speedy Romeo felt a little bit like New York, a little bit St. Louis, but it was mostly its own unique and delicious style.
