The food was presented very nicely and looked like it had been cooked with care. Unfortunately, with the exception of the pot pie, the other dishes were under seasoned.

Cute little restaurant in Greenpoint! A group of us 3 were here on a Wed night and shared everything:

- Hokkadio milk bread
- Fuyu burrata
- Bone marrow tartare
- Miso black cod
- Snow crab udon
- Duck
- Lingo beef pie
- Squash and sage rice

Everything was plated beautifully and tasted great. The beef pie could definitely use a side of rice since it's pretty rich and savory.

Service was great and super attentive throughout the night. This is definitely on the pricier side though, given the portion sizes. We each got one drink (1 being a yuzu soda), and total after tax & tip came out to $320ish. I'd definitely come back to check out their brunch menu.

A perfect experience from start to finish. The cod was cooked to perfection and the potato Mille-feuille was a superb side dish we got at the suggestion of our excellent waiter! A great date night option for some high end Japanese comfort food

I had high hopes for Place des Fêtes but I was pretty disappointed, especially for all the high reviews it received. For the price they’re charging here, you either have to increase the portion size or really knock the customers socks off. Some of the dishes were comically small, I get this is tapas but come on. My favorite dish was the sardine toast but that’s the only thing that was good. The pasta tasted like something you’d make at home and the cod was lukewarm, not appealing at all. The freshness of the ingredients was spot on, you can definitely taste the quality but it’s the actual delivery that flopped. I do have to shout out to our waiter who was great and offered some solid suggestions. There are some great restaurants in Brooklyn, especially in this area but PDF is not one of them.

The sardines toast was definitely the highlight for me! But the maitako mushroom with black garlic sauce & corn with eel bonito were delightful.

Super cute place inside, very cozy and nice bar seating area. All the staffs were super helpful, attentive and sweet.

Perfect date spot, light not too dim, portions are on the smaller end and pretty vibey.

Sleek and bustling spot. The swordfish, the pasta and the daily special mushrooms were very memorable, although really everything was good. Great wine choices and solid service too. A strong recommend for a weekend outing for groups of 2-4.

Had a really great experience here end-to-end. We came for my boyfriend’s birthday and I really appreciated that they wished him happy birthday on the walk in, had a card at our seat at the bar and poured us glasses of champagne as we sat down. It made the dinner feel very special before we even made it to the food.

The food was delicious! Every sauce and broth was so unique and well curated. Each dish got better and better with each bite. I know I’ll be craving another visit very soon.

My personal faves from the night were the sardine toast (I called it a sushi toast) and the mafaldine which had notes of almost a seaweed like flavor, but everything was great. My only note was with the asparagus and salt cod dish the flavor of the asparagus drowned out the cod - I appreciated the cod and the ramp more on their own or with the sourdough. Definitely get the sourdough to sop up any and all of the leftover sauces. They’re that good

One of my favorite wine bars/restaurant! Excellent rotating menu and really fun cozy environment with an open kitchen, knowledgeable staff. The mussel starter with green sauce and the lamb tartare were favorites. Everything was excellently prepared, no notes

Nice little restaurant in Williamsburg. They had a special friend fish sandwich that was bomb. We also shared some fried squid and fries. The squid was probably small to share with four people. My husband and I shared some fries and the special sandwich. We also shared the sundae. I got one of the mocktails. My friend of the pork sandwich, which was large, but looked good too. I would go back if I was in the area.

Walnut shrimp was standout, the shrimp had perfect texture and flavor.

Prob skip the cacio e Pepe and the crispy rice skate wings.

interesting fusion food and cute vibes

Came here with my friend for a nice girls night! We got a reservation at 9 pm and it was crazy packed when we walked in. A bunch of people waiting. Took a bit to get our table but seemed like it was just people staying too long that caused backup. The place was sooo cute and cool and the bathroom was like a mini club which I loved. Music was perfect, playing all my favorites. Waitress was AWESOME and super helpful. We got espresso martinis which came out quick and green beans and wontons to start. Green beans turned out to be our fav fish and were delicious with some fried bread on top. Great flavor. Wontons were good too and had a curry/Indian flavor. I thought they could have been hotter (temp and spice level), but we enjoyed them. we also got the noodles. I personally don't like the rolled noodles and I thought the flavor was weird. But my friend loved them.  Overall really thought this was a cool place and enjoyed our experience but didn't wow me like other spots in NYC. I'm also really tired of cocktails being $20, but I guess that's just what the reality is these days.

Made the “trek” to Brooklyn and was excited to try Bonnie’s. Service was good- the server was knowledgeable about the menu and very pleasant. Had heard ravings about the MSG martini which we tried, and also tried the sour cherry Negroni - neither were spectacular and the martini had a strange aftertaste.

For food, we ordered the chrysanthemum salad (Don Angie’s is so much better) - which was a large portion but mostly cabbage (?), the long beans were too mushy for my liking (liked the fried crullers but they were overly salty), the fuyu cacio e pepe mein which was just ok, and the sundae for dessert which was not that interesting (I liked the fried condensed milk). We also had the shrimp with walnuts and broccoli which was pretty basic. Overall, the food was pretty disappointing and I would not go back…

Food was very underwhelming. Everything seemed “gimmicky”. The bread for the sandwich was a little too dense, and flavour of the meat itself was barely there. Got some hot sauce on the side just to taste something. Pricey for what it was. Not sure how it’s bib gourmand.

Service was nice although maybe slightly misogynistic given the waiter only spoke to my partner and not me and also only gave him the bill (not a big deal but the female staff immediately did talk to me in comparison!)

Vibey atmosphere and drinks were actually really good.

Give the food a miss if you have a varied palette

What an excellent experience! I dined at a fantastic new Mexican pop-up where the food was a revelation, offering unique dishes far beyond traditional tacos. I'd highly recommend it for gathering with friends and family; everyone will find something to love.
Everything was great! My favorite was los sopecitos, the variety of salsas and the potato chips. We needed a bigger table haha, I guess they could bring the dishes little by little.

pretty good went with my girlfriend for her birthday. first thing i noticed was it was very “trendy” tiny tables and weird design but cute. like many nice restaurants in new york i can’t imagine the average american even fitting in the chairs there

food was great we got some of the little tacos as well as a caesar salad. then of course the steak what’s that called. carne asada i think and some sort of pasta dish.

honestly when i was single i never age salads but now i have a trendy girlfriend in brooklyn i feel like im constantly buying $16.00 caesar salads not even with chicken.

staff was great very helpful and kind and welcoming and cool

i thought there’d be more happy hour but they didn’t really have much outside of 10
dollar margaritas, which of course i had a few of but they weren’t very good, maybe too strong ! i forget what it was but my gf did not like her mixed drink much either. we were happier when we switched to beer

overall great time and experience, a little sticker shock at the price but hey i ordered the steak. what can i expect.

Olmo is that kind of Mexican food that’s not the usual tacos or burritos everyone knows. It’s real “chilango” food from Mexico City… like the homemade dishes my grandma used to cook on Sundays, but taken to a premium NYC level. As someone from Mexico City, I can say every plate is a treat for your taste buds, your eyes, and even your sense of smell.

The vibe is awesome: the music, the decor, the cantina-style concept, everything feels super authentic. The staff is warm and welcoming, which makes the whole experience even better.

The bar is also amazing. You’ll find everything from a classic Mexican michelada to creative mezcal cocktails.

It’s the perfect spot for a date night or just to hang out, disconnect for a while, and feel like you’re in a little corner of Mexico City right in the middle of Brooklyn.

Olmo is such a Bed-Stuy gem! It has a real CDMX vibe — lively, spacious, and fun without feeling cramped. We tried the crudité, crunchy chicharrón with cabbage and sauces, and the sopes (so addictive). For mains, the carne asada was packed with flavor, the eggplant milanesa was insanely good, and the branzino was perfectly cooked with flaky skin. Warm tortillas let us turn everything into little tacos — we cleaned every plate. Great mezcal-forward cocktails (loved the Ya Dijo El Jefe and Última Palabra) and a solid wine list. Don’t skip the flan paleta for dessert — creamy, sweet, and the perfect finish. Can’t wait to go back!!

Don’t let this small taco spot fool you…they don’t mess with the flavor! It was delicious! I’m creature of habit and I tend to go to the same taco spot all the time but I decided to venture out. It did not disappoint! It’s a small space so please don’t expect to sit down and dine but if you’re on a solo date you might get lucky and find a spot on their counter.

Amazing experience. All the tacos were PACKED with flavor and delicious taste. Easy to order on a self order screen to go back up and order as many as you want. Tacos came out fast, delicious picos to add by the front door, not cheap with the meat. I will be back!

These tacos in NYC are unreal.
If they were in Mexico, I’d honestly eat them every day.

The lengua taco was spectacular — tender, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Easily some of the best tacos I’ve had outside Mexico.

Been wanting to try el Chato for a couple months and finally popped in. In general, I love Al pastor and so I got it in quesadilla form and it was excellent. I always love the lil’ crispy pieces that are charred and this had plenty of them! I also tried the asada, suadero, & lengua and i enjoyed them in that order. I always try them with no salsas first and then add afterwards to see how good they are. I really enjoyed the asada and sister. The tongue wasn’t bad, but just not quite as good as the others. I was looking forward to chorizo & mushroom but they were out, so I’ll just have to come back. El Chato is definitely worth a visit and worthy of adding onto a taco tour you’re planning.  Come check it out!

Loved the food here! Came around 5:30pm on a Friday night and there was no line. My friend and I ordered at the kiosk. We weren’t super hungry. We just wanted to try this spot, so we got two tacos. The stand out was definitely the al pastor taco!

What a fantastic experience!! We entered with high expectations and enjoyed a meal that exceeded them. The food and service were impeccable.

Starters we sampled included the expertly composed Fluke Crudo (which was refreshing and delicious), Gamja Buchim (tuna sashimi on a potato pancake with wasabi-infused sour cream!), Dukboki Fundido (an incredible internationally-influenced dish incorporating Oaxacan cheese and Mexican chorizo alongside thick Asian noodles) and Grilled Oysters (savory and delicious with butter and herbs). All were exceptional.

For entrees, we greatly enjoyed Maine Uni Bibimbap (possibly our favorite dish of the night, absolutely delicious!) and the Bulgogi (some of the best I’ve had anywhere).

Throughout the evening, we tried 3 cocktails: The Squid & The Whale was my first drink of the night, and the sesame oil and egg whites were a fantastic treat for my palate. Drink 2 was Seoul Train, similar to a Manhattan with a clever addition of plum wine. My final drink of the night was the NY Sleepover, a delightful sour topped with a Chianti float.

The desserts are impressive as well — the Beignets were soft, fluffy, fresh, and impossible to deny even with a full stomach. The crème brûlée was a sweet and elegant finish to a perfect meal.

Thanks to the kind and attentive staff, the talented chefs, and everyone who made our meal and evening unforgettable. Park Slope is blessed to have Haenyeo, but diners from all over should make an effort to visit this exceptional restaurant.

Beautiful spot in Park Slope. This time around I only had a cocktail because of limited time. Our bartender was still training and he was so friendly and knew the menu very well to help make suggestions. My friend and I both loved our drinks, will try the food next time-smelled amazing.

This is definitely not average Korean restaurant, it is so contemporary that you get hint of it's Korean heritage only by reading menu (for better or worse). The place, if I am not mistaken it is mentioned in Michelin Guide, but in my opinion worth a star. The food was delicious and although by the end I was so full I couldn't stop eating until the plate was clean. Kalbi jjim which is short ribs and Bulgogi were out of this world! Again I have failed to try their dessert,  but definitely will make another trip to this place, hopefully getting chance to try them. The place is very popular so reservation is recommend.

I wish I came to Haenyeo earlier on because I’d hands down say this is the best restaurant in Park Slope. The vibe inside, the staff, and the food are up to standard with some of the best restaurants in the city. Some standouts are their kimchi and bulgogi but I really didn’t have anything that was below average. I 100% will be back soon, hopefully when people are in town so we can show them some delicious food. Would highly recommend if you’re in the area (or even outside the area and are reading this).

I recently had an amazing dining experience at Haenyeo, and I can’t recommend it enough! From the moment we arrived, the warm and inviting atmosphere set the perfect tone for the evening.

A huge shoutout to Izzy at the bar—she was incredibly informative, attentive, and made us feel truly taken care of. Her friendly and professional service really stood out!

Now, onto the food—absolutely phenomenal. We started with the Fluke Crudo and Grilled Oysters with Seaweed Butter on Brioche Toast—both were fresh, flavorful, and a perfect start to the meal. The Dukboki Fundido was next, and let me tell you, that sauce was straight-up crack—more on the sweet side than spicy, but still rich, saucy, and cheesy perfection with the chorizo and Oaxaca cheese bringing it all together. The kimchi was also excellent, adding just the right amount of tangy spice to complement everything. And to top it all off, we were treated to Sugar-Dusted Beignets—light, fluffy, and simply Soooo good!

Everything about Haenyeo was top-notch, from the impeccable service to the unforgettable flavors. Can’t wait to come back—highly recommend!

A cultural enrichment type restaurant.  It's a quaint restaurant that gives you the feeling of being in Albania.  You can tell the owners have pride in their culture.  Truly a hug from Albania that makes you feel like you’re there.  The authentic flavors did not disappoint. The staff is courteous and professional and super accommodating.  The food over exceeded our expectations.  Best dining experience I’ve had this week in NYC.

My first time trying Albanian food. It was very delicious and wholesome. The restaurant itself feels like you’re entering someone’s home. It felt very warm and cozy. The dishes tasted home cooked too. The flavors were full without feeling too heavy. The lamb was super tender and not gamey. Service was excellent and our waitress gave great recommendations! Id love to come back to try more of the dishes.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Absolutely amazing experience at Ça Ka Qëllue in Manhattan! The food was outstanding—rich flavors, beautifully prepared, and truly authentic. Every dish on the table was delicious and comforting.
The service was top-notch as well. John was incredibly attentive, friendly, and made sure we were taken care of the entire time. You can really feel the passion for both food and hospitality here.
Highly recommend this place if you’re in NYC—can’t wait to come back!

Albanian food is completely underrated and doesn't get nearly the attention it deserves.  This was my first time trying this cuisine and I wasn't disappointed.  I had the pepper dip appetizer which reminded me of a mildly spicy and perfectly balanced fondue served with fresh baked bread similar to a pita or puffy Naan.  For the entrée, I had the Tava Kosi, which is braised lamb served over an egg custard.  The custard reminded me of the inside of a quiche but with a much softer texture.  I went for Christmas dinner while visiting New York and the atmosphere and ambiance inside the restaurant could not have been better.  The interior looks like an old European tavern with rustic brick walls.  Cannot recommend this restaurant highly enough.  Extremely tasty food at an amazingly low price point.

First time trying Albanian food and really didn't know what to expect, but wow! This did not disappoint.

My group of 4 ordered a few things to share:

- Sausage dip
- Sesame baked cheese
- Fli
- Mantia (Tava)
- Qofte Shari
- Mixed meat combo (excluding the liver and qofte)

Everything was absolutely delicious, it's really hard to choose a favorite. The bread was so soft and fluffy, I dipped it in everything that I could.

The inside was super cozy, staff was great, will definitely be coming back to try more of the menu!

The staff at Yemenat were so gracious with me and my friend! We were a walk-in on a very busy day and still managed to get a table after a very short wait. The ambiance was warm and lively. The food was something to write home about! Absolutely rich and delicious! I had the lamb haneeth and the beef fahsa. Talk about flavor! I wish my stomach could take it all in, but the portions were so generous. Just when I thought it couldn’t get any better? I got dessert: The bent assahan was out of this world! Light, flaky, buttery. My goodness. Thank you so much Yemenat for a remarkable meal.

One of the best restaurants we’ve tried in NY! So so recommended.

The young waiter was kind, knowledgeable and professional. The kitchen delivers exquisite meals very quickly and you barely wait. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming.

You have unlimited homemade hot chai, which is ideal during winter.

We strongly recommend trying and supporting this place. We will come back!

It was our first time trying a Yemeni restaurant, and we were very impressed. The food was incredibly flavorful, bold, and colorful. I especially loved the Hadrami rice. The Chicken Haneeth, a traditional Yemeni dish with tender, slow-cooked chicken marinated in aromatic spices, was excellent.

I highly recommend making a reservation, as the restaurant is popular. We’ve visited twice on weekends, and both times it was full and crowded; otherwise, the wait time can be around an hour. The space and number of tables are limited.

Portions are very generous — we couldn’t finish everything and took some food home. The pomegranate drink was also great.

The only downside is if you’re seated near the entrance — every time the door opens, cold air comes in, which can be uncomfortable in winter. Installing a small vestibule or air curtain at the entrance would really help during winter.

A wonderful Michelin Bib Gourmand Yemeni restaurant in Bayridge. The large shafoot makes great platform to enjoy bubbling beef fahsa and the other dishes. Muva whole branzino came out tend on top and crispy on the skin , Lamb haneeth a little tougher than I expected. The dishes came out fast and hot, waiter kept waters refilled and we all tried the complimentary hot beverage. A great delicious inexpensive spot to take your family to.

Yemenat delivers an outstanding dining experience from start to finish.
The food, service, atmosphere, and cleanliness were all exceptional, and everything we ordered was full of flavor and beautifully prepared.

🍽️ Food Quality
Every dish was excellent and authentically prepared.

We ordered:
• Beef Fahsa
• Lamb Haneeth
• Hummus
• Rashoosh (fresh Yemeni bread)

Drinks:
• Fresh pomegranate juice
• Aseer Leem (mint lemon drink)

The meats were tender and deeply flavorful.
The bread was fresh and paired perfectly with the dishes.
The drinks were refreshing and clearly made with care.

Everything tasted fresh, balanced, and authentic.

👨‍🍳 Service
Customer service was excellent.
The staff was welcoming, attentive, and genuinely kind.

Many staff members speak Arabic, which is a big plus in this neighborhood and very helpful for Arabic-speaking guests.
Communication was smooth, respectful, and professional.

🏠 Atmosphere & Cleanliness
The restaurant is beautifully designed, warm, and inviting.
The dining area is clean, well organized, and comfortable.

The bathroom was exceptionally clean, including no unpleasant odor, which always reflects strong attention to hygiene and detail.

🥗 Vegetarian Options
There is a dedicated vegetarian section on the menu.
Options like hummus, vegetable dishes, and sides are clearly listed and well prepared.

Vegetarians will find good choices here.

🥘 Dietary Considerations
The staff is knowledgeable about ingredients and helpful if you have dietary questions.
Dishes are freshly prepared and customizable where possible.

🚗 Parking
Parking can be somewhat difficult, as this is a busy area.

Options include:
• Paid street parking nearby

Plan a little extra time if arriving during peak hours.

👶 Kid-Friendliness
The restaurant is suitable for families.
Spacious seating and a calm environment make it comfortable for children.

♿ Wheelchair Accessibility
The restaurant is wheelchair accessible.
There is sidewalk access that allows entry into the restaurant, and the interior layout is manageable for mobility needs.

✅ Final Recommendation
Yemenat is one of the best Yemeni dining experiences I have had.
Authentic food, outstanding service, a clean and welcoming environment, and thoughtful attention to detail make this place truly special.

I would highly recommend Yemenat and will absolutely be returning.

Sublime. We ordered every dish on the menu except the clams and it was consistently excellent across very single dish - I don’t remember the last time I had a meal like that, because most restaurants have clear stars in their menus and then other dishes are just ok, but here everything was a banger. Favorites - scallop and leek custard, egg and blue crab, wagyu crostini, and the panna cotta (I don’t even like panna cotta and yet this was one of the best desserts I’ve ever had). Can’t wait to come back for dinner or in another season!

Bravo. I’ve determined that this would officially be my last meal. Everything was perfect. The restaurant itself is super cosy. The service was excellent, relaxed. The food was interesting and flavourful. We tried a number of fun wines that paired well our food.

My only complaint is how hard it was to get a reservation 😆

An excellent operation with a chill vibe and a creative menu, taking amazing meals up a notch in unique ways. The Tartare Crostini is well formed and very flavorful, the salad’s cream and seasonings took some mixing up to get used to but that was good. Brown butter Crab with bread was great, and my two favorite starters the Grilled Octopus and the Seafood Rice. The octopus had perfect char and a sweet delicious taste paired great with the egg. The Seafood Rice was a great blend of fish stocked rice and cold fish as a topping. Then the Pork Collar, I loved this it’s a perfect preparation. Great portion with a beautiful seasoned top layer and a wonderful fatty center. We didn’t care much for the side, which for a dish this pricey you’d like solid side as a base but this gets a pass. Lastly to finish off the Panna Cotta was straight up great, safest dessert option.

Yes, it is hard to get in. But once you are in, good lord it is great. First off, you are made to feel like you are a regular at a neighborhood eatery. Then every course is perfect and beautiful. The suggested wines were outstanding and unique. The bartender, Sam, obviously enjoyed talking to me about the pairings even though I was a stranger. Sure didn't feel like one!

Four Horsemen feels like stumbling into a very well kept secret that somehow never tries to impress you… and still does.

I decided to try getting in without a reservation and luckily they thoughtfully keep bar and window seats available for walk-ins. The best approach is to line up right when the kitchen opens, or wait until the initial 5pm dinner rush tapers off and secure a seat at the bar.

The dining room is quietly romantic but a bit snug nonetheless creating a relaxed, understated atmosphere. Service is genuinely warm and technically precise without a hint of theatrics, striking an ideal balance of professionalism and ease.

The menu consists of tapas-style plates that are intentionally restrained. With minimal ingredients and thoughtful execution, each dish allows the quality of the product to shine rather than relying on excess or embellishment. The result is food that feels confident, focused, and deeply satisfying.

Four Horsemen is refined without feeling formal, and thoughtful without being precious, making it a place worth the effort, even on short notice.

Absolutely delicious food and its own mix on a variety of Persian cuisine. Service was great with thoughtful staff. Only note I would make is that we were 5people for a 6person reservation and they charged us 20$ ( yes I agreed to it when I made reso but this change is completely normal for dinner). I told them immediately when we arrived. This is despite the table really only being for 5 people to begin with. 5 stars for everything but management. I would give it 2 stars. The extra star is for decor music and design, last for service which was great. I would recommend the lamb shank and steak. Egg plant was delicious and a variety of very tasty drinks. I would recommend this spot, but for a second time visit for me, this far in BK and poor management where it took almost 90 mins for our meal to be served...I'm likely not to go back. Worth the trip but only once

Absolutely loved Sofreh. Every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. The atmosphere feels calm, elegant, and truly special. The staff were kind and attentive, and the whole experience had that warm Persian charm that makes you want to come back. Definitely one of the best restaurants in New York City.

I don’t say this lightly: Sofreh is truly one of the city’s standout restaurants. Every dish reflects a level of mastery that’s hard to overstate. The kitchen takes authentic Persian flavors and elevates them with real creativity—the ribeye “kebab” is a perfect example. I was equally taken with the eggplant and whey dip; it was so good that I bought their cookbook afterward just to understand the sorcery behind it. And a special shoutout to the wonderful service team, who made the experience even better.

I absolutely loved the atmosphere at Sofreh. The space is so beautiful and thoughtfully designed, and even the staff uniforms added to how stylish and put together everything felt. The whole place has such a cute and welcoming vibe, and the staff were beyond nice.

The food was fantastic. The dishes had small creative twists while still staying very authentic to traditional Persian flavors. The tahdig is an absolute must. It was the best I have ever had in my life. Just note that it is limited to one order per table. Portions are not very sharable unless you order several different dishes, which is what we ended up doing.

I also tried the kabob, which was delicious, especially with the pomegranate sauce. That said, it was more like a steak than a traditional kabob, so just something to keep in mind. Sadly, I could not get a picture of it because it was so good we ate it right away.

Overall, Sofreh is a beautiful restaurant with amazing food, wonderful staff, and a great atmosphere. I would definitely come back and recommend it to anyone looking for an elevated Persian dining experience in New York.

Insatiable food. The flavors of each dish were unique to its own but combined and complimented each other so beautifully.

Service was great - everyone was so kind. They were also well knowledgeable on the dishes and described the drinks and food with such detail! The suggestions were amazing.

Unfortunately didn’t take any pics but here’s the dessert. I was so full but I couldn’t stop eating the ice cream.

10/10 through and through.

I’m glad I got to try this restaurant. Located right next to the S train, Hart’s is a seafood, olive oil, simple menu focused eatery.

I appreciated the quality of the olive oil and the bread. The lamb burger was pretty damn good too. The tomato salad was one of the best I’ve had. A bit too pricey for the food and quantity, but hey, I’d come back again.
Most dishes except clam toast polish panceda were awesome. Clams were bit too tiny with not much of meat in it. Atmosphere was good. Service was great.

Loved everything about this place! The food was uncomplicated in the best way - fresh, straightforward, and delicious. The clam toast and gem salad stood out as particularly incredible. It's a great place for a date or small group to share plates so you can try a lot of different things! The atmosphere is cozy and cute, and the service was great. We will be coming back here regularly!

Hart’s is a stylish and cozy spot. Made a reservation earlier this week for a 6:30PM dinner and there were a few other patrons. By the time we were done, the place was full and lively! Since it is a small spot, making a reservation is a good call. The food was delicious and all had a fun ingredient detail to it. Drinks are great too! Go check out Hart for an intimate dinner experience.

Amazing! Our favorite restaurant in the area. We had a very attentive waitress last night and every dish we ordered was executed beautifully.

Our favorites were the pork Milanese, their seasonal cabbage salad, and their lamb burger. Will come back again soon.

Dubrovnik is one of those rare places where dining is an experience, not just eating out.

First, I was surprised to see that this place has dedicated parking for guests - rarest of the rare for someone from NYC! The host was super quick to offer a table and help us with their best seasonal offerings. Their seafood menu is one of the best in the region. Whether you like oysters or fish, you're not gonna be disappointed. The drinks are prepped with attention to detail as well. I had Sangria, and it was so good I had a repeat. The place maintains high hygiene standards.

After dining in hundreds of restaurants in NYC, for the first time, I witnessed a restaurant replace the tablecloth after it's been used.

What deserves a special mention? The food and hygiene standards just make this one of the best places to dine.

What could be better? Nothing for now - they're doing a great job!

I visit Dubrovnik Restaurant about four or five times a year, and it never disappoints. The parking can be quite difficult, so I highly recommend using the valet service to start your evening comfortably.

This place offers a level of Croatian cuisine that is hard to find in the NY/NJ area. Their philosophy is clearly about respecting the ingredients. The wood-grilled Branzino is exceptional; the fire gives it a subtle sweetness and the texture is perfect. We also enjoyed the Lamb Chops and Aged Rib Eye Steak, both cooked beautifully.

The appetizers are always fresh and vibrant. The Marinated Anchovies and Nona’s Octopus Salad had great texture with no fishiness. I particularly love the Pear and Apple Salad—the crisp fruit provides a wonderful balance to the savory dishes. The Cuttlefish Risotto is served perfectly al dente, rich with flavor but not heavy.

The service is generally skilled and attentive. We did have a small mix-up where a server mistook soy sauce for black vinegar, but it was an understandable mistake that didn't affect our enjoyment of the meal.

The wine list is a real highlight, especially the Croatian selections. We had the Stina Cuvée by the glass; it was excellent for the price, with enough acidity to pair perfectly with the seafood. It’s a dining experience I always look forward to returning to.

This was a delightful Croatian dining experience.  Admittedly, while enjoyable, I wasn't blown away.   I liked the free valet parking, as parking can be difficult in this area.  The atmosphere was very noisy, making it difficult to carry on a conversation.  While I enjoyed the 2 piece live band, they too were quite loud.  My meal itself was very good, but not spectacular.  I started with the chicken soup.  I enjoyed the large pieces of tender chicken in a savory broth, but didn't find this to be much different from any non-Croatian chicken soup.  For my main, I had the stuffed chicken breast with asparagus.  The chicken was tasty, but surprisingly was a bit tough.  Lastly, for dessert, we shared the palacinke with walnut cream.  It was creamy and delicious, and was a nice way to wrap up the meal.  Others in my party ordered the Branzino and had a much more positive dining experience.  I suppose if you dine here, you might be better off with the seafood options.
Great food and service! The appetizers have really large portions, almost like a main course portion. All delicious!

We just got back from a vacation in Croatia and finally decided to try this Croatian restaurant in New Rochelle - we had always known about it but never visited since we weren’t familiar with Croatian cuisine. After falling in love with the food during our trip, we knew it was time. And we’re so glad we did! The lamb and fish were outstanding - almost like being back in Croatia. And the sourdough bread… OMG! Absolutely delicious!

A 12 degrees evening before the anticipated arrival of the first big ice and snow storm of 2026 and wanted to have "last meal" of sorts before the great hibernation.
We had 5 lobsters-split broiled, braised abalone-sea cucumber-shitake, a giant steamed branzino (live from the on-site fish tank), dried scallop fried rice, braised crab yee-noodles, cold platter with suckling pig, beef, pickled vegetables and jellyfish, a sautéed seafood dish with sugar snap peas-squid-conch, chicken-abalone soup, fried chicken, fried crab claw with shrimp, deserts were a fruit platter and also sweet red bean soup.
Service was quick, but very, very rushed. Dishes came out every 5 minutes and were served and distributed. The next dish arrived before the current one could be finished and they brought us plastic boxes to pack what we couldn't finish. Food quality was fresh, but not particularly flavorful, slightly overcooked as seafood needs to be pretty exact.
Difficult to stay fully booked in the current economy, but the entire restaurant of about 400 seats, was filled, as well as the private rooms, on this evening.

Came here before and it was very good. Today’s visit was on New Year’s Day so it was super chaotic. We waited about 30-40 mins for a table for 8. The carts moved quickly and we were able to get what we wanted almost immediately. There were a few items we had to wait for. Today they didn’t have turnip cake. Some waiters were very helpful and scouted the dimsum items we wanted and ordered additional items. Others were typical and brushed us off. Any ordered food takes very long. They also have Hong Kong milk tea. Service is in Cantonese. Didn’t notice if they were super quick to help in English.

Pretty good dim sum, bookmarked this place for a while since my friend recommended it. A little bit far to get to in brooklyn's chinatown. Expect to wait before you get seats. I didn't see that many carts that went around, might be because we got there a little closer to 12:30pm, busy even on a weekday during lunch.

You might want to ask them for the menu to bring the food out if the carts don't come by. I think the food is flavorful, but the service was a little bit questionable since we were waiting for the carts to come by for a while and it didn't feel like there was a lot of variety.

There were definitely more items on the menu that they didn't bring out. Overall, I think it's good place to try once, I'm not sure if I would be back again.

It serves really authentic and traditional push cart style dim sum at all hours. Do expect a queue on weekend. You will also find extra ordinary and non typical dim sum dishes that please your appetite such as beef offal and pepper beef ribs.

I had a really disappointing experience here. The waitress that served us was very pushy—she kept trying to upsell us to the most expensive dishes. On top of that, she spoke my hometown dialect and constantly interrupted our family conversation, which felt extremely rude and unprofessional.

The presentation of the dishes looked nice, but the flavors were nowhere near what they used to be. It really seems like they’ve changed the chef. The Vancouver Crab Lotus Leaf Rice was especially awful—the sticky rice was far too greasy and completely lacked any lotus leaf aroma.

Considering the high prices, the overall quality was very poor. Definitely not coming back.

Omg this place was amazing!! Everything was super freaking delicious where we were happy to spend the money. I do have one small complaint that we opted to order the LARGE Henny Colada cocktails but were not warned that they were $60 each!! Luckily,we could afford it but I know that it could be a problem for some people. The drinks were tasty, strong and had 3 small Hennessy bottles as floaters do they were totally worth the $ but still, a little warning would've been nice.

Every single dish had soooo much flavor!!

I had am amazing time at Seis Vecinos. Shelley was my waitress. She was amazing. The food was fantastic as well. I ordered the Seafood Paella. It was perfectly seasoned and came with a salad . They sung Happy Birthday to me and made me feel so special.  I will definitely be back. I'm so lucky to have this gem of a restaurant so close in my neighborhood. You don't need to go to Manhattan for excellent service.

It ridiculous how you spend your money here because its not a charity you are paying your hard worked money and the service is unprofessional the orders are wrong and its not worth it. Sorry Seis Vecinos you have lost your touch even the quality and taste of the food you will be loosing customers well I know you already have. Get it right you had a dream and made it happen so be consistent and don't try to run your own people for their money.
This has become my new favorite place to eat… I highly recommend it!! Food is so good and if you want to drink this is the place…ask for a large drink, I dare you…incredible…so good!!!
I had the most amazing seafood soup 🙌🏼 5 stars !!! My wife had one her favorite dishes, sauteed liver. She absolutely loved it. The desert was delicious. A nice big piece of chocolate cake.

Such a delicious meal!!!! The oysters were so fresh; all of their seafood is super fresh. The grilled octopus was cooked perfectly it was soft with a slightly crispy outside from being char grilled. It had a great char flavor paired with the olive oil and vinegar was perfect. The pork souvlaki was my favorite of the night. The pork was juicy and had great flavor. I really like their tzatziki it’s very fresh with lots of cucumber. The lamb chops were also pretty good. I don’t usually like lamb because it’s gamey but this wasn’t and it was also cooked perfectly. They also gave delicious bread with a mashed olive dip at the start and a custard baklava type dessert for free! 8.5/10

This is the place to get seafood.  Very busy, but do t let that discourage you because at the end you'll be rewarded with some real, real fresh and delicious seafood. The octopus is simply fenomenal, the special combo seafood for two is amazing and the stuff filet  of sole very tasty.  All this complemented with a glass of sangria. Can't beat it. If you don't have reservation get ready to wait for at least 45 minutes, but it will be worth it.

This elegant, authentic greek seafood restaurant constantly has a 45 minute wait on Friday and Satueday nights. The meal is worth it, crispy olive bread with tapenade in olive oil, greek salads, a dozen varieties of fish including shark and swordfish as well as beef, chicken and lamb. The seafood pasta and the salmon were exceptional. Greek sides such as chard and lemon potatos follow the large entree portions. Excellent wine selection. Complementary house dessert with every meal. A staple of Ditmars, Tavern Kyclades never disappoints.

We visited Taverna Kyclades and had a wonderful experience. The service was impeccable—every staff member, even those who weren’t our primary server, made sure we had everything we needed.

For appetizers, we enjoyed crab cakes with fried zucchini. For dinner, my husband had a white fish stuffed with crab meat, while I had a pasta dish featuring five types of seafood: octopus, mussels, clams, scallops, and shrimp. Every bite was full of flavor, and the portions were incredibly generous—we had to take half of our food home and enjoyed it for a couple more days!

Overall, the combination of excellent service, delicious food, and large portions made this a truly delightful dining experience.

We have been wanting to go here for a very long time, but just never quite made it. That was a mistake! They don't take reservations so we waited for a while. It was fine the area has a lot to see and do, so we walked around. We had the village salad, Kyclades special (seafood platter),grilled chicken, rice, and potatoes. There was only 2 of us, and enough food to feed 4! Each bite was better than the next! All the food was fresh and delicious, and reasonable! We will be going back a lot! Great Greek food!🇬🇷

Ate here recently for my birthday and everyday was so delicious! We ordered a half portion of the squid ink calamarata, roasted beet salad and two specials crispy fried sea bass over white beans and a duck confit rotolo. Everything tastes so delicious and my favorite was the squid ink pasta
The Beet Salad is AMAZING and the best you'll ever have (nothing beets it). Di's service was friendly, honest and welcoming - give her a raise. :-)

I stopped by their stand at the McCarren Park farmers market and all of their baked goods looked amazing, but I grabbed a chocolate almond croissant for $6.25. Steep price but this is one of the best croissants I have ever eaten. Why do more places not mix the almond and chocolate together?!?!? This is one of the best things I have ever eaten.

The restaurant has a nice atmosphere and interesting decor. The service is great. The pretzel was somewhat dry. The arancini was good, a bit dense, the sauce was flavorful. The squid ink pasta was slightly overcooked, both the pasta and the squid and the sauce didn't have a lot of flavor. Overall the food was fine but nothing was memorable.

Chef Chris’s Slow Braised Lamb sandwich is an absolute standout—tender lamb perfectly complemented by the crunch of pickled red onions and carrots, fresh arugula, and a spicy yogurt sauce, all wrapped in a flavorful curried flatbread. The best part? Everything is made in-house, and you can truly taste the difference in every bite.

The entire staff, from the servers to the bakers, was incredibly friendly and welcoming. Natasha, the manager, made me feel like a part of the family and even sent me home with a loaf of their house-made Blueberry Buckwheat Levain, which was just as delicious as it sounds. It’s those personal touches and genuine hospitality that make this place so special.

Whether you’re a local or visiting Brooklyn, this place is a must-try. Chef Chris and his team put so much care into every detail, and it shows. Highly recommend!

Finally snagged a reservation! And yes, it was worth the hype. The atmosphere is amazing and warm. Our server was wonderful and kind. Love the sourdough with whipped ricotta. The mackerel toast was delicious. Red snapper ceviche excellent. And the whole dry-aged branzino, so good. The server also helped debone the fish and he did a great job. Would definitely come back again!

100/10. The culinary highlight of our NYC trip.

We ordered a bunch from the menu, and there wasn’t a dish we didn’t love.

We loved the Hiramsa to start, fresh and had a tang to it. The grilled mackerel is a must and comes on beautiful sourdough made fresh. It may not be visually appealing for some, but I recommend you try it!

The black cod was perfectly cooked, covered in an amazing sauce and salad. The whole butterflied trout was the standout item, packed full of Smokey flavour and different experiences you get switching from one side of the fish to the other is unique and delicious. This dish was what brought Theodora to my attention and it did not disappoint.

The service was fantastic and the waiters were tentative but we loved the chefs table experience. Eating in front of the grill and watching the food go through different stages if cooking so much fun. The chef was very friendly and made time to talk to us over the course of our dinner. If you are a small part, book the countertop table.

We spent about $200 for 2 people, we didn’t have alcoholic drinks.

Theodora is fully booked out weeks ahead, a reservation is a must, good luck getting one. I absolutely recommend this place and will be back the next time I’m in NY.

We absolutely LOVED this place! The hype is real!!
We were lucky to be sat at the chefs counter right next to the expo. We got to watch everyone work and they are a well oiled machine.
This is the best Mediterranean food we’ve had in NYC. All the dishes benefit from the wood firing even if they aren’t directly prepared on the grill which was a beautiful surprise. For example the oil on the hummus. Mind blown

Favorite bite of the night…the tilefish ceviche with wood fired pineapple. Wow!

Also and most importantly, the service was elite. Our server Zoe was just so great, friendly knowledgeable, attentive, all the things!
We also got to meet and chat a bit with the GM, Katie. So nice!

We can’t wait to go back and try everything we don’t get to try this time.

Theodora Restaurant absolutely lives up to the hype—even if getting a reservation feels like winning the lottery. Every dish is bold, flavorful, and confidently executed, especially the seafood-focused menu. The appetizers were flawless across the board, and the fish dishes truly shine. Don’t miss the sourdough (elite), yellowfin tuna, salmon king crudo, and the ceviche—standout bites that justify the buzz. The lamb was a bit too strong on aroma for my taste, and while the octopus was good, it wasn’t the star. Still, an exceptional meal overall and 100% worth the chase.

The team behind Theodora has truly captured the intimate Brooklyn-aesthetic. I loved the open kitchen layout and curated seating. We were in a curved booth right in the middle of it all (best for people watching) but would so come back to experience the chefs counter or alcove or front seats by the window.

Now the food is sublime. The Middle Eastern, Brazilian, Mexican flavors blend together so nicely for an exceptional taste in each bite. We started with the Hiramasa and Seeded Laffa. Holy I would eat five plates of the Hiramasa if that were socially acceptable… the dip with the warm Laffa is also really tasty. For mains, we got the Octopus and Whole Butterflied Trout which were both yum. I’d say the potato chips and brussel sprouts added a unique dimension to the octopus dish. To end the meal we got the chocolate cake, which as the reviews mention, was perfectly sweet and paired well with the mascarpone and olive oil on top. Bliss.

The cocktails are also noteworthy. We enjoyed the La Cigua and Mayahuel and would recommend the former for a smoky cucumber flavor and the latter for a savory mezcal martini.

A last note on service – the staff is really friendly and knows the menu well. Our dishes were paced out in multiple courses and were brought out fresh. You can tell the chef team enjoys their work and it was exciting to watch!

Highly recommend a visit, or two!

From the moment we walked in, R40 delivered a true five-star experience. Warm greeting, intimate atmosphere, and a room that feels thoughtfully put together without trying too hard.

Service was excellent. David our server was attentive and precise, and the general manager stopping by our table was a great touch. The pacing felt natural and unforced.

The food was outstanding. The skirt steak was perfectly cooked with clean, intentional plating, and the red snapper was bright, crisp, and well balanced. This kitchen clearly understands restraint, proportion, and timing. The cocktails were equally dialed in and thoughtfully executed.

Everything worked together seamlessly. Food, service, and atmosphere all aligned. R40 is doing something special, and I’ll definitely be back.

Pretty good spot,, but prices are a bit steep
For the type of food.  The pasta was rich, the fish excellent but next time i will stick to steak.  Enjoy

My first time here, everything was just perfect. I wanted a nice date with my boyfriend and the lights, the jazz live music and the food made everything just perfect. Shout out to Allison, our server, for so friendly and delicate service. She dame sure that we had our food as we wanted and at the time we wanted. My favorite dish was the crab empanada, it was different from what I’m used to but that empanada just hits different. The atmosphere was calm and nice. Remember that the live music is only Wednesday. Great experience, we will definitely come back.

We arrived 5 minutes prior to reservation but waited around 20 to 30 minutes until our table was ready. Service was amazing, the wait time can't be blamed on the staff as those who occupied the table we were waiting for seemed to just be sitting there sipping water. The food was amazing overall and staff was very friendly. Totally would recommend the wings and rosemary fries!

We had an amazing dinner at R40 LIC! Everything we ordered — the Arroz Negro, Arugula Pesto Gnocchi, and the 10 oz Prime Black Angus Skirt Steak — was absolutely delicious. Every dish was full of flavor and perfectly cooked. The service was just as wonderful — everyone was so friendly, and our server (the tall gentleman) was especially kind and attentive. Highly recommend this spot if you’re in Long Island City!

Went on a Sunday line was rather long but moves quick. Food was great got the BEC scallion pancake and another item I don’t remember the name of and the custard toast. Ah and a oolong tea to warm up and was it all down

This place is worth all the hype and the ridiculously long line out the door. The mochi donut is a must it’s so doughy and best served warm. I ate a shrimp scallion pancake and would order the same thing again but it was also so good I am interested in trying the whole menu. They also have excellent house sauce. I came here in a party of three at noon on a Sunday. The line was out the door but we got a table pretty fast. By the time we were out an hour later the line was gone. It’s not really suitable for large groups and mostly ideal for two people but you can make three or four work. I’m excited to come back here and try new things. 10/10 recommend!!

It’s just as good as people say it is!! The BEC scallion is amazing! It’s just the perfect combo of everything. The only thing is that it’s quite oily the grease soaked through the bag. The mochi donut is amazing with a chewy texture and lightly sweetened. The fantuan is great with crunchy pork floss.

great food. 4.5 stars because the scallion pancake egg and cheese was not as crispy as the williamsburg location, and the outside seating got a bit hectic because there were too many people waiting. Still one of the best breakfast or lunch meals you can get in the area. I’m stingy but this is worth the money.

Ambiance (5/5): Plenty of seating both indoor and outdoor. Very minimalistic and open space with a bathroom inside
Service (N/A): It is an order at the counter and they bring out the food to you. You grab your own utensils and water.
Mortadella scallion pancake ($18) (5/5): Okay the hype was worth it… It was very large and super filling. The pancake had a nice exterior crunch and all the ingredients melted together wonderfully. There was also a side dipping sauce that reminded of thousand island but also tasted wonderful with the pancake. I was full literally all day.
Twice Baked Bolo Bao PB ($8): The melted chocolate on the bottom was superb but overall was an okay muffin. It had too much going on.
This was an expensive breakfast. The scallion pancake IMO should not be that expensive. However, there’s so much more on the menu that I want to try so I will definitely be back.

A quote from my boyfriend after our appetizers: "ill never be a mother, but i imagine this feeling is the equivalent of holding your child for the first time"

My new fav spot, how this place isn't packed out is actually beyond me because it was easily one of the best meals I've ever had in New York and I've eaten a lottttt.
Everything I could hope for from an NYC seafood restaurant comes alive here.
Ambience is so nice lighting is perfect doesn't get too noisy but still feels alive, service is excellent, cozy but cool.

The food is just outstanding, I literally recommend everything like truly. Each dish was like wow I've never had something like that before and I need it again and again. In fact, I went two days in a row because I just had to get some appetizers again and try some more mains. I'm actually obsessed. I would be here much more often if I lived somewhat closer, but I will with no hesitation make the trek from Manhattan anytime I start craving it.

I honestly recommend every single dish that I have posted in this review (it's also every single dish that I've ordered in my times coming here) , but I think for me (i really love raw seafood) I can't go here without ordering the wild shrimp appetizer and the lobster tostada. The lobster tostada is one of the craziest things I've ever had I don't know how they made it taste like that and the textures (im salivating as i write) and they give you so much lobster i was swooning. Not that everything else isn't also perfection because it all really is in their own ways, but as a lobster lover this just tickled me.
Love their drink menu, non alcoholic list is pretty limited but what they do offer is tasty, for low ABV they have a lot of options featuring sherry, sweet wines, and amaros etc
Dessert was great im forgetting what it is called atm, but alongside the creamy looking one is their italian ice and flavors rotate.

This is our second time coming back to this restaurant. It’s a small cozy spot where I love sitting by the bar to see the action. The food was still amazing.

It’s our first time trying the violet hour though. We should have totally done that the first time. $45 PP - we can choose 3 dishes each. It was a tasing menu where dishes were supposed to come in half portion. It’s definitely bigger than half portion, we feel it’s almost like 2/3 of a real portion. The 2 of us with 6 dishes to share - we were full! Great value! Will definitely do this again if we come back between 5-6.

One star deducted to the service was because it seems we didn’t have a dedicated server. No one told us about violet hour nor special of the day x 2. We had to keep asking about it. Imagine if we didn’t overhead about the violet hour from the table next to us, we’d have totally missed it. So does the special of the day

The lighting is not photo friendly,  so don't judge the dishes by my pics.   The food was excellent.   Don't skip the anchovies or the iberico steaklette.   Cocktails were just as good and they even served me something off menu that turned out to be my favorite drink of the night. Excellent find in the neighborhood.

Incredible meal, no- experience. We got the chefs counter and were greeted by Winnie. She was helpful with an amazing drink recommendation. Then came the scallop tacos which I hear are only available on Friday/Saturday and Sunday if you’re feeling lucky (they run out)! The stars of the show were the seafood sausage and the squid. Can’t wait to go back!

I’ve been eating in NYC and similar establishments all over Europe for 40 years. I enjoyed the owners other places especially Txikito.  I don’t remember the last time I felt like having a slice of pizza after a meal.

Hushpuppies had a nice flavor. No complaints there.
Amberjack was good, appreciated the tomato water especially.  But when sharing with another, jute a couple of small pieces each.  One of the smallest “crudo” dishes I’ve seen.
A special of polenta fritters with babaganoush and salmon was delectable, but it’s more like a $20+ amuse bouche.
Rissotto was flavor packed and smoky. But again, poor value and a dish that felt like an excellent side dish midway.  Would have loved to pair this with some fish or something. This is a fisherie with zero cooked fish on the menu other than a very expensive whole fish special.
Squid a la Plancha - not as good as I hoped. Overly sweet and one-note until you mix all the sauces.

5 dishes, one drink - $170.  We could have easily ordered two more dishes but simply didn’t feel like paying more for such poor value.
Went for Thanksgiving lunch special and it was awesome and very filling and delicious. The service was Al’s excellent. Looking forward to coming back.

The place has an upscale casual feel. The service is excellent, fast and attentive. The dishes are creative and delicious. The hash browns were perfectly cooked and the topping is outstanding. The croquettes didn't have a lot of fish taste, the tomato sauce was great. The burger was outstanding, juicy, cheesy, the crust was a bit salty. The cheesecake was fluffy, creamy. Would definitely recommend!

Food was mediocre at best. Service was fine. Spacious. Mediocre across the board. Nothing bad at all. But also nothing remarkable. Seems popular with the locals.

The green salad was good. Crisp. Fresh. Good flavors. The hash browns were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Great creme fraiche dip.

The pork chop was small. You can sort of share it. The salsa verde was just okay. Not evenly cooked. One side was more tender than the other. Rather thin. A unremarkable dish I would. Very pedestrian. More like someone's home cooking.

The gemelli pasta was okay. I can make the same dish at home. Just a few shavings of guanciale. Nothing bad about this dish. But again nothing remarkable.

The burger we saw on Instagram was good. But it's a mix of beef and pork. The taste and texture is more like an Italian sausage. The slaw on top was good. But definitely not worth the trip to get to. Again, just mediocre food. I can make a more beefy burger at home.

The basque cheese cake was a tad overcooked. I think 15 min LESS in the oven would have resulted in a more creamy center. It was a big slice but it was dry. The texture was spongy and cakey overall. Not great.

The maple pie was the star of the entire dinner. It was light and velvety. There was a hint of brown butter. Not overly sweet. With a night amount of maple 🍁. The crust was flaky and crispy. The dollop of cream on top was just excellent. This was an incredible slice of pie.

Service was good overall. Water was filled. Dishes were taken away promptly. The wait staff were attentive. The bathrooms were clean.

But the food was overall underwhelming.

We hosted a private event at Gus's (dinner after a city hall wedding) and had an AMAZING experience. The manager, Megan, was so helpful to work with throughout -- she was a thought partner on food and decor choices, she coordinated with our other vendors, and most importantly made sure that the event itself went off without a hitch! The ambiance was on point and the food was DELICIOUS -- all of our guests have been raving about it since then!! The staff was also super warm and helped make the event feel extra special. (An extra shout out to the bartender Andrew for cracking jokes all night). Highly recommend Gus's under any circumstance!!

We love Popina so we had to try Gus’s. Been wanting to go since they opened up and damn they did not disappoint. The whole family loved every bite of food. We got a bunch of appetizers. We would have been satisfied just eating them. Sooo good. For entrees,  the pork porterhouse had so much flavor and was perfectly cooked. Delicious. The burger was also one of the best I’ve ever had. Also, do not skip out on the desserts.

As always, this restaurant group always has great wines. The wine we ordered really put this meal over the top. A dining experience we will never forget.

5 stars for value. 5 stars for service 5 stars for food.

Came during restaurant week for brunch. It was $45 pp and well worth it. Firstly, every single dish was perfection. Had the muffin to start and it was warm and fluffy on the inside yet crisp on the outside.

Same for the empanadas - crispy but the filling was soft and delicious.

Probably one of the best omelettes, it was evenly cooked and the fillings (spinach and mushroom) were also seasoned and cooked to perfection. Not a bad bite throughout.

Finished with sorbets and it was the most flavourful sorbets, especially the lemon and raspberry. I was surprised how jam packed the flavour was.

Only downside was we order coffees and those took a really long time to come to the table.

This place used to have Michelin stars but now it feels more like a neighborhood spot. Little pricey for a casual meal but great for a first date, or to make someone’s day.

We visited Meadowsweet on a snowy Sunday for brunch and were immediately impressed by the warm and polished experience from the moment we walked in. The restaurant was fairly quiet because of the weather and our group of four was seated right away. Water was brought to the table immediately and the front of house staff seemed completely in sync. The service felt smooth and professional without ever being stiff.

None of us ordered cocktails and instead stuck with coffee which everyone at the table kept praising. It was rich, balanced, and exactly what you want on a cold morning.

To start we ordered the donuts and the empanadas. The donuts were fun and reminded me of sugar coated munchkins. They were good but not particularly memorable. The empanadas on the other hand were excellent in terms of flavor. The filling was well seasoned and satisfying. The only critique is their size. At nineteen dollars for three empanadas we all felt they could be a bit larger to really showcase the filling.

For my main dish I ordered the duck pastrami hash with sunny side eggs and it was phenomenal. The dish had great depth of flavor and the eggs were cooked perfectly. In hindsight I should have ordered the sourdough bread with the hash instead of as a starter. The bread would have been perfect for soaking up everything on the plate.

My girlfriend originally ordered the bacon omelette but was accidentally served the mushroom spinach omelette. Luckily the mistake worked in our favor because it ended up being one of the best dishes on the table. The eggs were incredibly fluffy and cooked perfectly. The mushrooms absorbed a ton of flavor and created a savory richness that balanced beautifully with the spinach. Nothing felt overpowering and every bite was well composed. I tried a bite myself and was equally impressed.

Another friend ordered the burger and really enjoyed it. It was simple, satisfying, and executed exactly how a good brunch burger should be.

Overall the experience was excellent. The atmosphere was comfortable, the service was attentive, and the food showed strong technique and balance across the board. If brunch is this good I can only imagine how strong their dinner service must be.

Considering the price point, the quality of the food, and the level of hospitality, Meadowsweet easily earns five out of five stars. I would happily come back for brunch again.

My wife (has celiac / gluten allergy) and I came here for my birthday, and it was an excellent experience. The servers here are kind, and knowledgeable/attentive about gluten cross contamination. And the food was fresh and very well cooked. The chicken roulade was juicy and the burger slapped. Definitely looking to come back again!

I came here for my birthday brunch with friends and had the best experience ! Staff was very kind and service was excellent. All the dishes were very tasty and you could tell the ingredients were fresh and very good quality (they use seasonal produce from their farm). I took the biscuit & poached eggs and French toast: each dish was flavorful and well balanced. They also had freshly squeezed orange juice so 10 / 10 for me. Thank you for the hospitality; will be back for dinner soon :)

This is the best place I've been. They did an excellent job at every single step. First of all, the service was top notch, everyone seemed to come out of a happy movie, always kind, sweet and more. Then it came the food, OMG, I ate my place with my eyes closed just savoring every bite, and my husband's burger was not far behind, the flavor of the meat was amazing. Finally, I truly enjoyed that the environment allowed conversations without loud music blasting my ears. Overall, a great place to have a wine and relax.

Mexican spot that is featured on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list.

The list features restaurants that serve good food for reasonable prices and Alta Calidad delivered.

Must Try’s:

Yuca Fries + Chipotle sauce - out of the park delicious and salty

Alta Queso Fundido - probably the best thing we had. Make sure you order this. SO GOOD.

Churros - do yourself a favor and leave some room for dessert

Solid choices:

Carne Asada Tacos - would be on my must but the price point for tacos feels a little criminal. Very good but damn almost $10 per taco is rough

Pork Shoulder Carnitas - very good but again the other plates just put this to shame

Leave it:

Drinks - not a fan. Hot chocolate came out tepid and the mixed drink was just okay. Next time I’ll stick to water or coke

Verdict - solid choice for Mexican, would recommend, not in a rush to come back NYC just has too many other places to try

I visited Alta Calidad while on the hunt for a Mexican spot during NY Restaurant Week and it did not disappoint. I ordered the Snapper Tostaditas, Carne Asada, and Churros. My favorite of the bunch was the Carne Asada. I would order that again if I returned. The service was great. The waitress answered any questions we had and the drinks came out fast. This was great value for a price of $45 (because it was during restaurant week). The ambiance was great, with natural lighting and good music. I would recommend this place to someone looking for slightly upscale Mexican food.

We had a really good meal at this Mexican restaurant. We ordered chicken tacos, shrimp tacos, and a margarita, and everything was fresh and full of flavor. The sauce on the tacos was absolutely delicious, adding the perfect touch to each bite.

The presentation was neat, and the restaurant itself was clean and well-organized. The atmosphere was pleasant, and we especially enjoyed the music playing in the background, which added to the experience.

If you’re looking for tasty food, a nice ambiance, and good music, this place is definitely worth a visit.

Taste-wise, the food was delicious, and the drinks were very good. The service was amazing, and I really like the location of this place.

However, the portion sizes were quite small. If you’re coming here just to have a drink and a light bite, it’s perfect. But if you’re arriving hungry and expecting a full meal, even two plates might not be enough to fill you up.

Would highly recommend. Excellent food and service. They accommodated a kid request to simplify the tacos and a vegetarian request to make the queso meat-free. Margaritas were good. Tacos and short rib entree were great as was the rice and beans side. Portion sizes were perfect. Tres Leche dessert was delicious. The music wasn't too loud, so were were able to easily carry on a conversation. My only observation was that the music genre didn't really match the restaurant but that was hardly an issue. 5 stars!

Great all around. Came off peak time and ordered a fresh Bee Sting as many have reviewed. It did not disappoint and this would be my go-to pizza many times! People around me were drinking and the drinks looked fantastic. I'm sure the rest of the food is great as well since my pizza was so good. Would love to come again and try a different pizza and any other foods. New York has so many good restaurants and I'm glad I found this one!

I met my friend in NYC, she was coming from Connecticut and I was coming from New Jersey and we stumbled apron Roberta’s at Penn Station. We were so happy we did, from the moment we walked in to the moment we left! Our server was  Camilo, the food runner was Nisaun, the bar tender was Hadji, they made the experience even better everything was great! We had a small issues which was corrected immediately and we could not have been happier! When we were ready for our check Jema, not sure if she was the GM or AGM came out to make sure all was good! She was just as amazing as her staff! Please keep this staff, now a days good staff is so had to find, I know because I am constantly looking! It is so wonderful to eat at a restaurant where the staff is happy and like there jobs! Thank you for a great meal and experience! We will definitely be back soon!

Really delicious meal here. I had heard a lot about the pizza, so was excited to try it. However, the pizza was actually not the star of the meal. The stracciatella and anchovies was far and away the strongest item we had. The caesar salad was also phenomenal, but the cheese was amazing.

The pizza was decent as well, but if we came back, we would likely lean on the appetizers more!

Roberta’s Pizza at Penny Station is such a hidden gem in New York! The location is super convenient, and the pizza… oh, the pizza is absolutely delicious — perfectly made, full of flavor, and with that authentic taste that wins you over right away.

What I really love is the little details: they have a bathroom (which is rare around here!), and right outside there’s a lovely square where you can sit and enjoy your slice in the open air. It makes the whole experience even more charming, with that laid-back city vibe.

It’s the kind of spot that combines convenience, amazing food, and a touch of charm in the atmosphere. A place I truly loved discovering and one that’s already on my list of must-stops! 🌿🍕
The pizza is wonderful, but don’t sleep on the dry-aged burger. 10/10 blissful, juicy, flavorful burger with gooey American cheese. Served with delicious mini potatoes

This place never disappoints. I’ve been here with my friends before, and this time I came with my husband. I tried to bring him for Valentine’s Day, but it was already fully booked, so I definitely recommend making a reservation, especially for important dates. We went during the week, and my husband absolutely loved it.🤗
The food was delicious. I always recommend starting with the eggplant Napolitano appetizer and the mini shawarmas. The Figtini cocktail🍸 and the Harissa 🥥dessert were amazing 😋 The place feels very warm and cozy, with soft Arabic music playing in the background. The service from everyone was exceptional. I 100% recommend it🔥👌🏻
Sent from my iPhone

Early 6pm dinner and only 3 other tables occupied. Inattentive, but friendly staff, left quite an impression. It was the bartender that noticed us waiting and signaled the staff. Mezcal was great and Shepard beer was good too. Warm Nusakhan was tasty. Baked kibbie was simple. Chicken curry decent giant dish. Flavors were 3 out of 5. Will we return? No unfortunately. Maybe we'll try their sister location.

A wonderful mediterranean restaurant offering family style set meals including a variety of mezzes and your protein of choice. Go with a group to sample different entrees. The atmosphere is relaxed, quiet and conducive to conversation.

Most resturant reviews are about the food, service, and atmosphere, and rightfully so. But occassionally there is a restaurant that goes above and beyond. They realize the value of their relationship to the neighborhood and the community. Tanoreen is such a resturant. The food, service, and atmosphere are all exceptional. We do not live in NY but were visiting our kids that do. I was treating dinner for 7 of us. I did not realize that there is an automatic gratuity for that party size. I tipped $70 on top of the included $68 gratuity and did not realize it until the day after. When I called I was told the credit card billing was already submitted. They offered to refund the $70 in cash. However we were leaving and couldn't get back to the restaurant. They held the money in an envelope for my son to pick up a week later. Now that is customer service! Thank you!

I’ve been wanting to try this place for at least 7 years and I kept coming across it online in various features. I ended up in the area by chance, so I figured it was finally time to give it a try. I ordered a bunch of dishes to really give it a try based on waiter recommendations. The menu didn’t have some stuff I wanted to try. Someone else mentioned that they Chan the menu.

Unfortunately the food was generally bland and overly acidic (others have also mentioned this). It was hard to enjoy as a result. Though the kibbie was the best I’ve ever had and the lamb chops were good but ultimately a very small amount of meat (1/3 of them was extra tiny and there was a decent amount of fat for that cut) for more than $40. I would’ve preferred a cheaper cut and more of it.

The waiter raved about the hummus and babba, but  they were honestly mediocre and a bit sour. The Brussels sprouts could have been good if not for the excessive amount of acid. The eggplant and lamb lasagna was pretty bland. The eggplant seemed boiled though it looked a bit browned. The falafel were bland. The rice/noodle mixture was okay but I’ve had better. The potatoes were just okay though unseasoned. The tea seemed to be watered down.

The service was generally good, but there were some mishaps.

I was not told that I had to order dessert with the kitchen closing, so I did not get to try the kanafe that I was looking forward to trying.

I took the leftovers home to my husband and he agreed with my assessments (before I said anything). He had even more trouble with the high level of acid. I’ve been to Ayat/Albadawi (same owners/similar menu) several times and that was drastically better. There are people who like acidic food, so this could work for them. I might get the kibbie again, but that’s about it.

Nice Sichuan cuisine! I like here so much especially this sichuan cold noodles ! Every time I order it. Today tried Kung Pao Chicken， this is also very delicious. Had my lunch alone. So just two orders.

And I posted two years ago pictures ate here. Spicy beef is really great ! If u like spicy and beef , this is must try dish. !
Highly recommend!

Visited the Flushing location and was surprised by how affordable it is. Most dishes are $10+, and even the more expensive ones are just low $20s. We ordered a lot and still felt it was great value.

Food quality was excellent—no misses at all. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. Will definitely come back!

Really good and authentic Sichuan food! I tried most of the classic dishes and I loved all of them. My only complaint is that everything was a bit too salty but I think that’s inevitable since Sichuan food just has so many spices and is packed with flavor. The place looks small initially but is actually really long and there’s a basement too with extra seating. I would definitely come back here when craving Sichuan food.

Sautéed beef w. two kinds of pepper 7/10 - Too spicy for my liking (though it does have a spice level of 2 chilis on the menu)
Double cooked pork belly w. chili leeks 9/10
Sesame cold noodle w. sliced pork belly in garlic sauce 9/10 - This was one of my favorite new dishes!
Sautéed baby shrimp w. egg 8/10
Steamed whole fish w. fresh green pepper (tilapia) 9/10

Pork noodles were delicious! Good service. Food came quickly and we all enjoyed it a lot. Fish was very flavorful. We were able to request for the crispy beef to be more dry instead of oily, so that tasted great as well!

I’ve been here many times and the food is always consistently great. They’ve never gotten our order wrong. Today we had the Poached Fish in Chili Oil and Golden Potato Shreds, and both were absolutely delicious—very flavorful and perfectly spicy.
Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys authentic Sichuan food and can handle some heat. Will definitely keep coming back!

One of the best Chinese meals I've ever had. The food was all well prepared. The service was as good as it gets. The dragon dumplings and the mala cold noodle were out of this world. Everything was so well prepared and came out fast. The cumin lamb was dry but yet still tender. The spicy fried fish was crisp soft on the inside. They have some magic sauce that they use on the Szechuan vegetable dish that makes the cabbage into something like I've never had before yet Flavorful. I hope I get the chance to eat here again

Very good mapo tofu. Could be a bit spicier though. However I brought a white person with me so maybe that’s why it wasn’t so spicy. Munch munch. Waiters kept refilling our hot tea which was very nice on a cold day.

So we came with 7 friends to have a nice dinner. First time trying out this cuisine and it did not leave us disappointed. They focus on spicy dishes such as Mapo tofu but the non spicy ones are very excellent as well, like the black pepper steak. All the protein was nice and tender and quite exquisite.

This place is so god damn good!
Best Szechuan spicy flavor
Intestine very spicy and flavorful
Crispy pork and spicy chicken are all good
The best side dish is their DAN DAN noodles. Perfection

Chuan Tian Xia has a really pleasant atmosphere, which definitely makes for an enjoyable dining experience! The service was also pretty solid – attentive and friendly. The food, though, was a bit of a mixed bag; it was good, but honestly, it didn't quite blow me away. Overall, it's a decent spot, especially if you're looking for a nice ambiance and good service!

Have dined at Enso three times with family, and have loved the experience each time. We only have experience with the countertop menu so I can’t speak to the lounge menu and its service. The fish is the freshest we’ve had in New York, and the overall level of professionalism and dedication to omakase is next to none.
