The service by Chef Nick Wang and his team is impeccable and we always have a great time here. Highly recommend if you’d like to have an omakase experience that’s akin to one you’d find in Japan.

Just want to start off by saying the ambiance was impeccable unfortunately i cant say the same for the omakase. For some reason 3 out of the 4 tastings the fish kept tasting fishier. I’m not sure if that’s their way of trying to stand out but it was extremely unpleasant. We had the omakase tasting in the lounge room and even the waiter said this is the fishiest fish but no worries the ginger on top will mask the taste. I didn’t believe him until my friend had to try it first and let me tell you she had to force herself to swallow it. I also just googled that fresh fish should not taste fishy. Unless the fish was poorly handled. I’ve been to plenty of omakase places and never had I ever tasted the fishiest fish. We waited about 20 minutes in between each course for the next to come. We left starving and went across the street to Lucy’s :/ But overall the ambiance once again was amazing. The interior designer had great taste.

I went the other day after booking the omakase experience. I have to say, stunning. I got there a little early for the 6pm session, and was seated at the bar while the chefs got ready. The whiskey selection is incredible and unique, the wine and sake are plentiful and the cocktails are carefully constructed. I was seat at a bar setup with three others and proceeded to have the time of my life. Both chefs were fun, lovely and knowledgeable. All the dishes were crafted with a kind of skill that you have to see to believe. I thoroughly enjoyed myself and am already recommending this place. I understand why Michelin is eyeing this place

Such an incredible meal and experience that transports you out of Brooklyn. We booked the Chefs Counter and while it's a bit pricey, 100% worth it. Every single bite was packed with flavor. The hospitality was remarkable and made everything that much more enjoyable. Looking forward to my next visit already!

I have to say the dining environment here is truly impressive. The lighting, music, and decor all came together to elevate our dining experience.
We tried the tasting menu, which was priced at $95 per person. The photo shows everything included in that price. While the ambiance was excellent, I feel that the food itself didn’t quite match the value. For the same price, you can find more flavorful and cost-effective options in the city.

Dining at Shota was nothing short of phenomenal. From the moment we sat down, the chef created an experience that felt both personal and educational. He was incredibly warm and delightful, taking the time to explain the proper etiquette of fine Japanese dining and the philosophy behind each course. It felt less like a meal and more like being guided through a masterclass in traditional omakase.

The most memorable moment for me was trying uni. I’ve never been a fan before, but the chef encouraged me to give it another chance—and I’m so glad I did. It was, without question, the best tasting uni I have ever had: incredibly fresh, delicate, and perfectly prepared. It completely changed my perspective.

Shota isn’t just dinner—it’s an experience that deepens your appreciation for Japanese culinary tradition. A truly exceptional omakase that I would highly recommend to anyone who wants to understand sushi at its highest level.

A truly unique and meditative omakase experience

Shota Omakase delivers an experience unlike anything else. The atmosphere is calm, intimate, and almost monastic — a quiet space where attention is fully focused on the food and the moment.

Service is entirely dedicated to creating a flawless experience, with an impressive level of care, precision, and respect for timing and flow.

We chose the omakase with premium sake pairing, and it was exceptional. The selection of sakes was outstanding — complex, elegant, and perfectly matched to each course. The highlights included the premium sakes shown in the pairing, all impeccably chosen.

Every dish was surprising and beautifully executed. Special mention goes to the uni, which was remarkably sweet, clean, and creamy, with absolutely no bitterness or unpleasant aftertaste — a clear sign of top-quality sourcing and handling.

This is not just a meal, but a complete sensory experience. Refined, thoughtful, and deeply memorable. An outstanding destination for those seeking omakase at the highest level in New York City.

There are two menu options:
Premium Omakase - 18 courses featuring small bites, nigiri, a hand roll, and tamago, curated around the best seasonal ingredients. $195 per person.
Gentei Omakase - 19 courses led by chef-owner Cheng Lin, featuring rare seasonal fish and premium cuts for a more elevated journey. $255 per person.

I chose the Premium Omakase, and every course reflected incredible balance, precision, and freshness. My personal standouts were the hatate (Hokkaido scallop), tamago (egg), and the Japanese crown musk melon since each bite was beautifully prepared and bursting with clean, delicate flavor.

What really sets Shota apart from other omakases in New York is the knowledge and hospitality of the team. Our chef, who has over 20 years of experience, shared his passion and insights with us throughout the meal. He explained each piece in detail and even showcased four different types of uni side by side, which was such a treat for anyone who loves uni.

The interior is minimalist, clean, and beautifully maintained, allowing the food to take center stage. Service was warm and professional, and the pacing of each course was perfect.

I've been to many omakase spots in NYC, but Shota stands out for its attention to detail, high-quality fish, and genuine passion for the art of sushi.

Booked 7 seats at the bar for a team omakase. Fresh ingredients, nice variety of dishes, and felt like it was just enough food.

The chefs were lovely and I appreciated how they shared information about the ingredients and dishes served.

The food at Shota Omakase is excellent. The fish is pristine, and it certainly feels like it is all, or nearly all, imported from Japan. Technique is not in doubt. From the first bite, you can tell you are in the hands of someone who knows exactly what he is doing.

At the center of it all is Chef-Owner Cheng Lin, who also seems like a genuinely great guy. Warm, present, and clearly experienced. The kind of chef you would normally enjoy talking to in an omakase setting, where the meal becomes a quiet back and forth. The problem is that the restaurant’s scale makes that rapport almost impossible.

Omakase is not only about what you eat. It is also about intimacy, pacing, and attention. A reputable counter usually seats no more than eight to twelve people. Here, the main omakase bar is enormous, a horseshoe that felt like thirty or forty seats. That changes the entire rhythm. Chef Lin has to rely on a helper to get pieces out to everyone, and that breaks the direct exchange that defines the format.

If that were not enough, there is a second bar in the same restaurant, where a cheaper omakase appears to be served by another chef. At that point, the experience starts to feel less like a focused ceremony and more like a high-functioning operation. Busy, loud, and not particularly omakase in spirit.

Two moments captured that perfectly. On two separate occasions, “Happy Birthday” was sung to two different patrons. One time it was even encouraged by the chef and echoed by the second bar. It may be well intentioned, but it completely kills the omakase vibe. In those moments, the place shifts into the mood of a regular, high-volume sushi restaurant, not a counter built for concentration.

Service is efficient but intrusive. Servers are constantly clearing dishes and topping up water, glasses, or sake. Because you are seated so close to the person next to you, they often come from behind and you have to shift your body out of the way. It happens over and over, and it makes it hard to settle into the meal.

Even the logistics feel mismatched to the crowd. One bathroom for that many guests is hard to justify. There was always a line, and having to wait for the restroom mid-omakase feels absurd.

The price point is the temptation and the explanation. For the quality you get, it is a great deal, cheaper than many top omakase counters in the city. But it is clear how that price is achieved. Volume. Numbers. Many patrons served at the same time. You save money, but you lose the calm and intimacy that make the best omakase memorable.

Which is a shame, because the food is genuinely great, and Chef Lin seems like someone you would want to experience in a smaller room. As it stands, Shota Omakase delivers on ingredients and technique, but the experience does not match what the format promises.

Hands down my favorite omakase/sushi takeout spot. The fish is so fresh and every single piece is so delightfully delectable that it leaves you craving for more. The customer service is impeccable and and the quality is remarkable! Definitely worth every single penny. Isn't my first time eating from here and definitely won't be my last! P.S. If you choose the omakase option, their black cod is to die for! 😋

I go here quite often, and I’d have to say it’s always amazing each time I go. The fish is always seasonal so the menu changes slightly depending on what’s in season. The flavors are always new and I always look forward to what new fish they come up with. Each time I leave, I get a satisfying high from the flavors. It’s extraordinary how good this spot is compared to places in Manhattan! Worth the trip if you’re in Brooklyn. I’d highly recommend coming here for a special occasion. This place is reservation only, don’t miss the reservation time!

Came here for the first time for Valentine’s Day dinner and it did not disappoint! Everything was beautifully put together and so delicious. Every piece was fresh. They even gave us complimentary heart shaped uni! 18 courses for 125 is a steal. Will be coming back

Amazing omakase. Had the full course (steam egg cup/chawanmushi + 14 sushi + dessert). The price is a bit steep but it's all worth it. I guess the service can be improved, seems like waiters are a bit new in serving customers. But the food is really delicious which is more important.

Theres a reason this spot has received 4 Michelin Guide Awards in a row.

The food & drinks were amazing. Thank you Kevin & the Neta crew for the best Omakase experience in Brooklyn, New York!

Restaurant Yuu is where Japanese omakase meets French cuisine in the most thoughtful and refined way. This was truly a one-of-a-kind dining experience — every course felt intentional, balanced, and beautifully executed.

Chef Yuu is an artist. The precision, creativity, and harmony of flavors were on another level. What made the evening even more special was the unique collaboration with a chef from Edinbane Lodge from the Isle of Skye in Scotland — such a rare and inspired partnership that added depth and character to the experience.

We celebrated our 15th wedding anniversary here, and we couldn’t have chosen a better place for such a meaningful night. The atmosphere, the storytelling through food, and the overall care put into the experience made it unforgettable.

A truly exceptional restaurant.

Yuu in Williamsburg delivers an excellent dining experience blending French technique with subtle Japanese influence.

The service was absolutely top-notch: attentive, polished, and perfectly paced. The atmosphere is breezy and calm, with very little noise. Seating is aligned so you’re not distracted by other guests, and facing the open kitchen adds a wonderful sense of theater — it truly feels like part of the experience.

The tasting menu is excellent, with around ten courses that feel thoughtfully curated. The crab and the sweetbread were standouts and among my favorite dishes of the night. The salade de homard was very good, though it mixed quite a few savory elements — it might even benefit from being split into two separate dishes. The grouper was cooked to perfection, as was the pie, with an impressively thin, delicate crust.

We’re not big dessert people, but both desserts were surprisingly great — light, fresh, and well balanced.

I took the wine pairing, which was not my favorite but more from a taste than quality perspective. Pairing is expensive but they serve high-end wines which I was happy to discover.

The meal ends in a separate lounge area, where you relax on a couch with a tisane and mignardises, which I found especially pleasant and thoughtful.

Overall, a fantastic experience from start to finish. I will definitely be going back.

An unforgettable dining experience in Brooklyn. My husband and I agreed this was one of our favorite meals and we eat out a lot! The tasting menu flows effortlessly from one course to the next, each dish thoughtfully presented and full of subtle surprises. The service is attentive in a way that feels natural, and the atmosphere manages to be elegant while still completely comfortable.

People will rave about the food, and rightfully so, but what truly sets Restaurant Yuu apart is the personal touch. After dinner, we were invited to relax in the lounge for tea and additional desserts, which made the night feel even more special. We were not rushed out like many other restaurants. The chef even stepped outside into the freezing cold just to thank us for coming. That level of care is something you don’t forget.

A perfect balance of Japanese and French sensibility.
Each dish was elegant, thoughtful, and beautifully composed. The wine pairing elevated the experience without overpowering it. I recommend sitting at the counter to fully appreciate the choreography of the kitchen. Definitely going back soon!

An incredible dining experience in Brooklyn. The tasting menu feels like a theatrical performance — beautifully choreographed from start to finish. The French-Japanese fusion dishes are refined, balanced, and full of surprises. Service is attentive, the atmosphere is elegant yet relaxed, and the location is very convenient by subway (but parking is nearly impossible). The duck pie is a stunning presentation, though the other dishes impressed me more in flavor. Perfect for a special occasion — they even offer a small cake if noted for a celebration. Would definitely return to try a new menu.

Tobala is so worth the visit! We decided to give Tobala a try and we were not disappointed. The initial entry was warm and inviting, and we were immediately seated. The ambiance was romantic and cozy and the layout was efficient and flowy.
The playlist was great, the service was excellent and the food was impeccably delicious! We almost did not want to disturb it. Everything was spot-on!
The appetizers were small , but fresh, tasty and delish! The entrees were a bit larger in portion, delicious and filling! The prices were steep, but this place serves authentic high quality foods.  We were glad that we chose Tobala for our date night! We enjoyed the desserts— the bunuela and the tres leches, I preferred the center of my tres leches not be so distinctively orange-flavored.
We plan to return to Tobala, it was worth the trip!

Dairon is the most incredible bartender you could ever experience at this establishment. He makes you feel at home & gives every single guests the best experience possible. He is so knowledgeable and passionate about his craft, he makes guests excited to try every single cocktail on the menu.

Although the restaurant is pricey, the experience is worth every dollar. My partner & I visit this place at least once every other week for the past six months, it has never disappointed us.

As someone in hospitality, management here is certainly doing something right

This is a very laid back place, with a charged atmosphere. Impossible? Not at all. It's an experience. The food was delicious.  I had the baked fish and my wife had the grilled steak, we were both pleased.  The wait team was at our back and call.  Nice please for a romantic outing.

We stopped by Tobala in Riverdale this time just for drinks and dessert. I had their hibiscus margarita, which was really good — refreshing and perfectly balanced. We also tried their flan de maíz, our first time having flan with that flavor, and it was delicious! It came with a side of sapote, which had a great flavor and texture. Overall, a really nice experience — great place to relax and enjoy something different.

This restaurant was on my list for a while and was happy to finally stumble upon it. Our waiter Johnathan was great, witty, and knowledgeable. We had the draft beer, esquites, tacos de Barbacoa, duck mole, and the pastry/hot chocolate dessert. Food was balanced and delicious. If I had to be critical for this restaurant to reach its peak success- I would say the mole did not come out as hot as it could have (was just slightly warm) and the tacos de barbacoa could have used more balancing and freshness to it. Would definitely recommend and come back

Made a reservation wanting to try the restaurant week menu only got told after arrival that they don’t serve it on Saturday, which was a bummer. BUT - all the food we ordered were really nice. My favourite was the shrimp skewer and the tomato sauce fish. Overall a bit overpriced and there’s no train nearby but will def come back for the food! Fab service as well.

I appreciate all the help from the Director of Events- Sydney & Manager Chris and staff, I had an amazing time! The food was excellent and the service and hospitality was more than accommodating! I will be returning soon for a dinner as the falafel, especially was fresh and delicious. I had a prix fix , family style dinner for 11 ppl and it was was such a success. by the end of the dinner, we had a birthday cake that most of us were too full to indulge in, The staff cut the cake evenly and packed individual to go boxes for each person. Everyone got to enjoy the left overs and cake the next day and it was even better !

Overall just a great experience!!

beautiful ambiance. great food. went on a calm wednesday evening and it did not disappoint. i’ve said this before and will say it forever.. customer service will always take the cake. our server michelle was excellent, attentive and pleasant.

didn’t get to take many photos but will be back.

This Mediterranean spot is fire! The vibes were amazing last night and the décor is stunning. The food? Every dish was delicious. You must get their freshly made, hot frena bread and the melt-in-your-mouth lamb shank so worth every penny. Service was a 10/10.

The hummus and lamb’s neck are truly incredible. We eat out a lot and this is one of our favorite restaurants in our neighborhood. Each time we visit we cannot wait to come back. Food and service are outstanding.

I don't think their food is bad, despite the many poor reviews. Considering the limited space and lack of a full kitchen, I was impressed by the Isaan sausage, which is excellent and tastes authentic. Crab meat noodles is a rare find on the menu. While service could be improved, I will definitely come back for that sour sausage when I'm in the area.

Was recommended this place and decided to try. The food was quick and good with plenty of seating at the bar across the way. It's a little hard to find since it's not in the middle of Market 57. It's off to the right side facing the water. We ordered the papaya salad (Som Tum Pla Ra) with the fermented fish sauce. It offered a vinegary almost pickled flavor which nicely offset the rest of the meal. We tried the curry crab which was delicious, one of my favorites. It was a rice noodle with curry topped with a soft shell crab and half a hard boiled egg, bean sprouts and raw string beans. The larb beef was also good, which was more tangy and best eaten in the lettuce wrap. The chicken curry puff was perfectly golden on the outside, but soft and pillowy on the inside with coconut, a bit on the sweeter side but very good another favorite. It was enough food for 2 people for dinner and came out to $64. Apparently they are known for their spice and we did not go spicy enough as you can choose your spice level when you order. But if you like spice, definitely try this out.

Really disappointed, all the food here were frozen and reheated (maybe given the limitation of the space).

Crab curry had very little crab and the noodles were falling apart and soggy. The chicken curry puffs were mediocre as well.

Their original restaurant carries a good reputation and this pop up unfortunately was a huge disappointment.
I only tried their French fries, good size portion for $6, they were really good and came with a yummy sauce, if you’re need a quick bite, I recommend
Good taste! Busy weekend but the two staff are friendly and nice 🥰🥰

All the soba tofu dishes were pretty good- I think those were the highlights of the meal. There was a soba tofu appetizer as well as a soba tofu (branded as mochi) dessert.

Can skip soba sushi (we got yellowtail), got the duck (3 ways) shio and the black truffle curry - I think the duck shio is more classic and black truffle curry was more adventurous?

I liked the classic broth better but…. Black truffle curry was def more unique.

Their cucumber wasabi was great!

Pricy meal though.

I was invited there and liked the decors right away. Japanese style drapes at the entrance, very nice arrangements and rooms. This is a soba focused place and I had the duck and Uni (with a touch of truffle) cold soba dish and it was exceptional! Balanced, flavorful, exceptionally clean taste. BTW, buckwheat (soba noodles base) are gluten free. The waitress then told us that the pottery (bowls and tea cup) were all made locally by the chef, making each dish served in a unique manner. I HAD TO see it and ... went on the back. The chef was very kind and explained a bit - of course I expressed that I was delighted. Frankly never went to a place where the food was so good, the decor so unique and the dishes hand made by the chef as well. My overall assessment is that this is a must-go place really (I had such a good vibe).

an awesome dining experience!! every detail here rlly makes my time so worthwhile.

very spacious dining area with the friendliest staff. decoration was so amazing every corner looks extraordinary for photos.

we got the duck shio soba, salmon ikuri soba, unagi & duck stamina soba, which were all very good. it came in huge portion and very pretty bowls (which i think the handmade them in the backroom??)

oh and the monk mocktail was so delicious too!! yuzu soda was a little sour though

amazing spot for any family and intimate occasions !!

The place really makes you feel as though you have been transported to Japan with its calm presence. We were able to walk in without having reservations. There is a small lounge and bar area when you walk in plus two separate eating areas and a private room in the back.
We ordered two dishes to share: one hot/ one cold. They
were both delicious and different enough from one another. The authentic soba noodles are made in house. The cold Salmon Ikura Soba with the sweet dashi was my preference. The Duck Shio Soba was served hot and came with 3 different preparations of duck. The two entree bowls were more than enough food, we could have easily shared one. Presentation is well thought out with the fresh ingredients being strategically placed for viewing.
The food is presented in these gorgeous works of art one of a kind dishes that the owner/chef makes there. They are available for sale along with other pieces of his in the back of the restaurant.

Our waitress was so informative and attentive. She really guided us on what to have.
I can't wait to go back and try something else.

I had some friends who raved about this place. After stopping here, I was won over. The hot duck soba was so delicious! The space is gorgeous and so unique that also showcases the culture of Greenpoint.

Entrees were the absolute highlight of the meal. The sauce of the lamb shank left a lasting impression and made it so you just want more! The pork belly was on the sweeter side so came in second place. I would order both of these dishes again.

For appetizers, the steak tartar was delicious. The salmon was very fresh and clean. Squid was refreshing too. We should have gave our appetizers a bit more thought before ordering. The restaurant was chilly and cold appetizers didn’t help.

Great service! All dishes came out in a timely fashion. Staff were attentive and professional.

Can’t wait to go back! Hopefully we can have some new items next time.

This spot is available with InKind. Can get gift cards on Costco.

This modern Thai/Thai fusion spot in Williamsburg is a good spot for a date night. The interior is intimate, and cozy. Service here is good.

I came here for a group dinner with three friends and we ordered their steak tartare, lamb shank, and branzino (they have a fairly small menu). Everything was pretty solid. I enjoyed their steak tartare and thought that it was really unique that they paired the dish with fried tripe. Notes of lemongrass and other spices were really strong, reminding me of Southeast Asia. The lamb shank was flavorful and the meat was so tender. And, the branzino was also delicious. I would note that the portions were a lot smaller than we expected, and everything was a bit on the pricier side. Overall, a nice restaurant for some good food but I would personally prefer more authentic, casual Thai food.

Pre- fixed menu from nyc restaurant week. Food was tasty, we had to order more.
Staff is friendly and attentive.
The environment, nyc curse of lack of space makes for a loud restaurant and tables very close together.  Still enjoy but it was very loud for me.

We enjoyed a special dinner arranged by Kru Restaurant, and the experience was exceptional. The food was delicious, the staff provided warm and attentive service, and the atmosphere was perfectly suited for the occasion. A well-deserved five stars.

The food here is exceptional both in terms of flavor and presentation. What it lacks a little in ambience, it makes up for in the quality of its food. The squid salad was nicely chilled and had a beautiful aroma from the lemongrass and ginger. It had a nice blend of sweet fruit and sour lime flavors. The lamb shank was fall off the bone tender and was topped with a chive and garlic sauce. The garlic and onion spiced gravy had a moderate zing to it.

We came here for dinner, ordered more than enough for 3 people. Appetizers were REALLY good, entrees so-so, we ordered the Beef Fat Chili Oil Noodle, everything tastes good on its own, but the beef and noodle don’t taste like they come together as one dish. Fried rice was pretty good though, definitely recommend to come here for their appetizers!

We had a great first experience trying Taiwanese cuisine here. I was a bit worried about the spice level, but the dishes I ordered—Whole Striped Bass and Lily Fleming Fried Rice—were flavorful without being too spicy. My husband ordered the Three Cup Treasure (clam, squid, shrimp) and really enjoyed it.

For dessert, they only had one option—Fried Tangyuan with ice cream (black sesame tangyuan, condensed milk, and candied peanuts)—and it was absolutely delicious and unique.

The service was very friendly, and we enjoyed chatting with our waitress. The space is cute, well-designed, and welcoming. Overall, a lovely dining experience! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️½

WOW! Literally Wow. I don’t even know where to start… pretty small area in a pretty boring area of Greenpoint, but A Taiwanese gem! WenWen was recommended by a friend, so I knew I had to try. Upon entering you are greeted by staff and checked-in. We had reservations, so we were seated as soon as our table was ready. We ordered a bunch of things off the menu. We started with the Popcorn chicken and pea shoots. Then the chili oil wonton, and lo ba beng. Then topped it off with the beef fat chili oil noodles. Everything was bomb! I have absolutely no complaints! My favorite dishes had to be… omgosh I can’t decide everything was perfection: I highly recommend you add Wenwen to your list, you won’t be disappointed!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
I visited this restaurant on a rainy day, and it turned out to be one of the best decisions of my trip to New York! Coming from Toronto, where there’s no shortage of Chinese restaurants, I was truly impressed by how authentic this place is. The beef noodle soup was absolute perfection — rich, flavorful, and comforting. Every other dish we ordered was just as incredible.

From the moment we walked in, we were warmly greeted and seated right away. The host and staff were attentive, checking in regularly to make sure everything was great. The entire experience — from the cozy atmosphere to the delicious food — felt genuinely welcoming and full of heart.

Highly recommend this spot to anyone craving authentic Taiwanese food or just looking for a satisfying, well-prepared meal in the area. Definitely a must-try!

We visited on Saturday night,1/24. Special shoutout to the lady that ran after us because one of us left our hat on the table. Thank you so much!!!

Everything was great at Wenwen! Food hits the spot! Definitely an elevated experience to 886 on St Marks. Service was obviously great! Will be back soon!

Great quality food and beautiful views. Went in the winter so imagine views better as it gets warmer. Large area and good temp despite the email notice. Went with friends for Prefix - meat and small bites were all delicious as well as ice cream. Overall was soo good- great service, atmosphere, and food. Seasoning was delicious and recommend

I had a wonderful experience at Laser Wolf. Its been high on list of spots to try and it did not disappoint. While the food was exceptional and everything we ordered was delicious what really stood out to me was the amazing service.

Our waitress, Savannah was fantastic, warm and attentive. She really set the tone for a great night. And I have to give a big shout-out to manager Matthew, who checked in on us and made sure we felt like truly valued guests. Can't wait to come back and try some new dishes!

Went during the summer without a reservation and managed to snag two seats at the bar with only a 10-minute wait. The views of Manhattan, especially at sunset, are absolutely stunning and set the tone immediately.

Food – The French fries were flawless: thick-cut, shatteringly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and seasoned just right. Truly perfect. The mezze plate for two was good but felt like a rip-off. At $40 per person with an “unlimited” setup, you mostly end up filling up on bread. While the presentation was beautiful and a few of the dips were delicious, others were completely skippable. It also felt unreasonable that when a third friend arrived, they wouldn’t allow her to sit with us because of the per-person mezze charge.

the soft serve for dessert was absolutely worth it, creamy and refreshing, and the perfect sweet bite on a warm summer night.

This place is amazing, The menu is inventive and yummy. We had price fixe, lamb and beef.
The salatim is perfect - 11 small appetizers, original and tasty. The coal grilled meat is fantastic.
Cocktails are good, and great beer options.
We always eat a lot at this place, but it’s not heavy or tough.

This was hands down the most impressive dining experiences I have ever had. Our waiter Richie was kind, charismatic and knew the menus backwards and forwards. He was able to tailor the menus based on our preferences. And knew EVERYTHING about every single dish. From the spices to where they were sourced from and all flavor profiles. The food itself was just as impressive! Me and my boyfriend got the steak and the Dorado fish (which our waiter recommended). The fish was the BEST fish we have ever had! The flavor and crispness was amazing! It was incredible! The steak was also amazing! Cooked to perfection and sooo tender! From the food to the atmosphere this meal was an 11/10! Our waiter really MADE the experience as well!
Very authentic inventive Mexican cuisine.  Enjoyed the experience.  Sat at the bar since we didn’t have a reservation but still had a great dinner.  Not cheap, however
Excellent good and fantastic ambiance. The main room is very cozy. I loved their salsas and that they have many interesting dishes on the menu.

Very mixed feelings. Food was not bad, the salsa flight and carnitas were far and beyond the highlights, and I would encourage anyone to order them. The ceviche and tuna tostada were decent, good quality and a fair price, but they wouldn’t blow your mind. The chocolate cremeaux and coconut pudding were good as well.

The issue was with the service, specifically at the end. The bill was paid for not even two minutes and we had just finished signing the receipts before the waiter came around and told us to leave. We were there for less than 1.5 hours, caused no problems (no one made complaints to my knowledge and there we no comments about my party), and we get kicked out? I understand the restaurant is busy, but I would appreciate a few minutes to wrap up the night and leave myself. It’s a shame, the dining experience would have been good otherwise.

Overall, based on the dining experience alone, I would not come back here. There are plenty of other restaurants with similar quality that would not leave a bad taste in my mouth.

I was really excited to try this place, but overall I left feeling underwhelmed. The steak was delicious and cooked very well, and the proteins in general were prepared nicely. That said, the portions and overall experience did not justify the price point.

One thing that stood out was the pricing of the menu. There was a mole dish with broccolini and no protein that was still priced quite high, despite not including any particularly expensive ingredients. Because of that, I ended up ordering the steak to make the meal feel more worthwhile, but even then, the prices felt difficult to justify and seem like they need to be reevaluated.

The drinks were the least enjoyable part of the meal. They tasted watered down. We ordered a Paloma and a michelada, and when the bill came, I noticed the michelada was charged as two separate items , one for the beer and one for the michelada add-ons. Since a michelada is typically priced as a single drink, this was surprising and off-putting.

We were also charged for a second round of salsa. While I understand charging extra in some cases, the refill portion was very small, which added to the overall feeling that the value didn’t match the cost.

The food was very delicious but the service needs work, in my opinion. The biggest 'ick' for me was that the person responsible for garnishing drinks (with limes, etc.) that bartender just finished preparing was grabbing it all with bare hands instead of special tweezers. And that is right after touching menus and clearing dirty plates of tables.

Mili’s pop up here was outstanding. Truly a great experience. The rating should go to Jose and Alexis. The dishes were simple but beautifully balanced and every detail accounted for. We loved them all. I think the cheese dish was one of my favourite things I ate all year. The pork was expertly cooked and so flavourful. Would love to come again to any popup here because the space is also lovely and intimate. Thanks for a great meal!

This place is stellar. We went for Valentine's Day, and the tasting menu was legitimately some of the best food I've had in New York. The food was inventive and delicious. It's small and intimate, which gives it a lovely atmosphere. Perfect for date night or when you want a damn good meal. I will be going back regularly.

runner up is SUCH a wonderful place. snagged a last minute resy after eating winner sandwiches for a year, and WOW. food was outstanding — a nice meal, without being too stuffy / over fancy. love the intimacy of the space & the experience of sitting at the counter while everything is being fired. super accommodating to allergies, too. we ordered the focaccia+whipped ricotta, meats & cheeses, the bitter greens salad, and the short rib. short rib came with a bowl of baby purple lettuce, pickled radishes and cucumbers to wrap the meat into. Loni & Freddie were so welcoming and passionate, we had a lovely time!

Today I visited this cafe with my colleagues (a group of about 20 people). We sat on the second floor, it’s a converted apartment, but the atmosphere is simply unique and authentic, which I’m delighted with. Service at the highest level. The food is incredibly tasty, I liked the salads, especially the yellow beet salads. It should be noted that I ate it for the first time and was pleasantly surprised at how tasty it was. My colleagues were delighted with the pork and even took extra. The chicken is definitely delicious. In general, this is an ideal place for a company to have a great lunch or dinner.

Exceptional dining experience. Wonderful food served in a beautifully lit and intimate environment. The chef prepared a  well sourced  and seasonally appropriate menu, show casing marvelous flavors through simplicity that allowed for a natural pop of colors. Each dish excites the visual mind and palate. A wine list that stands up to the food  is rare to find at this price point and setting, runner up exceeded expectations, thoughtful curations that only amplified the experience. Having incredible options means nothing if you don't have the service aptitude to bring it all together in  a meaningful way, the team here handled each step with care representative of all the fantastic facets of this fantastic evening.

We spent our special night at Sushi Noz when we visited NY. We were informed during the reservation that Chef Nozomu Abe would not presented at that day. It was okay for us as we once had the worst experience at the world-most famous sushi omakase place so nothing can be worse than that.

We arrived just a little bit early so we were first asked to wait in front of the ash room while the chefs prepared for the very last bit. Then, we got invited to the Hinoki room right on the reservation time. The dinning room definitely brought us back to Japan. Feel warm and familiar. There was a little sealed letter set in front of us. I found it such a lovely setup. Then, we ordered different Sake for that night Omakase. The price was quite high for a glass.

They started off with 6 dishes before followed by 11 sushi (including a hand-roll) then finished off with Miso soup, Tamakoyaki and the sweetest melon. All 6 dishes definitely one of the best combination of best ingredients. However, I found this far from Edomae style. It’s more of western style for us. Although, we still like all the dishes. For the sushi, I found it interesting the way they chose to serve us each ingredient like Ika was served fresh, chewy and crispy (usually served super soft). Then, the rest of the sushi lines were served in a softer texture manner in a good interesting way. But to be honest, we found the ingredients a bit simple than any other Omakase we’ve been to. Nothing beyond expectation. The meal finished with the sweetest melon from Hokkaido. I miss this course ending. I think a lot of Omakase places stop serving melon and replace with other type of dessert.

Definitely you will be satisfied with the Omakase course but I found it a bit pricey and not valued for paying $1,500 (including drinks and tip) for 2.

Small Omakase sushi on the UES, that has a great standing counter with a good lunch special!
I totally recommend it.

An omakase experience well worth their Michelin stars. The sushi is top notch, and the service and attention to detail are excellent, as should be expected at this caliber of restaurant. The atmosphere and venue are unique. I believe there are multiple counters, but they are separated from each other so diners have a very intimate experience with their sushi chefs. It was a very quiet and serene experience. If you you're looking for something quiet and calm, this is the place.  I've been to a number of omakase places, and I think this one was memorable for me because the vibe was so different than the others. Don't get me wrong- the food was still incredible, though.

I love Sushi Noz. Aside from Atomix, it is my favorite restaurant in the city.

The service,  atmosphere, and most importantly food are spectacular.

My favorite part of the experience is as it should be -- the sushi.  They use wasabi in a way I've never really experienced before and there are many bites that you just wish that experience again. The flavor of each dish typically has many layers and you can amplify that even further with their drink pairing.

Often high end restaurants provide a pairing that detracts from the meal but that is very much not the case here.

I have been three times at this point and will go again.

Side note: their gift at the end of the meal rules

9.5/10

If I were able to give this sushiya 6 stars, I would. I went there on a Saturday night so it was not the famous Chef Noz. However, that didn't really affect the entire experience. Upon entering the dining area, the ambience was warm and welcoming. It was a very neat 8-seat setting. In front of you, on the table, was a welcome letter with your name on it. The server was very attentive as well as the sommelier. The sommelier clearly explained the menu and I ended up with Kirinzan Junmai Daiginjou. After I finished the first glass, I was thinking about trying a different one. The sommelier was kind enough to let me try before pouring the entire glass and I indeed didn't like it. So I just ordered the same sake. I really appreciate how the sommelier cared for each detail.

After choosing the drinks, now let's focus on the food. The Chef that day was Yudai Shibata. He was very friendly and professional (of course for a two-stat Michelin restaurant) and would answer any questions. The omakase started with the juicy oyster. It was a very refreshing appetizer and I'm glad that it also went well with the sake. The journey continued with Hokkaido uni and flounder sashimi. No special dressing so everything you tasted was from their most original flavor. This was another thing I love about this restaurant: nothing too fancy but the ingredient itself. Then there was the bonito. The skin was crisply fried but the fish was still raw. The different textures exploded in your mouth along with the nori. The next one was a show. You can see the sous chef squeezing the noodles into the boiled water. The noodles were not soba or anything traditional. Rather, they were made from fish so there was an extra layer of umami. The noodles blended well with the soup and fish. The last dish before entering the main sushi session was fried silver flounder. It was fried crisply and with the caviar on it, the taste was complex but simple at the same time. It was complex because you have the hot fried fish and cold caviar and sauce. The crispy outer skin, the soft meat, the tiny bites of caviar, all together formed an enjoyable dish. It was simple because it's just tasty.

Now it came to the protagonist (or I should say protagonists). All kans of sushis were made simple: seafood, wasabi, shoyu, and shyari (vinegar sushi rice). With the combination, you can clearly tell the difference between each fish. The sushi started with some light ones such as kinmedai and shrimps. Then you know the climax is coming when you see the tuna family: from akami to chutoro to the exquisite ootoro. When picking up the sushi, you can still feel the warmth left from the chef's hands, which I think is the main difference between those sushi that were pre-made. Each kan was made in perfect shape. After the ootoro was different styles of sushi, such as uni gunkan and anago temaki. Finally the sushi dishes ended up with tamago and miso soup.

The desserts were also well designed. The first one was corn ice cream, which I have never tasted before. It tastes like iced corn chowder. And the final one was my favorite: the Hokkaido Yubari melon. So sweet yet so easy to consume. Although you would already expect good food from a two star, the actual presentation still exceeded my expectations. Probably that's why this sushiya deserves two stars. Before leaving I also had a pleasant small chat with Chef Shibata. I'm certain that I would visit Sushi Noz again and don't be disappointed if the Chef is not Chef Noz.
Went for a job dinner and it was perfect. The appetizers and entrees were all so good. The queen margarita with tequila was perfect. The strawberry dannolo was a great way to end the night.

We were in town for a wedding. I checked out the Michelin Guide to pick out a place to eat and am so happy we came here! The food was absolutely incredible. They were also very accommodating of my food allergies. Wish we lived close by so we could come here more often!

Walked in Monday night with my friend and were seated right away. The food was great — I ordered the lamb chops and she had the black linguine. Unfortunately, when I got home, I realized my two leftover lamb chops weren’t packed, only the potatoes. There was also an empty bone packed in my friend’s linguine. It was disappointing to discover this after getting home, especially since the meal itself was otherwise excellent and expensive.

Came for birthday night. Food was great, service was good and took us for a walk in. They were sweet and accommodating. Thank you for helping me make a birthday night more special. No picture of food but they were good.

Friendly and attentive service. They don’t have a kids menu but kindly accommodated my daughter with an off menu request. I had the spinach gnocchi with Gorgonzola cream which was divine! My husband had the pork chop parmigiana which he also loved. We both had the margarita from the cocktail menu, 5 stars! Overall, a great spot with an intimate setting perfect for families, date night, or a casual outing with friends. I would definitely go back.

Delicious! A restaurant that’s really worth visiting — the broth is flavorful, the service is great, and the meat is exceptionally good. Everything is fresh, tender, and perfect for a comforting meal.

Had a very nice dinner here in an intimate and beautiful setting! It was my first time trying shabu omakase; they cooked the meat in front of us and placed each piece on our plate like sushi omakase. While the cooking is the fun part of shabu shabu and I would’ve liked to control the degree to which the meat was cooked (it wasn’t equal and I kept receiving the more raw piece), it was also pleasant to watch. The pace was a bit too fast for me, because we were the only party in the restaurant. It would’ve been better had they paced it like a full house instead of cooking the next as soon as the previous piece was gone from the plate. (I just kept half a piece on my plate so we wouldn’t get the next one so quickly.)

We got yuzu sake and umeshu in the beginning as refreshments, then got sake for the course which paired well with the heavy meat. The A5 wagyu truly melted in my mouth, but I personally preferred the wagyu after the first bite bc it was less fatty. The whole course might be a bit too much of meat after meat, especially if you’re a smaller person (I couldn’t eat any more after 5-6 slices). Better pacing might have helped with this, or maybe it’s just a lot.

At any rate I was happy by the end of the night and it was quite memorable. Just make sure you can stomach everything or bring someone who can take their portion as well as yours.

18 courses - interesting experience as it feels like you are eating hot pot but in a more fancy way hahaa - perfect for the rainy/cold days.
The meat truly melts in your mouth. They serve wagyu and pork belly.
The only thing I didn’t like was the chicken rice (it’s quite dry and also not warm). Overall interesting experience. Pricing is quite high for the value imo.

Delicious

The appetizers and dessert were ok, but the star of the meal is the shabu shabu and they’re generous delicious bites that switch up the sauces to keep it fresh each course. We were out by 7, and it was quick and efficient service, which I appreciated too!

Reservations were easy to make - 3 seatings noon, 530, and 7pm(I think). We were running late and showed up ten minutes late to a 530 reservation on a Tuesday but the staff was super chill about it and turns out it was just us and one other guy.

This place is an amazing experience if you really like shabu shabu and also appreciate well crafted experiences that aren't just about overloading you with meat/sauce.

The service is amazing, the people at the counter will cook the meat for you, regularly replace your bowls/dishes if they fill with broth, skim the fat out of your pot.

The meat is really high quality as well, I believe they source their wagyu straight from Japan and the quality is beyond what I can generally find in new york.

There are a lot of sauces and the restaurant puts a lot of care into serving interesting sauces & combinations. It seems they're always trying something new, when I went, they had just freshly prepared some nori sauce. The server will help you understand what sauce combinations work well, for which meats. I found that all their suggestions were amazing and really elevated the taste.

Their ice cream was made in-house, when I went, there was black sesame and earl grey. Both had an amazing crisp texture and soft sweetness.

Overall an amazingly unique meal with amazing service and just a beautiful, cozy spot.

Came here for a date night with my partner and we had such a great experience. Our reservation was at 5:30 PM, and it wasn’t too busy yet (it started getting packed around 6). The host was very kind and explained that they didn’t have any private seating areas, but he still tried his best to find us a good spot since we wanted to take pictures without using flash and disturbing others.

We ordered the chicken tandoori, which was a little salty in my opinion, but eating it with the onions balanced the flavor out really well. We also got the crispy potatoes, which were amazing. For our main dishes, we ordered garlic naan, butter chicken, and a side of white rice. The butter chicken was rich, flavorful, and super buttery. Surprisingly, my partner’s favorite dish was the white rice—he said it had so much flavor on its own.

We also tried two drinks: the mango lassi and a mint drink (I forgot the name), and we absolutely loved them. The mango lassi was especially delicious—honestly one of the best mango lassis we’ve ever had.

For dessert, we ordered the carrot pudding, which came with shredded carrots and vanilla ice cream on top. Everything we tried was so good and definitely did not disappoint.

The atmosphere was cozy and really nice, and the bar was huge with lots of wines and beautiful decorations. Since it’s Valentine’s season, they also has heart balloons floating around, which was super cute. At the end of the night, our server even gave us two balloons to take home.

The service was great overall—our server was friendly and checked in on us often. If you haven’t tried this place yet, you should definitely come check it out!

Kebab & Sharab never disappoints! It is hands down one of the best in the city for Indian food. We tried the lamb chops, chicken Kashmiri kebab, another lamb dish I can’t remember the name, and the waygu kebabs, bone marrow pulao, soya chaap, naan, their famous butter chicken, Kerala prawn curry and roomali roti everything was outstanding.

The lamb chops were tender and perfectly spiced, the Kashmiri kebab was packed with flavor, and the bone marrow pulao was rich and comforting. The butter chicken truly lives up to the hype, and the fresh naan and roomali roti were the perfect finishing touch.

The desserts were honestly the highlight, so unique and beautifully crafted. Their gulab jamun dessert was this perfect modern twist on a classic, warm and indulgent with just the right balance of sweetness. And the guava dessert was unbelievable: refreshing, fragrant, and layered with Indian flavors in a way that felt both nostalgic and completely new.

Amazing food, great vibe, and attentive service. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming to.

Oh my god, where can I start — Kebab Aur Sharab is hands down one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in NYC.

I came here with my friends and from the moment you walk in, the vibe pulls you in with warm lighting, stylish interiors, and an energy that feels upscale yet welcoming. It’s the kind of place where every detail feels intentional(even with the plating of the menu items!).

To start off it is vegetarian friendly and has amazing variety. The soya chaap to the paneer to gol gappe and to their vegetable kebab - everything was packed with amazing flavor.

I really loved the Dal Makhani and Paneer Butter Masala which went really well with the Garlic Butter Naan! We ordered 2 orders of the paneer and one order of the Dal which was more than enough for my friends and I!

I am a big fan of green chutney and I have to say the one here was top notch - it complemented everything!!!

What truly takes Kebab Aur Sharab to the next level, though, is the service. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about the menu. They’re happy to make recommendations and make you feel taken care of without ever hovering.

Overall, Kebab Aur Sharab isn’t just a restaurant — it’s an experience. Incredible food, amazing drinks, great vibes, and top-tier service all in one place. If you’re in NYC and don’t check this spot out, you’re seriously missing out. Will definitely be coming back soon!

If you want to go eat Indian food and feel happy about spending money at an Indian restaurant THIS IS NOT THE PLACE. The food is overpriced for the quantity. The flavors are okay. We ordered the dori kebab and it was $30+ for one small string of kebab. I thought Punjabi's love to feed and give a good portion size.

The chicken curry your mother could cook better. The biriyani was also very ordinary but good sized mutton pieces.
I've had much better food at Baar Baar, GupShup, Utsav. I would not come here the second time.

Kebab and Sherab is clearly a hot spot! We visited on a weekend evening and the place was absolutely packed, but despite the crowd, the service was incredibly fast and efficient. It's easy to see why they're so popular.
The real star of the show, however, was the food. The golgappa was absolutely amazing—easily some of the best I've ever had. We were so impressed by the flavor of the pani (the spiced water) that we actually had to call for extra puri just to finish it off!
Highly recommend this place for great food and quick service, even during peak hours.
